title: Professional Email Composer
primary_use_case: Draft professional emails for any business context
prompt_text:
Write a professional email for the following context:

Purpose: [e.g., requesting a meeting, following up on a proposal, introducing yourself]
Recipient: [e.g., CEO, client, colleague]
Tone: [e.g., formal, friendly-professional, persuasive]
Key Points to Include:
- [Point 1]
- [Point 2]
- [Point 3]
Desired Length: [Short / Medium / Detailed]

Ensure the email has a clear subject line, proper greeting, concise body, and a specific call-to-action.

variations.short: Write a brief professional email to [recipient] about [topic]. Keep it under 100 words with a clear CTA.
variations.detailed: Write a professional email for the following context. Include a compelling subject line, personalized greeting, structured body with context and value proposition, a clear call-to-action, and professional closing. Purpose: [purpose]. Recipient: [recipient]. Tone: [tone]. Key Points: [points]. Add a PS line if appropriate.
variations.strict: Write a professional email. Follow this exact structure: Subject Line (max 8 words), Greeting, Opening (1 sentence context), Body (2-3 sentences max), CTA (1 specific action), Closing. No fluff. Purpose: [purpose]. Recipient: [recipient].

tips: Always specify the recipient's seniority level and your relationship with them. Include the desired outcome explicitly for best results.

title: Blog Post Generator
primary_use_case: Generate SEO-friendly blog posts on any topic
prompt_text:
Write a comprehensive blog post on the following topic:

Topic: [topic]
Target Audience: [who will read this]
Target Keyword: [primary SEO keyword]
Word Count: [e.g., 1500-2000 words]
Tone: [e.g., authoritative, conversational, educational]

Structure the post with:
1. An attention-grabbing headline (and 2 alternatives)
2. A hook introduction (first 2-3 sentences must compel reading)
3. Clear H2 and H3 subheadings
4. Actionable insights in each section
5. Data points or examples where relevant
6. A conclusion with a clear takeaway
7. A meta description (under 160 characters)

Naturally incorporate the target keyword 3-5 times. Write for humans first, SEO second.

variations.short: Write a 600-word blog post on [topic] for [audience]. Include a headline, 3 sections with subheadings, and a conclusion. Target keyword: [keyword].
variations.detailed: Write an in-depth 2500+ word blog post on [topic]. Include: 5+ H2 sections, expert quotes or citations, comparison tables where useful, internal linking suggestions, FAQ section with 5 questions, meta description, and social media snippet. Target audience: [audience]. Keyword: [keyword]. Tone: [tone].
variations.strict: Write a blog post on [topic]. Exactly 1200 words. Flesch-Kincaid grade level 8. 5 H2 sections of equal length. Each section: claim, evidence, actionable tip. No filler. Keyword density 1.5% for [keyword].

tips: Provide specific audience demographics and their pain points for more targeted content. Include competitor URLs for the AI to understand the content landscape.

title: Document Summarizer
primary_use_case: Summarize long documents into concise key points
prompt_text:
Summarize the following document/text into a concise, actionable summary:

[Paste document text here]

Provide:
1. One-paragraph executive summary (3-4 sentences)
2. Key findings/points (bullet list, max 7 items)
3. Action items or implications (if any)
4. Notable data points or statistics mentioned
5. Any areas of concern or risk flagged

Keep the summary under [X] words. Preserve the original meaning without editorializing.

variations.short: Summarize this in 5 bullet points, each under 20 words: [text]
variations.detailed: Provide a structured summary with: 1-paragraph executive summary, key themes (grouped), supporting evidence for each theme, stakeholder implications, recommended next steps, and open questions. Text: [text]
variations.strict: Summarize in exactly 3 sentences. Sentence 1: main thesis. Sentence 2: key evidence. Sentence 3: conclusion/implication. No opinions. Text: [text]

tips: For very long documents, break them into sections and summarize each, then ask for a meta-summary. Specify who the summary is for to adjust the depth.

title: Social Media Post Creator
primary_use_case: Create engaging social media content for any platform
prompt_text:
Create a social media post for the following:

Platform: [LinkedIn / Twitter / Instagram / Facebook / TikTok]
Topic/Announcement: [what you're posting about]
Goal: [engagement / awareness / traffic / conversions]
Brand Voice: [professional / casual / witty / inspirational]
Target Audience: [who should engage]

Include:
- The post copy (platform-appropriate length)
- A hook in the first line
- A clear call-to-action
- Relevant hashtags (5-10)
- Suggested image/visual description
- Best posting time recommendation

variations.short: Write a [platform] post about [topic]. Max [character limit]. Include a hook, CTA, and 5 hashtags.
variations.detailed: Create a 7-part LinkedIn carousel post on [topic]. For each slide: headline (max 6 words), body (max 30 words), visual suggestion. Include an intro slide and CTA slide. Write the LinkedIn caption with hooks and hashtags.
variations.strict: Write a Twitter/X post. Exactly 280 characters or less. Must include: 1 insight, 1 data point, 1 CTA. No hashtags in the main post. Topic: [topic].

tips: Always specify the platform first — character limits, tone, and format vary dramatically. Include your brand voice guidelines if you have them.

title: Rewrite and Tone Adjuster
primary_use_case: Rewrite text to match a specific tone, style, or reading level
prompt_text:
Rewrite the following text to match these specifications:

Original Text: [paste text]

Target Tone: [e.g., professional, conversational, academic, persuasive, empathetic]
Target Audience: [e.g., executives, teenagers, technical engineers, general public]
Reading Level: [e.g., 8th grade, college-level, expert]
Special Instructions: [e.g., shorter sentences, more active voice, add examples, remove jargon]

Preserve the core meaning and all factual content. Do not add new information. Highlight any changes that alter the nuance of the original.

variations.short: Rewrite this in a [tone] tone for [audience]: [text]
variations.detailed: Rewrite this text three ways: (1) Formal/executive version, (2) Casual/conversational version, (3) Simplified/plain-language version. For each, note what was changed and why. Original: [text]
variations.strict: Rewrite this text. Same meaning, half the word count. Flesch-Kincaid grade 6. Active voice only. No sentences over 15 words. Original: [text]

tips: Provide an example of the desired tone from your own writing for best style-matching results.

title: Press Release Writer
primary_use_case: Draft a professional press release for company announcements
prompt_text:
Write a press release for the following announcement:

Company Name: [name]
Announcement: [what is being announced]
Key Details: [dates, numbers, names, locations]
Quote From: [name, title — or generate an appropriate quote]
Target Media: [tech press, business press, local media, trade publications]
Boilerplate: [company description, or ask AI to draft one]

Follow standard press release format:
1. Headline (compelling, newsworthy)
2. Subheadline
3. Dateline and opening paragraph (who, what, when, where, why)
4. Supporting details (2-3 paragraphs)
5. Executive quote
6. Additional context or data
7. Call-to-action / availability info
8. Boilerplate
9. Media contact info placeholder

variations.short: Write a 200-word press release announcing [announcement] for [company]. Include headline, one quote, and boilerplate.
variations.detailed: Write a comprehensive press release with: AP-style formatting, 2 executive quotes, industry context paragraph, market data, customer impact section, availability details, multimedia assets description, and SEO-optimized headline. Announcement: [details].
variations.strict: Write a press release. Max 400 words. Inverted pyramid structure. No adjectives like 'excited' or 'thrilled.' Facts only. Announcement: [details].

tips: Include specific metrics and dates. The more concrete data you give, the more newsworthy the output. Always review quotes for authenticity.

title: Technical Documentation Writer
primary_use_case: Create clear technical documentation for products or APIs
prompt_text:
Write technical documentation for the following:

Product/Feature/API: [name and brief description]
Target Reader: [developer, end-user, admin, etc.]
Technical Level: [beginner / intermediate / advanced]
Documentation Type: [quickstart guide, API reference, tutorial, troubleshooting guide]

Include:
1. Overview / Introduction (what it does and why)
2. Prerequisites
3. Step-by-step instructions with code examples where relevant
4. Configuration options (in a table format)
5. Common errors and troubleshooting
6. FAQs
7. Links/references placeholders

Use clear, concise language. Prefer active voice. Use code blocks for all technical content. Include copy-pasteable examples.

variations.short: Write a quickstart guide for [product/API] in under 500 words. Include: overview, 3 steps to get started, one code example.
variations.detailed: Write comprehensive API documentation for [API name]. Include: authentication section, all endpoints with method/URL/params/response schemas in tables, rate limits, error codes table, SDK examples in Python and JavaScript, changelog section, and migration guide from v[X] to v[Y].
variations.strict: Write a README.md for [project]. Sections: Title, Badges placeholders, Description (2 sentences), Install (code block), Usage (code block), API (table), Contributing, License. No prose paragraphs.

tips: Provide actual code snippets, endpoint details, or config schemas for the AI to document accurately. Generic requests produce generic docs.

title: Newsletter Content Generator
primary_use_case: Create engaging email newsletter content
prompt_text:
Write an email newsletter with the following details:

Newsletter Name: [name]
Audience: [who subscribes]
Edition Theme: [this issue's focus]
Content to Include:
- [Topic/article 1]
- [Topic/article 2]
- [Topic/article 3]
Tone: [informative, playful, authoritative]
Desired Length: [short digest / medium / long-form]

Structure:
1. Subject line (and 2 A/B alternatives)
2. Preview text (under 90 characters)
3. Opening hook / personal note
4. Main content sections with brief summaries and CTAs
5. Quick links / resources section
6. Closing + CTA
7. Footer note suggestion

variations.short: Write a 3-item newsletter digest about [theme] for [audience]. Subject line + preview text + 3 short blurbs with links placeholders.
variations.detailed: Write a full newsletter edition. Include: personalized greeting using merge tags, 5 content sections each with headline/summary/CTA, curated links section (8 items), poll or engagement question, sponsor section placeholder, and referral CTA.
variations.strict: Write a newsletter. Subject line max 45 characters. Preview text max 85 characters. 3 sections, each exactly 50 words. One CTA per section. Total under 300 words.

tips: Include past subject line performance data if available. Specify if the newsletter is B2B or B2C — the tone difference is significant.

title: Copywriting — Landing Page
primary_use_case: Write high-converting landing page copy
prompt_text:
Write landing page copy for the following product/service:

Product/Service: [name]
Value Proposition: [one-sentence description of value]
Target Customer: [who is this for, including pain points]
Key Features: [list 3-5 features]
Social Proof: [any testimonials, stats, logos to reference]
Desired Action: [sign up, buy, book demo, download]
Tone: [bold, professional, friendly, urgent]

Write the following sections:
1. Hero Section: Headline (max 10 words), subheadline (max 25 words), CTA button text
2. Problem Section: Agitate the pain (3-4 sentences)
3. Solution Section: How this product solves it
4. Features Section: 3-5 features with benefit-driven headlines and 1-sentence descriptions
5. Social Proof Section: Testimonial framework or stats callout
6. FAQ Section: 5 objection-handling FAQs
7. Final CTA Section: Urgency-driven closing with CTA

Use proven copywriting frameworks (PAS, AIDA, or BAB). Focus on benefits, not features.

variations.short: Write hero section copy for [product]: headline, subheadline, CTA button text, and 3 feature one-liners.
variations.detailed: Write full landing page copy for [product] using the StoryBrand framework. Include: hero, problem, guide positioning, plan (3 steps), CTA, success outcome, failure outcome, transformation statement. Add A/B variants for the headline and CTA.
variations.strict: Write landing page copy. Headline: max 8 words. Subheadline: max 20 words. 3 features: each a 5-word headline + 15-word description. CTA: 3 words. No superlatives. No 'we' statements — only 'you' framing.

tips: Include competitor positioning and your unique differentiator. Provide real customer language or reviews for the AI to mirror authentic voice.

title: Content Repurposer
primary_use_case: Transform one piece of content into multiple formats
prompt_text:
Repurpose the following content into multiple formats:

Original Content: [paste content or describe it]
Original Format: [blog post, webinar transcript, podcast notes, report, etc.]

Create the following derived content:
1. Twitter/X thread (8-12 tweets)
2. LinkedIn post (engaging, professional)
3. Email newsletter snippet (150 words)
4. Instagram carousel outline (8-10 slides with headline + body per slide)
5. Short-form video script (60 seconds)
6. Key quote graphics (5 pull quotes)
7. Blog summary (200 words) if original is not a blog

Maintain the core message across all formats. Adapt tone and structure to each platform's best practices.

variations.short: Turn this blog post into a Twitter thread (8 tweets) and a LinkedIn post: [content]
variations.detailed: Repurpose this [format] into 10 different content pieces across platforms. For each: specify platform, format, word/time count, hook, CTA, and hashtags. Include a content calendar suggesting when to publish each piece over 2 weeks.
variations.strict: Convert this content into exactly 5 formats. Each must be under 200 words. No overlapping sentences between formats. Original: [content]

tips: The more complete the original content, the better the repurposing. Always review platform-specific character limits and norms.

title: Proposal and Pitch Deck Narrative
primary_use_case: Write compelling business proposals or pitch deck narratives
prompt_text:
Write a business proposal/pitch narrative for the following:

Company/Product: [name]
Proposal Type: [investment pitch, client proposal, partnership, grant]
Audience: [investors, potential client, partner org]
Problem Being Solved: [describe the problem]
Solution: [your solution]
Key Metrics/Traction: [any data points]
Ask: [what you want — funding amount, contract, partnership terms]

Structure:
1. Executive Summary (compelling opening paragraph)
2. Problem Statement (data-backed, emotional resonance)
3. Solution Overview
4. Market Opportunity (TAM/SAM/SOM if relevant)
5. Business Model
6. Traction / Proof Points
7. Team (placeholder for bios)
8. The Ask (clear and specific)
9. Timeline / Next Steps

Tone: Confident but not arrogant. Data-driven but narrative-focused.

variations.short: Write a 1-page executive summary for a [type] proposal. Company: [name]. Problem: [problem]. Solution: [solution]. Ask: [ask].
variations.detailed: Write a full 10-page proposal narrative with appendices. Include financial projections framework, competitive landscape analysis, risk mitigation section, implementation timeline with milestones, and ROI calculations for the client/investor.
variations.strict: Write a pitch script for a 3-minute presentation. Max 450 words. Must include: problem (30 sec), solution (45 sec), market (30 sec), traction (30 sec), ask (15 sec), close (30 sec).

tips: Include specific numbers and traction metrics. Generic claims weaken proposals. Tailor the language to the specific audience's priorities.

title: Creative Story Generator
primary_use_case: Generate creative fiction, stories, or narrative content
prompt_text:
Write a creative story with the following parameters:

Genre: [e.g., sci-fi, thriller, literary fiction, fantasy, realistic]
Setting: [time period and location]
Main Character: [brief description, motivation, flaw]
Conflict: [central tension or problem]
Theme: [underlying message or exploration]
Tone: [dark, humorous, hopeful, suspenseful]
Length: [flash fiction ~500 words / short story ~2000 words / opening chapter ~3000 words]

Requirements:
- Open with a hook in the first two sentences
- Show, don't tell — use sensory details and dialogue
- Include at least one plot twist or unexpected element
- End with a resonant closing line
- Develop the character's voice distinctly

variations.short: Write a 500-word flash fiction story. Genre: [genre]. Must start in the middle of action and end with a twist.
variations.detailed: Write a 3000-word short story with full character arc. Include: inciting incident, rising action with 2 complications, climax, and denouement. Use at least 3 different scene locations and 2 POV shifts. Genre: [genre]. Theme: [theme].
variations.strict: Write a story in exactly 100 words (drabble). Genre: [genre]. Must have a beginning, middle, and end. Every word must count.

tips: Provide character details and the specific emotion you want the reader to feel at the end. This dramatically improves output quality.

title: Resume and Cover Letter Writer
primary_use_case: Create or optimize resumes and cover letters
prompt_text:
Help me create/optimize my resume and cover letter:

Target Role: [job title]
Company: [company name, if known]
Job Description: [paste key requirements]

My Background:
- Current/Most Recent Role: [title at company, duration]
- Key Achievements: [list 3-5 with metrics]
- Skills: [relevant skills]
- Education: [degrees, certifications]
- Years of Experience: [X years]

Please provide:
1. A professional summary (3-4 sentences)
2. Experience bullets rewritten with the STAR format (Situation, Task, Action, Result) and quantified metrics
3. Skills section organized by category
4. A tailored cover letter (3 paragraphs: hook + relevance, value I bring, enthusiastic close)

Optimize for ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems) by naturally incorporating keywords from the job description.

variations.short: Rewrite these resume bullets to be more impactful with metrics and action verbs: [bullets]
variations.detailed: Create a complete application package: ATS-optimized resume, tailored cover letter, LinkedIn headline + summary, and 3 networking message templates for reaching out to people at [company]. Target role: [role]. Background: [background].
variations.strict: Rewrite my resume summary in exactly 3 sentences. Sentence 1: years of experience + domain. Sentence 2: top 2 achievements with numbers. Sentence 3: what I'm seeking. Current: [details].

tips: Always paste the actual job description — it's the #1 factor in generating a tailored, ATS-friendly resume. Include specific metrics for every achievement.

title: Ad Copy Generator
primary_use_case: Write high-converting ad copy for paid campaigns
prompt_text:
Write ad copy for the following campaign:

Platform: [Google Search / Google Display / Facebook / Instagram / LinkedIn / TikTok]
Product/Service: [what you're advertising]
Target Audience: [demographics, interests, pain points]
Campaign Goal: [clicks, conversions, awareness, app installs]
Key Offer: [discount, free trial, limited time, etc.]
Brand Voice: [professional, edgy, friendly, luxurious]

Generate:
1. 5 headline variations (within platform character limits)
2. 3 description/body copy variations
3. 3 CTA options
4. Ad extensions suggestions (if applicable — sitelinks, callouts)
5. Negative emotion/urgency hooks vs. positive/aspirational hooks (both approaches)

All copy must be within platform-specific character limits. No clickbait.

variations.short: Write 5 Google Search ad headlines (max 30 chars each) and 3 descriptions (max 90 chars each) for [product]. Keyword: [keyword].
variations.detailed: Create a full ad creative brief: 10 headline variants, 5 descriptions, 3 primary text options, A/B test hypotheses, audience targeting suggestions, and a recommended budget allocation rationale. Platform: [platform]. Product: [product].
variations.strict: Write Facebook ad copy. Primary text: exactly 125 characters. Headline: exactly 40 characters. Description: exactly 30 characters. Must include one number and one action verb. Product: [product].

tips: Include your conversion data from previous campaigns if available. Specify competitor ads you admire for style reference.

title: Meeting Notes to Action Items
primary_use_case: Convert raw meeting notes or transcripts into structured summaries
prompt_text:
Convert the following meeting notes/transcript into a structured summary:

[Paste meeting notes or transcript here]

Provide:
1. Meeting Overview (1-2 sentences: who met, purpose, date)
2. Key Discussion Points (grouped by topic)
3. Decisions Made (numbered list with rationale)
4. Action Items (table format):
   | Action Item | Owner | Deadline | Priority |
   |------------|-------|----------|----------|
5. Open Questions / Parking Lot Items
6. Next Meeting: suggested agenda items

Be specific about who said what when assigning ownership. Flag any conflicting statements or unresolved disagreements.

variations.short: Extract action items from these meeting notes in a table (Action, Owner, Deadline): [notes]
variations.detailed: Create a comprehensive meeting report: executive summary, detailed discussion by agenda item, sentiment analysis of key stakeholders, decision log with pros/cons discussed, RACI for action items, risk register updates, and draft follow-up email to attendees.
variations.strict: From these notes, extract exactly: 3 decisions (one sentence each), 5 action items (who + what + when), and 2 unresolved items. Nothing else. Notes: [notes]

tips: Provide context about attendees' roles and the project background for better ownership assignment. Raw transcripts work better than paraphrased notes.

title: Product Description Writer
primary_use_case: Write compelling e-commerce product descriptions
prompt_text:
Write a product description for the following item:

Product Name: [name]
Product Type: [category]
Key Features: [list features]
Target Customer: [who buys this]
Price Point: [budget / mid-range / premium]
Platform: [Amazon, Shopify, own website]
Tone: [luxurious, practical, fun, technical]

Provide:
1. A benefit-driven headline
2. A short description (50-75 words) that sells the transformation/outcome
3. A bullet-point feature list (5-7 items, each starting with a benefit)
4. SEO keywords to include naturally
5. A brief 'Who It's For' statement

variations.short: Write a 50-word product description for [product] that highlights the top 3 benefits. Include a headline.
variations.detailed: Write a complete Amazon product listing: Title (max 200 chars with keywords), 5 bullet points (feature + benefit format), A+ Content description (500 words with lifestyle narrative), backend search terms (250 chars), and comparison chart vs 3 competitors.
variations.strict: Write product copy. Headline: max 8 words. Description: exactly 60 words. 5 bullets: each max 15 words, start with an action verb. No superlatives.

tips: Include the product's unique selling point vs competitors. Customer review language is gold — include common praise phrases customers use.

title: Proofreading and Grammar Checker
primary_use_case: Proofread and correct grammar, style, and clarity issues
prompt_text:
Proofread and improve the following text:

[Paste text here]

Please:
1. Fix all grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors
2. Improve sentence structure and flow
3. Remove redundancies and wordiness
4. Ensure consistency in tense, voice, and style
5. Flag any unclear or ambiguous statements

Provide:
- The corrected version
- A changelog of edits made (grouped by type: grammar, clarity, style, word choice)
- A readability score estimate (before and after)
- Suggestions for further improvement (optional)

variations.short: Fix grammar and spelling in this text. Return only the corrected version: [text]
variations.detailed: Proofread this text with detailed annotations. For each change: mark the original, provide the correction, explain the rule, and rate severity (minor/moderate/critical). Also provide a style guide consistency check and suggest 5 vocabulary upgrades.
variations.strict: Proofread for errors only. Do not change style, voice, or word choice. Only fix: grammar, spelling, punctuation, subject-verb agreement, and tense consistency. Mark each fix with [FIXED: reason]. Text: [text]

tips: Specify the style guide you follow (AP, Chicago, APA, etc.) for consistent corrections. Mention if English is not your first language for appropriate sensitivity.

title: Script Writer — Video and Podcast
primary_use_case: Write scripts for videos, podcasts, or presentations
prompt_text:
Write a script for the following content:

Format: [YouTube video / podcast episode / explainer video / webinar / presentation]
Topic: [what the content is about]
Target Audience: [who will watch/listen]
Duration: [target length in minutes]
Tone: [educational, entertaining, professional, casual]
Speaker(s): [single host, interview, panel]

Include:
1. Cold open / Hook (first 15 seconds — must grab attention)
2. Intro / Context setting
3. Main content (organized in clear segments/chapters)
4. Transitions between sections
5. Engagement prompts (questions to audience, like/subscribe reminders if YouTube)
6. Conclusion with key takeaway
7. CTA / Outro
8. Timestamps / Chapter markers

Write in natural spoken language, not written-essay style. Include [VISUAL] cues or [B-ROLL] suggestions where relevant.

variations.short: Write a 60-second video script about [topic]. Hook (5 sec), main point (40 sec), CTA (15 sec). Natural spoken tone.
variations.detailed: Write a 20-minute YouTube video script on [topic]. Include: A/B hook options, animated visual descriptions for each section, lower-third text suggestions, 3 audience engagement questions, end screen strategy, and a companion blog post outline.
variations.strict: Write a script for a 90-second explainer video. Format: [TIMESTAMP] [VISUAL] [VOICEOVER]. Max 200 words narration. Must explain [concept] to a non-technical audience.

tips: Specify your speaking pace (average is 150 words/minute). Include your channel's typical style reference for consistent voice.

title: Case Study Writer
primary_use_case: Write compelling customer case studies and success stories
prompt_text:
Write a customer case study based on the following details:

Customer Name: [company name]
Industry: [customer's industry]
Company Size: [employee count or revenue range]
Challenge: [what problem they faced]
Solution: [how your product/service solved it]
Results: [specific metrics and outcomes]
Timeline: [how long the implementation took]
Quote: [customer quote, or generate an appropriate one]

Structure:
1. Title (results-focused, e.g., 'How [Customer] achieved [Result] with [Product]')
2. Executive Summary (3 sentences)
3. Customer Profile (brief background)
4. The Challenge (paint the pain vividly)
5. The Solution (how they discovered and implemented your product)
6. The Results (quantified, with before/after comparison)
7. Customer Quote (prominent placement)
8. Key Takeaways (3 bullet points)
9. CTA: 'Ready to achieve similar results?'

variations.short: Write a 300-word case study snapshot: Customer, Challenge, Solution, Results (with metrics). Company: [details].
variations.detailed: Write a comprehensive 1500-word case study with: industry context section, detailed implementation timeline, technical architecture overview, ROI calculation, multiple stakeholder quotes (IT, business, exec), lessons learned, and future plans.
variations.strict: Write a case study in exactly 5 sections of 100 words each. Must include at least 3 specific metrics. No adjectives. Only facts and quotes.

tips: Real metrics make or break a case study. Even rough numbers (e.g., '~40% reduction') are far better than vague claims. Include the timeline to build credibility.

title: Content Calendar Planner
primary_use_case: Plan a comprehensive content calendar with topics and schedules
prompt_text:
Create a content calendar for the following:

Brand/Company: [name]
Industry: [industry]
Target Audience: [who you're reaching]
Content Channels: [blog, LinkedIn, Twitter, YouTube, newsletter, etc.]
Planning Period: [e.g., 1 month, 1 quarter]
Content Pillars: [3-5 core themes or topics]
Publishing Frequency: [e.g., 3 blogs/week, daily social, weekly newsletter]
Key Dates: [product launches, holidays, events]
Goal: [brand awareness, lead gen, engagement, SEO]

Provide a calendar in table format:
| Week | Date | Channel | Content Type | Topic/Title | Target Keyword | CTA | Status |

Also include:
- Content theme for each week
- Mix of content types (educational, promotional, engagement, curated)
- Repurposing opportunities
- Suggested hashtag groups per content pillar

variations.short: Give me 20 blog post ideas for [industry/niche] organized by content pillar. Include title, target keyword, and content type for each.
variations.detailed: Create a full quarterly content strategy: monthly themes, weekly calendar with 5+ posts per week across 4 channels, SEO keyword mapping, content funnel alignment (TOFU/MOFU/BOFU), A/B test ideas, influencer collaboration opportunities, and KPI targets per content type.
variations.strict: Create a 4-week content calendar. Exactly 3 posts per week. Table format only. Columns: Date, Platform, Type, Title, Keyword. No descriptions.

tips: Include your existing top-performing content topics. Mention seasonal trends relevant to your industry for timely content suggestions.

title: White Paper Writer
primary_use_case: Create comprehensive white papers that establish thought leadership and provide in-depth analysis on complex topics
user_role: Content Strategist, Technical Writer, Marketing Director, Research Analyst
prompt_text: You are an expert white paper writer specializing in creating authoritative, well-researched documents that establish thought leadership and provide comprehensive analysis. Your task is to write a professional white paper on the topic of [TOPIC] for [TARGET_AUDIENCE]. The white paper should be approximately [WORD_COUNT] words and address the following key objectives: [OBJECTIVES]. Begin with an executive summary that clearly articulates the main findings and recommendations. Structure the document with clear sections including: introduction and background context, problem statement and current challenges, detailed analysis of [SPECIFIC_AREAS], proposed solutions or frameworks, case studies or real-world examples, implementation considerations, and a conclusion with actionable next steps. Use a formal yet accessible tone that balances technical depth with readability. Include data points, statistics, and references where relevant. Ensure the content positions [COMPANY/ORGANIZATION] as a trusted authority while providing genuine value to readers. Incorporate visual elements suggestions (charts, graphs, diagrams) where appropriate. The white paper should be persuasive but evidence-based, avoiding overt sales language while subtly guiding readers toward [DESIRED_OUTCOME].

variations.short: Write a white paper on [TOPIC] for [AUDIENCE]. Include executive summary, problem analysis, solutions, and recommendations. Target [WORD_COUNT] words.
variations.detailed: Create a comprehensive white paper on [TOPIC] targeting [TARGET_AUDIENCE]. Structure: executive summary, introduction with industry context, detailed problem analysis covering [KEY_ISSUES], proposed solutions with supporting evidence, relevant case studies from [INDUSTRY], implementation roadmap, risk assessment, and conclusion with actionable recommendations. Include data visualization suggestions and ensure the document establishes [ORGANIZATION] as a thought leader. Maintain formal tone with technical depth. Target length: [WORD_COUNT] words.
variations.strict: Write a white paper following this exact structure: 1) Executive Summary (200 words), 2) Introduction & Background (500 words), 3) Problem Statement (800 words), 4) Analysis Section with [NUMBER] subsections (2000 words), 5) Solutions Framework (1000 words), 6) Case Studies (600 words), 7) Implementation Guide (500 words), 8) Conclusion (300 words). Topic: [TOPIC]. Audience: [AUDIENCE]. Include [NUMBER] citations, [NUMBER] data points, and [NUMBER] visual element suggestions. Tone: authoritative, evidence-based, no sales language. Total: [WORD_COUNT] words.

tips: Start with thorough research on the topic and audience. Use a clear hierarchy with headings and subheadings. Include credible sources and data. Balance technical depth with accessibility. End each section with a transition to the next. Use active voice where possible. Include a table of contents for longer papers. Consider creating an infographic summary for promotion.

title: Speech Writing
primary_use_case: Craft compelling speeches for various occasions including conferences, ceremonies, and corporate events
user_role: Executive Assistant, Communications Director, Public Relations Manager, Event Coordinator
prompt_text: You are a professional speechwriter with expertise in crafting engaging, memorable speeches that connect with audiences and deliver key messages effectively. Write a [SPEECH_TYPE] speech for [SPEAKER_NAME] to be delivered at [EVENT/OCCASION] to an audience of [AUDIENCE_DESCRIPTION]. The speech should be approximately [DURATION] minutes long (roughly [WORD_COUNT] words when spoken at average pace). The primary message or theme should focus on [CORE_MESSAGE]. Begin with a strong opening that captures attention—consider using a story, surprising statistic, or thought-provoking question. Structure the speech with clear sections: introduction that establishes rapport, main body with [NUMBER] key points or stories that support your message, and a powerful conclusion that reinforces the core message and includes a call to action or memorable closing statement. Adapt the tone to match [FORMALITY_LEVEL]—whether it's conversational, inspirational, formal, or humorous. Incorporate personal anecdotes, relevant examples, and rhetorical devices such as repetition, metaphors, or parallel structure where appropriate. Ensure the speech reflects [SPEAKER_NAME]'s voice and speaking style. Include natural pauses, emphasis markers, and delivery notes where helpful. The speech should feel authentic, engaging, and leave the audience with a clear takeaway.

variations.short: Write a [DURATION]-minute [SPEECH_TYPE] speech for [SPEAKER] on [TOPIC]. Include engaging opening, [NUMBER] main points, and memorable conclusion.
variations.detailed: Craft a [SPEECH_TYPE] speech for [SPEAKER_NAME] to deliver at [EVENT] to [AUDIENCE]. Duration: [DURATION] minutes. Core message: [MESSAGE]. Structure: attention-grabbing opening (story/statistic/question), introduction establishing speaker credibility, [NUMBER] main sections each with supporting stories/examples, smooth transitions between sections, powerful conclusion with call-to-action. Tone: [FORMALITY]. Include speaker notes for emphasis, pauses, and delivery tips. Reflect [SPEAKER]'s authentic voice. Use rhetorical devices (repetition, metaphors, parallel structure) strategically.
variations.strict: Write a speech with exact timing: Opening (30 seconds), Introduction (1 minute), Point 1 (3 minutes), Point 2 (3 minutes), Point 3 (3 minutes), Conclusion (1 minute). Total: [DURATION] minutes. Speaker: [NAME]. Event: [EVENT]. Message: [MESSAGE]. Include [NUMBER] stories, [NUMBER] statistics, [NUMBER] rhetorical devices. Mark pauses with [PAUSE] and emphasis with [EMPHASIS]. Opening must be [HOOK_TYPE]. Conclusion must include [CALL_TO_ACTION]. Word count: [WORD_COUNT].

tips: Read the speech aloud to check flow and timing. Use shorter sentences for impact. Include pauses for emphasis. Match the speaker's natural speaking style. Practice transitions between sections. Use concrete examples over abstract concepts. End with a strong, memorable closing. Consider audience energy levels—shorter speeches often work better. Include speaker notes for delivery guidance.

title: SOP / Process Documentation
primary_use_case: Create clear, comprehensive standard operating procedures and process documentation for organizational consistency
user_role: Operations Manager, Quality Assurance Specialist, Training Coordinator, Process Engineer, Compliance Officer
prompt_text: You are an expert technical writer specializing in creating clear, actionable standard operating procedures (SOPs) and process documentation that ensure consistency, compliance, and operational excellence. Write a comprehensive SOP document for the process of [PROCESS_NAME] that will be used by [TARGET_USERS] in the [DEPARTMENT/AREA] department. The document should follow a standard SOP format and include the following sections: document control information (version, date, author, approver), purpose statement clearly explaining why this procedure exists, scope defining what is covered and any exclusions, roles and responsibilities listing who performs each step, required materials and resources, step-by-step procedures numbered sequentially with clear action items, quality checkpoints and verification steps, troubleshooting section addressing common issues, safety considerations and warnings, revision history, and appendices with relevant forms or references. Each step should be written in imperative mood (e.g., 'Click the Submit button' not 'You should click'). Include specific details such as system names, button labels, file locations, and decision points. Use clear formatting with numbered lists, bullet points, and visual hierarchy. The language should be precise, unambiguous, and accessible to users with [EXPECTED_EXPERTISE_LEVEL] level of knowledge. Include screenshots placeholders or diagrams where visual aids would enhance understanding.

variations.short: Create an SOP for [PROCESS_NAME] used by [USERS]. Include purpose, scope, step-by-step procedures, and troubleshooting. Format: clear numbered steps.
variations.detailed: Write a comprehensive SOP document for [PROCESS_NAME] targeting [TARGET_USERS] in [DEPARTMENT]. Structure: document control (version, date, approver), purpose and scope, roles/responsibilities, prerequisites and materials, detailed numbered step-by-step procedures with decision points, quality checkpoints, safety considerations, troubleshooting guide for common issues, related procedures, revision history. Use imperative mood, specific system/file names, clear formatting. Include visual aid placeholders. Language level: [EXPERTISE_LEVEL]. Ensure compliance with [STANDARDS/REGULATIONS].
variations.strict: Create SOP following exact template: 1) Header (Title, SOP Number, Version, Date, Author, Approver), 2) Purpose (50 words), 3) Scope (100 words), 4) Roles (list all), 5) Prerequisites (materials, access, training), 6) Procedure Steps (numbered 1-N, each with: action, expected result, decision point if applicable), 7) Quality Checks ([NUMBER] checkpoints), 8) Troubleshooting (table: Issue | Cause | Solution), 9) Safety Warnings, 10) References. Process: [PROCESS_NAME]. Users: [USERS]. Format: imperative mood, specific details, no ambiguity.

tips: Test the procedure by following it step-by-step. Use consistent terminology throughout. Include 'what if' scenarios in troubleshooting. Number steps sequentially and use sub-numbering for substeps. Add visual aids (screenshots, flowcharts) where helpful. Keep language simple and direct. Include estimated time for each major section. Review with actual users before finalizing. Update regularly as processes evolve.

title: UX Writing / Microcopy
primary_use_case: Create clear, concise, and user-friendly microcopy for digital interfaces that guides users and enhances usability
user_role: UX Writer, Product Designer, UI Designer, Content Strategist, Product Manager
industry: Technology, E-commerce, SaaS, Mobile Apps, Web Development
output_type: Short copy snippets and interface text
prompt_text: You are a UX writing specialist focused on creating clear, concise, and user-centered microcopy that improves digital product usability and user experience. Write microcopy for [INTERFACE_ELEMENT] in a [PRODUCT_TYPE] application. The context is [USER_SCENARIO] where users need to [USER_GOAL]. The copy should be [TONE] in tone, align with [BRAND_VOICE], and be appropriate for [TARGET_AUDIENCE]. Consider the following UX writing principles: use active voice and present tense, write in plain language avoiding jargon, keep it concise (aim for [WORD_LIMIT] words or less), use positive framing when possible, provide clear action-oriented language, include helpful context when needed, and ensure accessibility with clear labels. For this specific element, address [SPECIFIC_REQUIREMENT] while maintaining consistency with the overall product experience. If this is an error message, explain what went wrong in user-friendly terms and provide a clear path forward. If it's a call-to-action button, use action verbs and be specific about what will happen. If it's instructional text, break complex information into digestible chunks. Consider the user's emotional state at this point in their journey and write accordingly. Include alternative versions for A/B testing if relevant.

variations.short: Write UX microcopy for [ELEMENT] in [PRODUCT]. Context: [SCENARIO]. Goal: [GOAL]. Tone: [TONE]. Max [WORDS] words. Clear, actionable, user-friendly.
variations.detailed: Create UX microcopy for [INTERFACE_ELEMENT] in [PRODUCT_TYPE] used in scenario [USER_SCENARIO] where users [USER_GOAL]. Requirements: tone [TONE], brand voice [BRAND_VOICE], audience [AUDIENCE], max [WORD_LIMIT] words. Apply UX principles: active voice, plain language, positive framing, clear actions, accessibility. Address [SPECIFIC_REQUIREMENT]. Consider user's emotional state. Include [NUMBER] alternative versions for testing. Ensure consistency with product patterns. If error: explain issue + solution. If CTA: action verb + clear outcome.
variations.strict: Write microcopy meeting exact specs: Element: [ELEMENT], Context: [SCENARIO], Max words: [NUMBER], Tone: [TONE], Voice: [VOICE]. Must include: [REQUIRED_ELEMENTS]. Must avoid: [FORBIDDEN_WORDS]. Format: [FORMAT_REQUIREMENT]. Provide [NUMBER] variations. Each version must: use active voice, be under [WORD_LIMIT], include [KEY_INFO], pass accessibility check. Test for clarity with [USER_TYPE].

tips: Test copy with real users when possible. Keep it shorter than you think—every word counts. Use 'you' and 'your' to speak directly to users. Avoid technical jargon. Make error messages helpful, not just informative. Use consistent terminology across the product. Consider the user's context and emotional state. Write for scanning—users don't read, they scan. Test different versions to see what works best.

title: Knowledge Base Article Writer
primary_use_case: Create comprehensive, searchable knowledge base articles that help users find answers and solve problems independently
user_role: Technical Writer, Customer Support Manager, Documentation Specialist, Product Manager, Content Manager
industry: Technology, SaaS, E-commerce, Customer Service, Education
prompt_text: You are a knowledge base content specialist skilled at creating clear, comprehensive, and easily discoverable help articles that enable users to solve problems independently. Write a knowledge base article on [TOPIC] for [PRODUCT/SERVICE_NAME] targeting users with [EXPERTISE_LEVEL] level of knowledge. The article should help users [PRIMARY_GOAL] and address the common question or problem: [USER_QUESTION/PROBLEM]. Structure the article with a clear hierarchy: an engaging title optimized for search (include keywords like [KEYWORDS]), a brief introduction (2-3 sentences) explaining what the article covers and who it's for, a table of contents for longer articles, step-by-step instructions or explanations organized with clear headings, visual aids placeholders (screenshots, diagrams, videos) where helpful, a 'Related Articles' section linking to [NUMBER] relevant topics, and a 'Was this helpful?' feedback mechanism. Write in a friendly, helpful tone that assumes the user may be frustrated or confused. Use clear, simple language avoiding unnecessary technical jargon. Break complex processes into numbered steps with clear action items. Include troubleshooting tips, common mistakes to avoid, and 'what's next' suggestions. Ensure the content is scannable with proper headings, bullet points, and formatting. Optimize for search by naturally incorporating relevant keywords and addressing common search queries. Include metadata suggestions: tags, categories, and related topics.

variations.short: Write a knowledge base article on [TOPIC] for [PRODUCT]. Address: [QUESTION]. Include intro, step-by-step guide, troubleshooting, and related articles. User-friendly tone.
variations.detailed: Create a comprehensive knowledge base article for [PRODUCT/SERVICE] on topic [TOPIC] addressing [USER_QUESTION]. Target audience: [EXPERTISE_LEVEL]. Structure: SEO-optimized title with [KEYWORDS], brief intro explaining scope, table of contents, detailed step-by-step instructions with clear headings, visual aid placeholders (screenshots/diagrams), troubleshooting section with common issues, tips and best practices, related articles ([NUMBER] links), feedback section. Tone: friendly, helpful, patient. Language: simple, clear, jargon-free. Format: scannable with headings, bullets, numbered lists. Include metadata: tags [TAGS], category [CATEGORY], related topics [TOPICS].
variations.strict: Write KB article with exact structure: Title (SEO: [KEYWORDS]), Intro (50 words), TOC, Section 1 ([TITLE], [WORD_COUNT] words), Section 2 ([TITLE], [WORD_COUNT] words), Section 3 ([TITLE], [WORD_COUNT] words), Troubleshooting (table format), Related Articles ([NUMBER] links), Tags: [TAGS]. Topic: [TOPIC]. Product: [PRODUCT]. Question: [QUESTION]. Must include: [NUMBER] screenshots, [NUMBER] code examples, [NUMBER] tips. Tone: [TONE]. Max jargon level: [LEVEL].

tips: Write for search—include terms users actually search for. Start with the solution, then explain why. Use clear, descriptive headings. Include screenshots for visual steps. Link to related articles to keep users engaged. Update articles based on user feedback and support tickets. Keep content current—outdated info frustrates users. Use consistent formatting across all articles. Test articles by following them yourself.

title: Job Description Writer
primary_use_case: Create compelling, accurate job descriptions that attract qualified candidates and set clear expectations
user_role: HR Manager, Talent Acquisition Specialist, Recruiter, Hiring Manager, People Operations
prompt_text: You are an expert job description writer specializing in creating compelling, inclusive, and accurate job postings that attract top talent while setting clear expectations. Write a comprehensive job description for the position of [JOB_TITLE] at [COMPANY_NAME] in the [DEPARTMENT] department. This is a [EMPLOYMENT_TYPE] position (full-time/part-time/contract) located in [LOCATION] with [REMOTE_OPTIONS]. The ideal candidate should have [YEARS] years of experience in [FIELD/INDUSTRY] and possess [KEY_QUALIFICATIONS]. Structure the job description with the following sections: an engaging job title and brief overview (2-3 sentences), company introduction highlighting [COMPANY_CULTURE/VALUES], key responsibilities listed in order of importance (use bullet points, start with action verbs, focus on outcomes), required qualifications (education, experience, skills, certifications—distinguish between must-haves and nice-to-haves), preferred qualifications that would make a candidate stand out, compensation and benefits information (salary range: [RANGE], benefits: [BENEFITS]), work environment and culture details, application instructions and process, and equal opportunity statement. Write in an inclusive, welcoming tone that avoids biased language. Use clear, specific language that accurately represents the role. Highlight growth opportunities and what makes this role unique. Ensure the description is optimized for applicant tracking systems (ATS) with relevant keywords. Include information about [SPECIFIC_ASPECTS] that are important for this role.

variations.short: Write a job description for [JOB_TITLE] at [COMPANY]. Include: overview, responsibilities, qualifications, compensation, benefits. [EMPLOYMENT_TYPE], [LOCATION]. Attract [TARGET_CANDIDATES].
variations.detailed: Create a comprehensive job description for [JOB_TITLE] position at [COMPANY_NAME] in [DEPARTMENT]. Employment: [TYPE], Location: [LOCATION], Remote: [OPTIONS]. Structure: engaging title and overview, company intro with culture/values, detailed responsibilities (prioritized, action verbs, outcome-focused), required qualifications (must-haves vs nice-to-haves), preferred qualifications, compensation ([RANGE]), benefits ([LIST]), work environment, growth opportunities, application process, EEO statement. Target: [YEARS] years experience in [FIELD]. Key skills: [SKILLS]. Tone: inclusive, welcoming, unbiased. ATS-optimized. Highlight: [UNIQUE_ASPECTS].
variations.strict: Write JD with exact sections: 1) Title & Overview (100 words), 2) Company Intro (150 words), 3) Responsibilities ([NUMBER] bullets, prioritized), 4) Required Qualifications (Education: [LEVEL], Experience: [YEARS], Skills: [LIST], Certifications: [LIST]), 5) Preferred Qualifications ([NUMBER] items), 6) Compensation ([RANGE]), 7) Benefits ([NUMBER] items), 8) Application ([PROCESS]). Job: [TITLE]. Company: [NAME]. Type: [TYPE]. Location: [LOCATION]. Must include: [REQUIREMENTS]. Avoid: biased language. ATS keywords: [KEYWORDS].

tips: Use inclusive language—avoid gendered terms and unnecessary requirements. Focus on outcomes, not just tasks. Be specific about must-haves vs nice-to-haves. Include salary range when possible—it attracts more candidates. Highlight growth opportunities and company culture. Use action verbs (manage, develop, create). Keep it scannable with clear sections. Test with ATS systems. Review for unconscious bias. Update regularly to reflect role evolution.

title: Release Notes Writer
primary_use_case: Create clear, user-focused release notes that communicate product updates and changes effectively
user_role: Product Manager, Technical Writer, Marketing Manager, Developer Relations, Product Marketing
industry: Technology, SaaS, Software Development, Mobile Apps
prompt_text: You are a release notes specialist skilled at translating technical changes into clear, user-friendly communications that help users understand and adopt new features and improvements. Write release notes for [PRODUCT_NAME] version [VERSION_NUMBER] released on [RELEASE_DATE]. This release includes [NUMBER_OF_MAJOR_FEATURES] major features, [NUMBER_OF_IMPROVEMENTS] improvements, and [NUMBER_OF_BUG_FIXES] bug fixes. Structure the release notes with: a compelling headline and brief summary (2-3 sentences highlighting the most exciting updates), a 'What's New' section featuring major features with clear descriptions of what they do and why users should care (include benefits, not just features), an 'Improvements' section listing enhancements to existing functionality, a 'Bug Fixes' section with user-friendly explanations of issues resolved, breaking changes or migration notes if applicable (clearly marked with warnings), upgrade instructions if needed, and links to documentation or tutorials. Write in a friendly, conversational tone that celebrates the work while being clear about changes. Use the user's perspective—focus on benefits and outcomes, not just technical details. Include visual elements suggestions (screenshots, GIFs, videos) for major features. Organize content by user impact (most impactful first). Use clear formatting with headings, bullet points, and emoji sparingly for visual interest. Address [SPECIFIC_USER_CONCERNS] if relevant to this release.

variations.short: Write release notes for [PRODUCT] v[VERSION] released [DATE]. Include: headline, major features ([NUMBER]), improvements ([NUMBER]), bug fixes ([NUMBER]). User-friendly, benefit-focused.
variations.detailed: Create release notes for [PRODUCT_NAME] version [VERSION] released [DATE]. Content: compelling headline and summary, 'What's New' section with [NUMBER] major features (descriptions, benefits, visual suggestions), 'Improvements' section ([NUMBER] items), 'Bug Fixes' section ([NUMBER] items, user-friendly explanations), breaking changes/migration notes if applicable, upgrade instructions, links to docs/tutorials. Tone: friendly, conversational, user-focused. Emphasize benefits over features. Organize by impact. Format: clear headings, bullets, minimal emoji. Address: [USER_CONCERNS]. Include visual placeholders for major features.
variations.strict: Write release notes with exact structure: Headline ([WORDS] max), Summary (50 words), What's New ([NUMBER] features, each: title, description 100 words, benefit, visual), Improvements ([NUMBER] items), Bug Fixes ([NUMBER] items), Breaking Changes (if any, marked [WARNING]), Upgrade Notes. Product: [NAME]. Version: [VERSION]. Date: [DATE]. Tone: [TONE]. Must include: [REQUIREMENTS]. Format: [FORMAT]. Each feature must explain: what, why, how to use.

tips: Lead with user benefits, not technical changes. Use clear, simple language. Group related changes together. Include screenshots or GIFs for visual features. Highlight breaking changes prominently. Link to detailed documentation. Use consistent formatting across releases. Celebrate improvements, not just new features. Test with non-technical users for clarity. Keep a changelog archive for reference.

title: Internal Memo Writer
primary_use_case: Create clear, professional internal memos that communicate important information, decisions, or updates to employees
user_role: Executive Assistant, HR Manager, Communications Manager, Department Head, Operations Manager
prompt_text: You are an expert business communicator specializing in writing clear, professional internal memos that effectively convey important information to employees. Write an internal memo regarding [SUBJECT] to be distributed to [RECIPIENT_GROUP] from [SENDER_NAME/TITLE] on [DATE]. The memo should address [PRIMARY_PURPOSE] and communicate [KEY_INFORMATION]. Structure the memo using standard business memo format: header section with 'MEMORANDUM' label, 'TO:' line listing recipients, 'FROM:' line with sender name and title, 'DATE:' line, 'SUBJECT:' line with clear, concise subject, opening paragraph that immediately states the purpose and provides context, body paragraphs (2-4 paragraphs) that provide detailed information, supporting details, rationale, or background as needed, action items or next steps if applicable, closing paragraph that summarizes key points or provides contact information for questions, and signature line if needed. Write in a professional yet approachable tone appropriate for [ORGANIZATIONAL_CULTURE]. Be direct and clear—get to the point quickly. Use active voice and concise language. Organize information logically with clear paragraphs. If the memo contains sensitive information or requires action, make that clear upfront. Include relevant dates, deadlines, or contact information. Address potential questions or concerns proactively. Ensure the memo is scannable with clear structure and formatting.

variations.short: Write an internal memo on [SUBJECT] from [SENDER] to [RECIPIENTS] dated [DATE]. Include: purpose, key information, action items if needed. Professional tone.
variations.detailed: Create an internal memo following standard format: Header (MEMORANDUM, TO: [RECIPIENTS], FROM: [SENDER/TITLE], DATE: [DATE], SUBJECT: [SUBJECT]). Content: opening paragraph stating purpose and context, body paragraphs ([NUMBER]) with detailed information on [TOPICS], rationale/background, action items/deadlines if applicable, closing with summary and contact info. Subject: [SUBJECT]. Purpose: [PURPOSE]. Key info: [INFORMATION]. Tone: professional, approachable, appropriate for [CULTURE]. Be direct, clear, scannable. Address: [CONCERNS].
variations.strict: Write memo with exact format: MEMORANDUM header, TO: [RECIPIENTS], FROM: [SENDER, TITLE], DATE: [DATE], SUBJECT: [SUBJECT]. Opening (50 words), Body Para 1 ([TOPIC], [WORD_COUNT]), Body Para 2 ([TOPIC], [WORD_COUNT]), Body Para 3 ([TOPIC], [WORD_COUNT]), Action Items ([NUMBER] items with deadlines), Closing (30 words, contact: [INFO]). Subject: [SUBJECT]. Tone: [TONE]. Must include: [REQUIREMENTS]. No fluff.

tips: Get to the point in the first paragraph. Use clear subject lines. Keep paragraphs short and focused. Use bullet points for lists. Include action items with deadlines when applicable. Be transparent about sensitive topics. Provide contact information for questions. Use consistent memo format across organization. Proofread carefully—internal memos still need to be professional. Consider the audience's perspective and address likely questions.

title: Investor Update Email
primary_use_case: Create professional investor update emails that communicate company progress, metrics, and strategic direction
user_role: CEO, CFO, Investor Relations Manager, Founder, Executive Team
industry: Startups, Venture Capital, Private Equity, Technology, Finance
prompt_text: You are an investor relations specialist skilled at crafting compelling, transparent investor update emails that build trust and keep stakeholders informed. Write an investor update email for [COMPANY_NAME] covering the period [TIME_PERIOD] (e.g., Q1 2024, January 2024) to be sent to [INVESTOR_GROUP] from [SENDER_NAME/TITLE]. The email should communicate [PRIMARY_MESSAGE] and highlight key achievements, challenges, and forward-looking plans. Structure the email with: a compelling subject line that indicates the period and hints at key highlights, a personalized greeting, an executive summary paragraph (2-3 sentences) providing high-level overview of the period, key metrics section highlighting [METRIC_CATEGORIES] with specific numbers and context (revenue, users, growth rates, etc.), major wins and achievements with concrete examples, challenges and how they're being addressed (be transparent but constructive), team updates including key hires or changes, product/strategy updates highlighting important developments, financial highlights if applicable (burn rate, runway, key financial metrics), forward-looking section outlining goals and priorities for [NEXT_PERIOD], and a closing with appreciation and invitation for questions or discussion. Write in a confident, transparent tone that balances celebration of wins with honest discussion of challenges. Use data and metrics to support claims. Be concise but comprehensive—investors are busy. Use clear formatting with headings, bullet points, and visual hierarchy. Include a professional email signature. Address [SPECIFIC_INVESTOR_CONCERNS] if relevant.

variations.short: Write an investor update email for [COMPANY] covering [PERIOD] to [INVESTORS] from [SENDER]. Include: summary, key metrics, wins, challenges, forward plan. Professional, data-driven.
variations.detailed: Create an investor update email for [COMPANY_NAME] period [TIME_PERIOD] to [INVESTOR_GROUP] from [SENDER/TITLE]. Structure: compelling subject line, greeting, executive summary (2-3 sentences), key metrics section ([METRIC_CATEGORIES] with numbers/context), major wins ([NUMBER] achievements with examples), challenges addressed (transparent, constructive), team updates (hires/changes), product/strategy updates, financial highlights (burn, runway, metrics), forward-looking goals for [NEXT_PERIOD], closing with appreciation and Q&A invitation. Tone: confident, transparent, data-driven. Format: clear headings, bullets. Address: [INVESTOR_CONCERNS]. Include signature.
variations.strict: Write investor email with exact structure: Subject ([WORDS] max), Greeting, Summary (50 words), Metrics ([NUMBER] categories, each with number + context), Wins ([NUMBER] items), Challenges ([NUMBER] items, each: issue + solution), Team ([NUMBER] updates), Product ([NUMBER] updates), Financial ([METRICS]), Forward Plan ([NUMBER] goals), Closing. Company: [NAME]. Period: [PERIOD]. Recipients: [GROUP]. Sender: [SENDER]. Must include: [REQUIREMENTS]. Data-driven, transparent.

tips: Lead with the most important information. Use specific numbers and metrics—avoid vague statements. Be transparent about challenges—investors appreciate honesty. Show progress over time with comparisons. Keep it concise—investors receive many updates. Use clear formatting for easy scanning. Include forward-looking statements to show direction. Send consistently (monthly/quarterly). Follow up on action items from previous updates. Personalize when possible for key investors.

title: Crisis Communication Drafting
primary_use_case: Create effective crisis communication messages that address issues transparently while protecting organizational reputation
user_role: PR Manager, Communications Director, Crisis Manager, Executive Team, Legal Counsel
prompt_text: You are a crisis communications expert specializing in crafting messages that address difficult situations with transparency, empathy, and clarity while protecting organizational reputation. Write a crisis communication statement regarding [CRISIS_SITUATION] for [ORGANIZATION_NAME] to be delivered via [COMMUNICATION_CHANNEL] (press release, social media, internal memo, etc.) to [TARGET_AUDIENCE]. The situation involves [SITUATION_DETAILS] and requires [COMMUNICATION_OBJECTIVES]. Structure the communication with: a clear, direct opening that acknowledges the situation without defensiveness, an expression of concern, empathy, or apology where appropriate (be genuine and specific), factual information about what happened (be transparent but avoid unnecessary detail that could cause harm), what the organization is doing to address the situation (immediate actions, investigation, remediation), what steps are being taken to prevent recurrence (if applicable), commitment to transparency and ongoing communication, contact information for media inquiries or questions, and a closing that reinforces values and commitment. Write in a tone that is [TONE_REQUIREMENTS]—typically calm, empathetic, transparent, and responsible. Avoid defensive language, blame-shifting, or minimizing the situation. Take responsibility where appropriate. Be concise but comprehensive. Use clear, simple language that avoids jargon. Ensure legal review for sensitive matters. Address [SPECIFIC_CONCERNS] that stakeholders may have. Include timeline for updates if the situation is ongoing.

variations.short: Write a crisis communication statement for [ORGANIZATION] regarding [SITUATION] to [AUDIENCE] via [CHANNEL]. Include: acknowledgment, facts, actions taken, prevention measures, contact info. Transparent, empathetic tone.
variations.detailed: Create a crisis communication statement for [ORGANIZATION_NAME] about [CRISIS_SITUATION] delivered via [CHANNEL] to [AUDIENCE]. Structure: direct opening acknowledging situation, genuine expression of concern/empathy/apology, factual details (transparent, appropriate level), immediate actions taken, investigation/remediation steps, prevention measures, commitment to transparency, contact information, closing reinforcing values. Situation: [DETAILS]. Objectives: [OBJECTIVES]. Tone: [TONE]—calm, empathetic, transparent, responsible. Avoid: defensiveness, blame-shifting, minimizing. Address: [STAKEHOLDER_CONCERNS]. Include: update timeline if ongoing. Legal review recommended.
variations.strict: Write crisis statement with exact structure: Opening (acknowledgment, [WORDS] max), Empathy/Apology ([WORDS], specific), Facts ([WORDS], transparent), Actions ([NUMBER] items, immediate), Investigation ([DETAILS]), Prevention ([MEASURES]), Transparency Commitment, Contact ([INFO]), Closing ([WORDS]). Organization: [NAME]. Situation: [SITUATION]. Audience: [AUDIENCE]. Channel: [CHANNEL]. Tone: [TONE]. Must include: [REQUIREMENTS]. Must avoid: [FORBIDDEN_ELEMENTS]. Legal review required.

tips: Respond quickly but accurately—speed matters in crisis. Lead with empathy and acknowledgment. Be transparent but don't share information that could cause harm. Take responsibility where appropriate. Avoid defensive language. Have legal counsel review sensitive statements. Provide regular updates if situation is ongoing. Use multiple channels if needed. Monitor response and adjust messaging. Train spokespeople on key messages. Have a crisis communication plan ready before crises occur.

title: Course/Training Content Creator
primary_use_case: Develop comprehensive educational content for courses, training programs, and learning materials
user_role: Instructional Designer, Training Manager, Educator, Learning & Development Specialist, Content Creator
industry: Education, Corporate Training, E-learning, Professional Development, Technology
prompt_text: You are an instructional design expert specializing in creating engaging, effective educational content that facilitates learning and skill development. Develop comprehensive course/training content for [COURSE_TOPIC] targeting learners with [PREREQUISITE_KNOWLEDGE] level of prior knowledge. The course should help learners achieve [LEARNING_OBJECTIVES] and be delivered in [FORMAT] (online, in-person, hybrid) over [DURATION]. The event's tone is: [formal, casual, celebratory, sentimental, humorous] and the audience includes: [audience_composition]. Structure the speech with: (1) A compelling opening (approximately [opening_length] seconds) that: grabs attention: [attention_grabber], introduces yourself: [speaker_introduction], establishes your relationship: [relationship_to_subject], and sets the tone: [tone_setter], (2) A body section (approximately [body_length] minutes) that: tells 2-3 engaging stories: [story_outlines] that illustrate: [qualities_or_themes], includes specific details: [vivid_details], uses humor appropriately: [humor_level], incorporates emotional moments: [sentimental_touches], and connects stories to broader themes: [themes_or_lessons], (3) A tribute section that: highlights key qualities: [admirable_qualities], acknowledges achievements: [achievements], expresses appreciation: [what_you_appreciate], and recognizes others if relevant: [other_people_to_thank], (4) A forward-looking section that: offers wishes: [future_wishes], shares hopes: [hopes_for_future], and provides encouragement: [encouraging_words], and (5) A memorable closing (approximately [closing_length] seconds) that: includes a toast, quote, or call-to-action: [closing_element], leaves a lasting impression: [final_message], and ends on a high note: [positive_ending]. title: Translation and Localization Assistant
primary_use_case: Provide translation and localization guidance that ensures content is culturally appropriate and linguistically accurate for target markets
user_role: Translator, Localization Specialist, Content Manager, Marketing Professional, Product Manager
industry: Technology, Marketing, E-commerce, Publishing, Global Business
prompt_text: You are an expert translator and localization specialist with deep cultural and linguistic expertise. Translate and localize [content_type: website_content, marketing_materials, user_interface, documents, etc.] from [source_language] to [target_language] for the [target_market_or_region] market. The original content is: [source_content] and it serves the purpose of: [content_purpose]. The target audience is: [target_audience_demographics] with cultural context: [cultural_background]. Key considerations include: [industry_specific_terminology], [brand_voice_guidelines], [legal_or_regulatory_requirements], and [formatting_preferences]. Provide a comprehensive translation that: (1) Accurately conveys the meaning: [preserve_intended_message], tone: [maintain_tone], and style: [preserve_style] of the original while adapting for: [cultural_nuances], [local_idioms], and [regional_preferences], (2) Adapts content culturally by: replacing cultural references: [cultural_adaptations_needed], adjusting humor: [humor_appropriateness], modifying examples: [example_replacements], and ensuring imagery is appropriate: [visual_considerations], (3) Localizes practical elements: [dates_and_formats: date_format, time_format, currency, measurements], [contact_information: phone_formats, addresses], [legal_compliance: disclaimers, terms], and [technical_considerations: character_encoding, text_expansion], (4) Maintains brand consistency: [brand_voice], [terminology_consistency], [messaging_alignment], while respecting: [local_market_expectations], (5) Optimizes for the target language's: [linguistic_features: grammar_rules, sentence_structure, formality_levels], [reading_patterns: left_to_right, right_to_left, vertical], and [character_limitations: if_applicable]. Provide both: a direct translation: [translation_output], cultural adaptation notes: [adaptation_rationale], and alternative phrasings: [variations] where multiple valid translations exist. variations.detailed: As a translation expert, translate [content_type] from [source_lang] to [target_lang] for [market]. Source: [source], purpose: [purpose]. Audience: [audience], culture: [background]. Considerations: terminology [terms], brand [voice], legal [requirements], format [preferences]. tips: Never translate word-for-word—translate meaning. Understand cultural context deeply. Work with native speakers for review. Consider regional variations within the same language. Test with target audience when possible. Maintain consistency with existing translations (use glossaries). Consider text expansion (some languages need 30% more space). Respect local regulations and sensitivities.

title: Performance Review Writer

user_role: Manager, HR Professional, Team Lead, Supervisor, Executive

Write a comprehensive performance review for [employee_name] in the role of [job_title] within [department] at [company_name]. The review period covers: [review_period: e.g., Q1_2024_to_Q4_2024] and this is a [review_type: annual, quarterly, mid_year, etc.] review. The employee's key responsibilities include: [job_responsibilities] and their goals for this period were: [performance_goals_or_KPIs]. Key achievements during this period: [specific_accomplishments] with quantifiable results: [metrics_and_numbers]. Areas of strength: [strengths] demonstrated through: [examples_of_strength]. Areas for improvement: [improvement_areas] evidenced by: [specific_examples]. The employee's performance ratings should reflect: [rating_scale: e.g., 1-5, exceeds_meets_below_expectations] across dimensions: [evaluation_criteria: quality_of_work, productivity, collaboration, leadership, innovation, etc.]. Structure the review with: (1) Executive summary that: provides overall assessment: [overall_rating], highlights key achievements: [top_achievements], identifies primary focus areas: [focus_areas], and sets tone for discussion: [review_tone], (2) Accomplishments section that: details major achievements: [achievement_details], quantifies impact: [metrics], provides context: [challenges_overcome], and links to goals: [goal_alignment], (3) Strengths analysis covering: [core_competencies] with specific examples: [strength_examples], impact on team/organization: [organizational_impact], and development potential: [growth_areas], (4) Development areas that: identify specific gaps: [gap_analysis], provide constructive feedback: [feedback], explain impact: [why_it_matters], and frame as opportunities: [growth_opportunities], (5) Goals and expectations for next period: [future_goals], [success_metrics], [development_objectives], and [support_resources], (6) Overall rating and summary: [final_assessment], [recommendations: promotion, raise, development_plan, etc.], and [next_steps]. Ensure the review is: balanced and fair, specific with examples, actionable with clear next steps, supportive and developmental, and aligned with company values: [company_values]. Structure the rewritten document to: (1) Begin with a clear overview section that: explains what the document is: [document_purpose], who it applies to: [applicable_parties], and why it matters: [importance_to_reader], (2) Organize content into logical sections with: descriptive headings: [section_headings], clear subheadings: [subheadings], and summary boxes: [key_points_highlighted], (3) Rewrite each section using: simple, everyday language: [plain_language_guidelines], short sentences: [sentence_length_guidelines], active voice: [voice_preference], and concrete examples: [examples_to_include], (4) Define legal terms when first introduced: [term_definitions] using: [definition_style: inline_definitions, glossary, footnotes], (5) Use formatting to enhance readability: [formatting_elements: bullet_points, numbered_lists, tables, callout_boxes], (6) Include a 'What this means' section for complex provisions: [explanatory_sections], and (7) Provide a summary or checklist: [executive_summary_or_checklist]. Flag any areas where: [legal_review_may_be_needed] due to: [complexity_or_risk]. Include both: the plain language version: [rewritten_document], and a comparison table: [before_after_comparison] showing key changes. Add a disclaimer: [legal_disclaimer] noting that: [plain_language_note] and recommending: [legal_consultation_if_needed].

title: Code Review and Feedback

user_role: Senior Developer, Code Reviewer, Tech Lead
prompt_text:
