Analyze the code for: 1) Code quality and readability - check naming conventions, code organization, and adherence to language-specific best practices. 2) Potential bugs and edge cases - identify logic errors, null pointer exceptions, array out-of-bounds issues, and unhandled error conditions. 3) Security vulnerabilities - look for SQL injection risks, XSS vulnerabilities, insecure authentication, and improper input validation. 4) Performance considerations - identify inefficient algorithms, unnecessary database queries, memory leaks, and optimization opportunities. 5) Maintainability - assess code complexity, documentation quality, and testability. Provide specific, actionable feedback with line numbers and suggestions for improvement. Rate the code on a scale of 1-10 and prioritize issues by severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low). Include code examples for suggested improvements where applicable.

Code to review:
[code_snippet]

variations.short: Review this [language] code for bugs, security issues, and best practices: [code_snippet]
variations.detailed: Conduct an exhaustive code review of the following [language] codebase located at [file_path]. Examine the entire codebase structure, including all dependencies and related files. Provide a detailed report covering: architecture patterns, design principles adherence, test coverage analysis, documentation completeness, dependency management, build configuration, and deployment considerations. Include a comparison with industry standards and frameworks. Generate a comprehensive improvement roadmap with prioritized action items.
variations.strict: Perform a strict, standards-compliant code review of [code_snippet] in [language]. Enforce [specific_standard] (e.g., PEP 8, Google Style Guide, Airbnb JavaScript Style Guide). Flag ALL violations, including formatting, naming conventions, and structural requirements. Provide exact fixes with no deviations from the standard. Include automated linting suggestions and ESLint/Prettier configuration recommendations.

tips: Provide the full context of the code including imports, related functions, and the problem it's solving. Specify the language version and any frameworks being used. Mention your team's coding standards or style guide if applicable.

title: Bug Debugging Assistant
primary_use_case: Identify and fix bugs in code
prompt_text: Debug the following issue in [language] code. The error message is: [error_message]. The stack trace shows: [stack_trace]. The problematic code section is: [code_snippet]. Additional context: [context_information]. Analyze the error systematically: 1) Parse the error message and stack trace to identify the exact line and function causing the issue. 2) Examine the code logic flow leading to the error - trace variable values, function calls, and data transformations. 3) Identify the root cause - determine if it's a logic error, type mismatch, null reference, index out of bounds, or resource management issue. 4) Check for related issues - look for similar patterns elsewhere in the codebase that might cause the same problem. 5) Provide a fix with explanation - suggest corrected code with comments explaining why the fix works. 6) Suggest prevention strategies - recommend error handling, input validation, or defensive programming techniques to prevent similar issues. Include test cases that reproduce the bug and verify the fix works correctly.

variations.short: Debug this error: [error_message]. Code: [code_snippet]
variations.detailed: Perform deep debugging analysis for the following production issue. Error occurred at [timestamp] in [environment]. Error details: [error_message]. Full stack trace: [stack_trace]. Affected codebase: [repository_url] at commit [commit_hash]. Code section: [code_snippet]. Related logs: [log_excerpts]. User reports: [user_feedback]. System metrics at time of error: [metrics]. Analyze the complete execution path, examine all related code, check dependencies and versions, review recent changes, analyze logs and monitoring data, identify contributing factors, and provide a comprehensive fix with rollback plan and monitoring recommendations.
variations.strict: Debug [error_message] in [code_snippet] following strict debugging protocol. Step 1: Reproduce the error with exact steps. Step 2: Isolate the minimal code causing the issue. Step 3: Identify the exact line and variable state. Step 4: Apply fix and verify with unit tests. Step 5: Check for regressions. Provide only verified solutions with test coverage.

tips: Include the complete error message, full stack trace, and relevant code context. Mention the environment (development/staging/production), recent code changes, and steps to reproduce. Include any relevant logs or monitoring data.

title: Code Refactoring
primary_use_case: Improve code structure and maintainability without changing functionality
user_role: Senior Developer, Software Architect, Tech Lead
prompt_text: Refactor the following [language] code to improve maintainability, readability, and adherence to best practices while preserving exact functionality. The code to refactor is: [code_snippet]. Current issues identified: [issues_list]. Refactoring goals: [refactoring_goals]. Apply the following refactoring techniques as appropriate: 1) Extract methods/functions - break down large functions into smaller, single-responsibility functions with descriptive names. 2) Remove code duplication - identify and consolidate repeated logic using helper functions or classes. 3) Improve naming - use clear, descriptive names for variables, functions, and classes that express intent. 4) Simplify conditionals - reduce nesting, use guard clauses, and apply early returns where beneficial. 5) Apply design patterns - introduce appropriate patterns (Factory, Strategy, Observer, etc.) if they improve structure. 6) Improve error handling - add proper exception handling and validation. 7) Add type hints/annotations - improve type safety and IDE support. 8) Optimize data structures - choose more appropriate collections or data types. Provide the refactored code with before/after comparisons and explanations for each major change. Ensure all existing tests still pass.

variations.short: Refactor this [language] code for better maintainability: [code_snippet]
variations.detailed: Perform comprehensive refactoring of the entire [module/class/file] located at [file_path]. Analyze the codebase structure, dependencies, test coverage, and documentation. Create a refactoring plan addressing: architecture improvements, design pattern application, dependency injection, SOLID principles adherence, testability enhancements, documentation updates, and performance optimizations. Provide phased refactoring approach with risk assessment, migration strategy, and rollback plan. Include before/after metrics (cyclomatic complexity, test coverage, code smells).
variations.strict: Refactor [code_snippet] strictly following [specific_refactoring_pattern] (e.g., Extract Method, Replace Conditional with Polymorphism). Apply only proven refactoring techniques from Martin Fowler's catalog. Maintain 100% test coverage. No functionality changes allowed. Provide refactoring steps with verification at each stage.

tips: Specify which aspects to focus on (performance, readability, testability). Include existing tests to ensure functionality is preserved. Mention any constraints (e.g., must maintain backward compatibility, specific patterns to use/avoid).

title: Unit Test Generator
primary_use_case: Generate comprehensive unit tests for code
prompt_text: Generate comprehensive unit tests for the following [language] code using [testing_framework]. The code to test is: [code_snippet]. Testing requirements: [requirements]. Create tests that cover: 1) Happy path scenarios - test normal operation with valid inputs and expected outputs. 2) Edge cases - test boundary conditions, empty inputs, null values, zero, negative numbers, and maximum values. 3) Error handling - verify proper exception throwing and error messages for invalid inputs and error conditions. 4) Edge behaviors - test with unexpected but valid inputs, type boundaries, and state transitions. 5) Integration points - mock external dependencies, APIs, databases, and file systems appropriately. 6) Performance considerations - include tests for performance-critical paths if applicable. Use descriptive test names following [naming_convention] (e.g., Given-When-Then, Should-When). Structure tests with proper setup, execution, and assertions. Include test fixtures, mocks, and test data builders as needed. Aim for high code coverage while ensuring tests are maintainable and readable. Provide both positive and negative test cases.

variations.short: Generate unit tests for this [language] function: [code_snippet]
variations.detailed: Create a complete test suite for [class/module] at [file_path] using [testing_framework]. Include: unit tests, integration tests, property-based tests, performance tests, and mutation tests. Set up test infrastructure (fixtures, factories, mocks, test database). Generate tests for all public methods, edge cases, error scenarios, and integration points. Include test documentation, coverage reports, and CI/CD integration. Follow [testing_pattern] (AAA, BDD, etc.). Target 90%+ coverage with meaningful assertions.
variations.strict: Generate unit tests for [code_snippet] following strict TDD principles. Write tests FIRST before implementation. Use [specific_framework] with [specific_pattern]. Cover 100% of branches. All tests must be isolated, fast, and deterministic. No flaky tests. Include property-based tests using [property_testing_library]. Enforce with [coverage_tool] at 100% threshold.

tips: Specify the testing framework (Jest, pytest, JUnit, etc.) and preferred testing patterns. Include the code's dependencies and context. Mention any mocking requirements or specific edge cases to cover.

title: API Endpoint Design
primary_use_case: Design RESTful or GraphQL API endpoints
user_role: Backend Developer, API Designer, Software Architect
prompt_text: Design a [REST/GraphQL] API endpoint for [functionality_description]. Requirements: [requirements]. The endpoint should handle [operations] operations. Design considerations: 1) URL structure - create RESTful, hierarchical URLs following REST conventions (e.g., /api/v1/resource/{id}/subresource). Use appropriate HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) for each operation. 2) Request/Response format - define JSON schemas for request bodies and response payloads. Include proper status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 500, etc.). 3) Authentication and authorization - specify authentication mechanism (JWT, OAuth, API keys) and authorization rules (who can access what). 4) Input validation - define validation rules for path parameters, query parameters, and request bodies. Include required fields, data types, formats, and constraints. 5) Error handling - design consistent error response format with error codes, messages, and details. 6) Pagination and filtering - implement pagination (offset/limit or cursor-based) and filtering/sorting capabilities for list endpoints. 7) Rate limiting and caching - specify rate limits and caching strategies. 8) Versioning - include API versioning strategy. Provide OpenAPI/Swagger specification or GraphQL schema, example requests/responses, and implementation code in [language] using [framework].

variations.short: Design a REST API endpoint for [functionality]: [requirements]
variations.detailed: Design a complete API system for [domain] including all CRUD operations, relationships, authentication, authorization, rate limiting, caching, versioning, documentation, SDK generation, monitoring, and analytics. Create OpenAPI 3.0 specification, GraphQL schema, Postman collection, API documentation site, and implementation in [framework]. Include API gateway configuration, request/response transformation, error handling strategy, and deployment architecture.
variations.strict: Design REST API endpoint strictly following OpenAPI 3.0 specification and RFC 7231 HTTP standards. Endpoint: [endpoint_description]. Must include: OpenAPI YAML, JSON Schema validation, OAuth 2.0 flow, rate limiting (100 req/min), pagination (max 100 items), proper HTTP status codes, HATEOAS links, and CORS configuration. No deviations from REST principles.

tips: Specify the API type (REST/GraphQL), framework (Express, FastAPI, Spring Boot), and authentication method. Include business requirements, data models, and any constraints (rate limits, response size). Mention versioning requirements.

title: Database Schema Design
primary_use_case: Design database schemas and data models
user_role: Database Administrator, Backend Developer, Data Engineer
prompt_text: Design a database schema for [database_type] (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, etc.) to support [application_description]. Requirements: [requirements]. Business entities: [entities_list]. Design a schema that includes: 1) Table/Collection structure - define all tables/collections with appropriate names following [naming_convention]. Include all necessary columns/fields with correct data types, constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK), and default values. 2) Relationships - establish proper relationships (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) using foreign keys or references. Include junction tables for many-to-many relationships. 3) Primary keys and indexes - define primary keys (single or composite) and create indexes on foreign keys and frequently queried columns. Consider unique indexes and composite indexes for query optimization. 4) Data integrity - add constraints to ensure referential integrity, data validation, and business rules enforcement. 5) Normalization - apply appropriate normalization level (typically 3NF) to eliminate redundancy while considering denormalization for performance if needed. 6) Audit fields - include created_at, updated_at, created_by, updated_by fields for audit trails. 7) Soft deletes - consider soft delete patterns if needed. Provide CREATE TABLE statements or schema definitions, ER diagram description, migration scripts, and example seed data. Include performance considerations and indexing strategy.

Explain the trade-offs between different solutions.

variations.strict: Translate [source_code] from [source_language] to [target_language] with 100% functional equivalence. Use only standard libraries. No functionality changes. Provide unit tests proving equivalence. Include performance comparison and memory usage analysis.

title: Security Vulnerability Scanner

Scan for: 1) Injection vulnerabilities - check for SQL injection, NoSQL injection, command injection, LDAP injection, and XML injection risks. Identify places where user input is directly concatenated into queries or commands. 2) Authentication and authorization flaws - review authentication mechanisms, session management, password policies, and authorization checks. Look for broken authentication, session fixation, and privilege escalation risks. 3) Sensitive data exposure - identify hardcoded secrets, API keys, passwords, and sensitive data in code or configuration. Check for proper encryption of data at rest and in transit. 4) XML/XXE vulnerabilities - check XML parsing for external entity injection risks. 5) Broken access control - verify proper access controls, authorization checks, and CORS configuration. 6) Security misconfiguration - identify insecure default configurations, unnecessary features, and missing security headers. 7) XSS vulnerabilities - check for reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS in web applications. 8) Insecure deserialization - identify unsafe deserialization of untrusted data. 9) Dependency vulnerabilities - check for known vulnerabilities in dependencies. Provide a prioritized list of vulnerabilities with severity ratings, affected code locations, exploit scenarios, and remediation steps with code examples.

variations.strict: Perform security scan strictly following [standard] (e.g., OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25). Code: [code_snippet]. Must identify all vulnerability categories, provide CVSS scores, exploit proof-of-concepts, and remediation with verified fixes. Zero false positives.

prompt_text: Implement a [REST/GraphQL] API endpoint/service for [functionality_description] using [language] and [framework]. API specification: [api_spec]. Database: [database_type]. Authentication: [auth_method]. Requirements: [requirements]. Implement: 1) Endpoint/Resolver implementation - create the API endpoint (REST) or resolver (GraphQL) with proper routing and request handling. Handle HTTP methods and status codes appropriately. 2) Request validation - validate input parameters, request bodies, and query parameters. Return clear error messages for invalid inputs. 3) Business logic - implement the core business logic, data processing, and workflow. Follow clean architecture principles. 4) Database operations - implement database queries using [orm/query_builder] with proper error handling, transactions, and connection management. 5) Authentication and authorization - implement authentication checks and authorization logic to ensure users have proper permissions. 6) Error handling - implement consistent error handling with appropriate HTTP status codes and error response format. 7) Logging and monitoring - add logging for important operations and integrate with monitoring systems. 8) Testing - provide unit tests and integration tests. Include complete implementation code, database models/schemas, tests, and API documentation.

variations.short: Implement [REST/GraphQL] API for [functionality] using [framework]: [requirements]
variations.detailed: Build complete backend API system for [domain] including: API implementation (REST/GraphQL), database models and migrations, authentication/authorization system, input validation, error handling, logging, monitoring, rate limiting, caching, API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger), unit tests, integration tests, load testing, deployment configuration, and CI/CD integration. Framework: [framework]. Support [scale] requests/sec.
variations.strict: Implement API endpoint strictly following [framework] best practices and [API_design_pattern] (e.g., Repository pattern). Endpoint: [description]. Must include: input validation, error handling, logging, tests (90%+ coverage), OpenAPI documentation, and security best practices. No N+1 queries, proper transaction handling.

tips: Specify the API type (REST/GraphQL), framework, language, and database. Include the API specification or requirements. Mention authentication method and any specific patterns or constraints.

title: Data Pipeline Builder
primary_use_case: Create data processing and ETL pipelines
user_role: Data Engineer, Backend Developer, Data Scientist
prompt_text: Design and implement a data pipeline for [pipeline_description] using [technology_stack] (Apache Airflow, Spark, Kafka, etc.). Data sources: [data_sources]. Data destinations: [destinations]. Transformation requirements: [transformation_requirements]. Processing type: [batch/streaming]. Requirements: [requirements]. Create a pipeline that includes: 1) Data ingestion - implement data extraction from sources (databases, APIs, files, streams) with proper error handling and retry logic. Handle different data formats (JSON, CSV, Parquet, etc.). 2) Data transformation - implement data cleaning, validation, transformation, and enrichment logic. Handle data quality issues, duplicates, and missing values. 3) Data validation - add data quality checks, schema validation, and business rule validation. Implement data quality monitoring. 4) Data loading - implement data loading into destinations (data warehouses, databases, data lakes) with appropriate loading strategies (full load, incremental, upsert). 5) Error handling and monitoring - implement comprehensive error handling, logging, alerting, and monitoring. Handle failures gracefully with retry and dead-letter queues. 6) Scheduling and orchestration - set up pipeline scheduling, dependencies, and orchestration. 7) Scalability - design for horizontal scaling and handle large data volumes efficiently. 8) Testing - provide unit tests and integration tests. Include pipeline code, configuration, tests, and deployment instructions.

variations.short: Create data pipeline for [task] using [technology]: [requirements]
variations.detailed: Design comprehensive data engineering solution for [use_case] including: data ingestion from [sources], ETL/ELT pipeline, data transformation, data quality framework, data validation, error handling, monitoring and alerting, scheduling (Airflow/Luigi), data warehouse design, data lake architecture, streaming pipeline (Kafka/Flink), batch processing (Spark), data governance, and documentation. Process [data_volume] daily with [latency] requirement.
variations.strict: Create data pipeline strictly following [framework] best practices (e.g., Apache Airflow DAG patterns). Pipeline: [description]. Must include: idempotent operations, proper error handling, data quality checks, monitoring, and tests. Process [data_volume] with [SLA] guarantee.

tips: Specify the technology stack (Airflow, Spark, etc.) and processing type (batch/streaming). Include data sources, destinations, transformation logic, and volume/latency requirements. Mention any data quality or compliance requirements.

title: Cron Job / Scheduled Task Creator

user_role: DevOps Engineer, Backend Developer, System Administrator
prompt_text: Create a scheduled task/cron job to [task_description] using [scheduling_method] (cron, systemd timer, task scheduler, etc.). Task details: [task_details]. Schedule: [schedule] (e.g., daily at 2 AM, every 5 minutes, on first Monday of month). Execution environment: [environment]. Requirements: [requirements]. Create a solution that includes: 1) Task script - implement the actual task logic in [language] with proper error handling, logging, and exit codes. Make the script idempotent and handle failures gracefully. 2) Scheduling configuration - create cron expression or scheduling configuration with proper syntax. Ensure timezone is correctly specified. 3) Logging - implement logging to files or logging systems with rotation and retention policies. Include timestamps and log levels. 4) Error handling - implement error handling, retry logic, and notification on failures (email, Slack, etc.). 5) Resource management - ensure the task doesn't consume excessive resources and handles long-running operations appropriately. 6) Monitoring - add monitoring and alerting for task execution status, duration, and failures. 7) Testing - provide ways to test the task manually and verify the schedule. Include the task script, scheduling configuration, logging setup, and monitoring configuration.

variations.short: Create cron job to [task] running [schedule]: [requirements]
variations.detailed: Design comprehensive scheduled task system for [organization] including: task scheduler setup (cron/Airflow/Celery), task implementation, error handling and retries, logging and monitoring, alerting (email/Slack/PagerDuty), task dependencies, resource limits, execution history tracking, dashboard for task status, and documentation. Support [task_count] tasks with [execution_frequency].
variations.strict: Create cron job strictly following [scheduler] syntax (e.g., standard cron format). Task: [description]. Schedule: [cron_expression]. Must include: proper logging, error handling, idempotency, and monitoring. No resource leaks. Provide exact cron syntax and verification steps.

tips: Specify the scheduling method (cron, systemd, cloud scheduler) and execution environment. Include the exact schedule needed and any constraints (timezone, resource limits). Mention notification requirements.

title: Environment Configuration Manager
primary_use_case: Manage application configuration across environments
user_role: DevOps Engineer, Backend Developer, Platform Engineer
prompt_text: Design an environment configuration management system for [application_type] to handle configuration across [environments] (development, staging, production). Configuration requirements: [requirements]. Secrets handling: [secrets_requirements]. Configuration sources: [config_sources]. Create a solution that includes: 1) Configuration structure - design a hierarchical configuration system with environment-specific overrides. Use configuration files (YAML, JSON, TOML, .env) or configuration management tools. 2) Environment variables - define environment variables with defaults, validation, and documentation. Use 12-factor app principles. 3) Secrets management - integrate with secrets management systems (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, etc.) for sensitive data. Never hardcode secrets. 4) Configuration validation - implement validation for configuration values (types, ranges, required fields) with clear error messages. 5) Configuration loading - implement configuration loading logic that merges defaults, environment-specific configs, and environment variables with proper precedence. 6) Type safety - use typed configuration objects/interfaces for type safety and IDE support. 7) Documentation - document all configuration options, their purposes, defaults, and environment-specific values. 8) Testing - provide configuration testing and validation tools. Include configuration files, loading code, validation logic, and documentation.

variations.short: Create configuration management for [application] across [environments]: [requirements]
variations.detailed: Design comprehensive configuration management system for [organization] including: multi-environment configuration (dev/staging/prod), secrets management integration (Vault/AWS Secrets Manager), configuration validation, type-safe configuration loading, configuration templates, environment variable management, configuration versioning, rollback capabilities, configuration documentation, and tooling for configuration management. Support [application_count] applications with [config_complexity].
variations.strict: Create configuration management strictly following 12-factor app principles and [framework] best practices. Application: [type]. Must include: environment-based configs, secrets management, validation, type safety, and documentation. No hardcoded values. Support [environments] with [secrets_count] secrets.

tips: Specify the application type and environments. Include configuration requirements and any secrets management tools. Mention preferred configuration format and any validation rules or constraints.

title: Code Complexity Reducer
primary_use_case: Reduce code complexity and improve maintainability
user_role: Senior Developer, Software Architect, Tech Lead
prompt_text: Reduce the complexity of the following [language] code: [code_snippet]. Current complexity metrics: [complexity_metrics] (cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, etc.). Target complexity: [target_complexity]. Requirements: [requirements]. Analyze and reduce complexity by: 1) Complexity analysis - measure current complexity using metrics (cyclomatic complexity, cognitive complexity, nesting depth). Identify complexity hotspots and problematic patterns. 2) Extract methods/functions - break down complex functions into smaller, single-purpose functions with clear names. Apply the Single Responsibility Principle. 3) Simplify conditionals - reduce nested if statements using guard clauses, early returns, and boolean logic simplification. Consider using switch statements or lookup tables for complex conditionals. 4) Reduce nesting - flatten nested structures using early returns, extraction, and inversion of conditions. 5) Eliminate code duplication - identify and extract common patterns into reusable functions or classes. 6) Apply design patterns - introduce appropriate design patterns (Strategy, Command, Factory) to simplify complex logic. 7) Improve data structures - use more appropriate data structures that simplify algorithms. 8) Add abstraction layers - introduce abstractions to hide complexity and improve readability. Provide refactored code with complexity metrics before/after, explanations of changes, and verification that functionality is preserved.

variations.short: Reduce complexity of this code: [code_snippet]
variations.detailed: Perform comprehensive complexity reduction for [module/codebase] including: complexity analysis (cyclomatic, cognitive, nesting), identification of complexity hotspots, refactoring plan, code simplification, design pattern application, test coverage maintenance, complexity metrics tracking, and documentation. Target: reduce complexity by [percentage]% while maintaining functionality. Include before/after metrics and refactoring guide.
variations.strict: Reduce code complexity strictly to meet [target_metric] (e.g., cyclomatic complexity < 10). Code: [code_snippet]. Must maintain 100% functionality, pass all tests, and achieve target complexity. Provide refactored code with complexity analysis proving the reduction.

tips: Provide the code and current complexity metrics if available. Specify target complexity goals. Include existing tests to ensure functionality is preserved. Mention any constraints or specific patterns to use/avoid.

title: Microservices Architecture Planner
primary_use_case: Design and plan a microservices architecture for a [application_type] application
prompt_text: Design a comprehensive microservices architecture for a [application_type] application that needs to handle [expected_load] requests per second. The system should support [key_features] and integrate with [external_services]. Create a detailed architecture plan that includes: (1) Service decomposition strategy identifying [number_of_services] microservices with clear boundaries and responsibilities, (2) Communication patterns (synchronous REST/GraphQL APIs, asynchronous message queues like RabbitMQ/Kafka) between services, (3) Data management approach (database per service pattern, event sourcing, CQRS where applicable), (4) API gateway configuration for routing and load balancing, (5) Service discovery mechanism (Consul, Eureka, Kubernetes services), (6) Distributed tracing and monitoring setup (Jaeger, Zipkin, Prometheus), (7) Security implementation (OAuth2, JWT tokens, service mesh with mTLS), (8) Deployment strategy (containerization with Docker, orchestration with Kubernetes, CI/CD pipeline), and (9) Failure handling (circuit breakers, retries, bulkheads). Consider scalability requirements, fault tolerance, and maintainability. Provide code examples for service interfaces, configuration files, and deployment manifests.

variations.short: Design microservices architecture for [application_type] with [number_of_services] services, including communication patterns, data management, and deployment strategy.
variations.detailed: Create a comprehensive microservices architecture plan for [application_type] application handling [expected_load] RPS. Include service decomposition, inter-service communication (REST/GraphQL/message queues), database-per-service pattern, API gateway, service discovery, distributed tracing, security (OAuth2/JWT), containerization (Docker/Kubernetes), CI/CD pipeline, and failure handling patterns. Provide implementation code examples.
variations.strict: Design microservices architecture following Domain-Driven Design principles. Must include: bounded contexts mapped to services, event-driven communication via Kafka, database-per-service with eventual consistency, API gateway (Kong/AWS API Gateway), Kubernetes deployment manifests, service mesh (Istio) for security, distributed tracing (Jaeger), and comprehensive monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana). Provide complete YAML configs and code.

tips: Start with domain boundaries before technical decisions. Use event-driven architecture for loose coupling. Implement health checks and graceful shutdowns. Consider API versioning strategy. Use container orchestration for scalability.

title: Authentication/Authorization Implementation
primary_use_case: Implement secure authentication and authorization system for [application_type]
prompt_text: Implement a complete authentication and authorization system for a [application_type] application using [authentication_method]. The system should support [user_types] with different permission levels. Requirements include: (1) User registration with email verification and password strength validation (minimum [password_length] characters, requiring uppercase, lowercase, numbers, special characters), (2) Login functionality with rate limiting ([max_attempts] attempts per [time_window] minutes) and account lockout after failed attempts, (3) Token-based authentication using JWT with access tokens (expires in [access_token_expiry] minutes) and refresh tokens (expires in [refresh_token_expiry] days), stored securely in httpOnly cookies, (4) Password reset flow via email with secure token generation and expiration, (5) Multi-factor authentication (MFA) using TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) via authenticator apps, (6) Role-based access control (RBAC) with roles [list_of_roles] and permissions [list_of_permissions], (7) Session management with token refresh mechanism, (8) OAuth2 integration for [social_providers] (Google, GitHub, etc.), (9) API endpoint protection with middleware for route-level authorization, and (10) Security best practices (password hashing with bcrypt/argon2, CSRF protection, XSS prevention, secure headers). Provide complete implementation code including database schema, middleware, routes, and frontend integration examples.

variations.short: Implement authentication system with JWT tokens, password hashing, MFA, RBAC, and OAuth2 integration for [application_type].
variations.detailed: Build secure authentication/authorization system for [application_type] with user registration, email verification, login with rate limiting, JWT tokens (access/refresh), password reset, MFA (TOTP), RBAC with roles [list_of_roles], OAuth2 ([social_providers]), session management, API protection middleware, and security best practices. Include database schema and frontend examples.
variations.strict: Implement authentication following OWASP guidelines. Must use: argon2 for password hashing, JWT with RS256 algorithm, refresh tokens in httpOnly cookies, rate limiting (10 attempts/15min), MFA with TOTP, RBAC with role hierarchy, OAuth2 PKCE flow, CSRF tokens, secure session management, and comprehensive audit logging. Provide complete code with tests.

tips: Never store passwords in plain text. Use secure random tokens for password reset. Implement token rotation for refresh tokens. Validate all inputs server-side. Use HTTPS in production. Store sensitive data in environment variables.

title: Websocket/Real-time Feature Builder
primary_use_case: Build real-time communication features using WebSockets for [feature_type]
prompt_text: Build a real-time [feature_type] system using WebSockets that enables [real_time_capabilities]. The implementation should include: (1) WebSocket server setup using [websocket_library] (Socket.io, ws, or native WebSocket API) with connection handling and reconnection logic, (2) Authentication and authorization for WebSocket connections using JWT tokens passed in connection handshake, (3) Room/channel management for organizing users into [room_types] (e.g., chat rooms, game lobbies, collaborative sessions), (4) Real-time message broadcasting to [broadcast_scope] (all users, room members, specific users) with message queuing for offline users, (5) Presence system showing online/offline status and typing indicators, (6) Heartbeat/ping-pong mechanism to detect and handle disconnected clients, (7) Message persistence to database for history and recovery, (8) Rate limiting per connection to prevent abuse ([messages_per_second] messages per second), (9) Error handling and graceful degradation (fallback to polling if WebSocket fails), (10) Frontend integration with connection state management, auto-reconnect, and UI updates. Support [number_of_concurrent_users] concurrent connections. Provide complete server-side and client-side implementation code with examples for [use_case_scenarios].

variations.short: Build WebSocket-based real-time [feature_type] with authentication, rooms, broadcasting, presence, and reconnection handling.
variations.detailed: Implement real-time [feature_type] using WebSockets ([websocket_library]) with JWT authentication, room management, message broadcasting, presence indicators, heartbeat mechanism, message persistence, rate limiting, error handling, and frontend integration. Support [number_of_concurrent_users] concurrent users.
variations.strict: Build production-ready WebSocket system using Socket.io with Redis adapter for horizontal scaling. Must include: JWT auth in handshake, room management with Redis pub/sub, message persistence (MongoDB), presence tracking (Redis), heartbeat (30s interval), rate limiting (100 msg/min), graceful shutdown, connection pooling, and comprehensive error handling. Provide full code with tests.

tips: Use connection pooling for scalability. Implement message queuing for offline users. Handle reconnection gracefully. Use Redis for horizontal scaling. Monitor connection count and message throughput. Implement backpressure for high-load scenarios.

title: Caching Strategy Designer
primary_use_case: Design and implement a comprehensive caching strategy for [application_type]
prompt_text: Design and implement a multi-layer caching strategy for a [application_type] application that needs to reduce database load and improve response times for [cached_resources]. The caching architecture should include: (1) Application-level caching using in-memory cache (Redis/Memcached) for frequently accessed data with TTL (Time To Live) of [cache_ttl] seconds and cache invalidation strategies (TTL-based, event-driven, manual), (2) Database query result caching for expensive queries with cache keys based on query parameters and user context, (3) HTTP response caching using CDN (CloudFlare, AWS CloudFront) for static assets and API responses with appropriate cache headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified), (4) Session storage caching for user sessions and authentication tokens, (5) Cache warming strategies for pre-loading critical data during low-traffic periods, (6) Cache-aside pattern implementation with fallback to database on cache miss, (7) Write-through or write-behind caching for write operations depending on consistency requirements, (8) Cache key naming conventions and namespacing to prevent collisions, (9) Cache monitoring and metrics (hit rate, miss rate, eviction rate) using tools like Prometheus, (10) Distributed caching setup for multi-server deployments with cache coherence. Handle cache stampede prevention using locks or probabilistic early expiration. Provide implementation code for cache middleware, cache utilities, and configuration examples.

variations.short: Design caching strategy with Redis, CDN, query caching, and cache invalidation for [application_type].
variations.detailed: Implement multi-layer caching: Redis for application cache (TTL [cache_ttl]s), database query caching, CDN for static assets, session caching, cache warming, cache-aside pattern, write-through/write-behind, key naming conventions, monitoring, and distributed caching. Include cache stampede prevention.
variations.strict: Design caching following best practices: Redis cluster for distributed cache, CDN with cache headers, query result caching with invalidation on data changes, cache-aside with circuit breaker, write-behind for high write loads, consistent hashing for key distribution, cache warming cron jobs, and comprehensive monitoring (hit/miss rates). Provide Redis config and code.

tips: Choose TTL based on data update frequency. Implement cache invalidation on data mutations. Use cache keys with versioning. Monitor cache performance metrics. Consider cache warming for predictable access patterns. Use distributed locks for cache stampede prevention.

title: Email/Notification System Builder

prompt_text: Build a comprehensive email and notification system for [application_type] that sends [notification_types] to users. The system should include: (1) Email service integration using [email_provider] (SendGrid, AWS SES, Mailgun, SMTP) with API key management and rate limiting handling, (2) Email template system supporting HTML and plain text versions with dynamic variable substitution using [template_engine] (Handlebars, Jinja2, Mustache), (3) Email queue system using [queue_system] (RabbitMQ, Redis Queue, AWS SQS) for asynchronous processing and retry logic with exponential backoff, (4) Multiple notification channels: email, SMS (via Twilio/AWS SNS), push notifications (FCM/APNS), and in-app notifications, (5) User preference management allowing users to opt-in/opt-out of specific notification types, (6) Notification templates for common scenarios ([template_scenarios]: welcome emails, password reset, order confirmations, alerts), (7) Email tracking and analytics (open rates, click rates, bounce handling) with webhook integration, (8) Batch sending capabilities for bulk notifications with throttling to respect provider limits, (9) Notification scheduling for delayed sends (reminders, follow-ups), (10) Error handling and dead letter queue for failed notifications. Support [email_volume] emails per day. Provide complete implementation code including queue workers, template examples, and configuration files.

variations.short: Build email/notification system with [email_provider], templates, queue system, multi-channel support (email/SMS/push), user preferences, and analytics.
variations.detailed: Implement notification system: [email_provider] integration, HTML/text templates ([template_engine]), async queue ([queue_system]) with retries, multi-channel (email/SMS/push/in-app), user preferences, templates for [template_scenarios], tracking/analytics, batch sending, scheduling, error handling. variations.strict: Build production notification system: AWS SES/SendGrid with SPF/DKIM/DMARC, Handlebars templates, Redis Queue workers, Twilio SMS, FCM push, user preference DB, webhook tracking, exponential backoff retries (max 3), dead letter queue, rate limiting, and monitoring. Provide complete code with tests.

title: File Upload/Processing System

variations.short: Build file upload system with validation, [storage_backend] storage, processing pipeline ([processing_tasks]), thumbnails, metadata storage, access control, and rate limiting.
variations.detailed: Implement secure file upload: multipart API, validation (type/size/virus scan), [storage_backend] storage, processing ([processing_tasks]), thumbnail generation ([thumbnail_sizes]), metadata DB, signed URLs, cleanup, rate limiting ([max_uploads_per_hour]/hour), error handling. variations.strict: Build production file upload: multipart API with streaming, validation (whitelist MIME types, max [max_file_size]MB, ClamAV scan), S3 with versioning, async processing (Celery/Redis), image optimization (Sharp/Pillow), thumbnail variants, metadata (PostgreSQL), presigned URLs (15min expiry), cron cleanup, rate limiting (Redis), comprehensive error handling. tips: Validate files server-side, not just client-side. Use streaming uploads for large files. Generate unique filenames to prevent overwrites. Implement virus scanning for user uploads. Use CDN for file delivery. Set appropriate file size limits. Clean up failed uploads regularly.

title: Rate Limiting and Throttling

Support [number_of_concurrent_users] users.
variations.strict: Implement Redis-based distributed rate limiting: sliding window log algorithm, per-API-key limits (1000/min, 10000/hour), tier-based (free: 100/min, premium: 1000/min), Redis with Lua scripts for atomicity, standard rate limit headers, 429 with Retry-After, IP whitelist/blacklist, endpoint-specific configs, burst (20% over limit), Prometheus metrics. tips: Use Redis for distributed rate limiting. Implement multiple algorithms for different use cases. Return clear rate limit headers. Use exponential backoff for retries. Monitor rate limit hits to adjust limits. Consider burst allowances for better UX.

title: Data Migration Script Writer
primary_use_case: Create data migration scripts to migrate [data_type] from [source] to [destination]
prompt_text: Create a robust data migration script to migrate [data_type] from [source_system] to [destination_system] while ensuring data integrity and minimal downtime. title: Accessibility (a11y) Compliance Fixer
primary_use_case: Fix accessibility issues and ensure WCAG [wcag_level] compliance for [application_type]
prompt_text: Fix accessibility issues and ensure WCAG [wcag_level] (A, AA, AAA) compliance for [application_type] built with [framework]. The accessibility fixes should include: (1) Semantic HTML structure with proper heading hierarchy (h1-h6), landmarks (header, nav, main, aside, footer), and ARIA labels where needed, (2) Keyboard navigation support for all interactive elements with proper tab order, focus indicators, and keyboard shortcuts, (3) Screen reader optimization with ARIA attributes (aria-label, aria-describedby, aria-live, aria-hidden), roles, and proper labeling for form inputs, buttons, and complex widgets, (4) Color contrast compliance meeting WCAG contrast ratios (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) for all text and UI elements, (5) Form accessibility with proper labels, error messages, fieldset/legend for groups, and validation feedback announced to screen readers, (6) Image accessibility with descriptive alt text for informative images and empty alt attributes for decorative images, (7) Focus management for modals, dropdowns, and dynamic content with proper focus trapping and focus restoration, (8) Responsive design ensuring accessibility on mobile devices with touch targets at least 44x44 pixels, (9) Accessibility testing using automated tools ([a11y_tools]: axe, Lighthouse, WAVE) and manual testing with screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), (10) Documentation of accessibility features and keyboard shortcuts for users. Fix [identified_issues] accessibility issues. Provide complete fixed code with accessibility improvements and testing results.

variations.short: Fix a11y for WCAG [wcag_level]: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes, color contrast, form labels, image alt text, focus management, responsive design, testing ([a11y_tools]), documentation.
variations.detailed: Accessibility compliance: semantic HTML (headings/landmarks), keyboard nav (tab order/focus), ARIA (labels/roles/live regions), contrast (4.5:1), forms (labels/errors/fieldsets), images (alt text), focus (modals/dropdowns), mobile (44x44px targets), testing ([a11y_tools]/screen readers), docs. Fix [identified_issues] issues.
variations.strict: WCAG AA compliance: semantic HTML5, keyboard nav with skip links, ARIA 1.1 attributes, contrast checker (4.5:1), form labels + aria-describedby, descriptive alt text, focus trap (react-focus-lock), touch targets (48x48px), axe-core + Lighthouse + manual testing (NVDA), a11y docs. Full fixes.

tips: Test with actual screen readers. Use semantic HTML first, ARIA when needed. Ensure keyboard navigation works. Check color contrast. Provide text alternatives for images. Test with real users. Automate accessibility testing in CI/CD.

title: Internationalization (i18n) Implementation
primary_use_case: Implement internationalization (i18n) support for [application_type] supporting [target_languages]
prompt_text: Implement comprehensive internationalization (i18n) support for [application_type] built with [framework] to support [target_languages] languages. The implementation should include: (1) i18n library setup using [i18n_library] (react-i18next, vue-i18n, i18next, react-intl) with configuration and locale detection, (2) Translation file structure organizing translations by locale ([locale_structure]: JSON, YAML, separate files per namespace) with proper key naming conventions, (3) String extraction and translation management workflow for identifying translatable strings and managing translations, (4) Locale detection from browser settings, user preferences, or URL parameters with fallback to default locale, (5) Dynamic language switching with UI language selector and persistence of user preference, (6) Pluralization support for different languages with proper plural rules and plural forms, (7) Date and time formatting using locale-specific formats and timezone handling with [date_library] (date-fns, moment.js, Intl.DateTimeFormat), (8) Number and currency formatting with locale-specific number formats, currency symbols, and decimal separators, (9) Right-to-left (RTL) language support for [rtl_languages] with CSS direction changes and layout adjustments, (10) Translation loading strategy with lazy loading of translation files, code splitting by locale, and fallback to default locale for missing translations. Support [number_of_languages] languages. Provide complete implementation code including configuration, translation files, and component examples.

variations.short: Implement i18n with [i18n_library]: translation files ([locale_structure]), locale detection, language switching, pluralization, date/number formatting, RTL support ([rtl_languages]), lazy loading. Support [target_languages].
variations.detailed: i18n implementation: [i18n_library] setup, translation structure ([locale_structure]), string extraction, locale detection (browser/URL), language switcher, pluralization, date formatting ([date_library]), number/currency formatting, RTL ([rtl_languages]), lazy loading. [number_of_languages] languages.
variations.strict: Production i18n: react-i18next with i18next, JSON translation files (namespaces), i18next-scanner extraction, browser locale detection + localStorage, language switcher, pluralization (i18next-plural), date-fns formatting, Intl.NumberFormat, RTL (dir='rtl'), code splitting (loadNamespaces). Full code.

tips: Extract all user-facing strings. Use translation keys, not hardcoded text. Support pluralization properly. Format dates/numbers per locale. Test RTL layouts. Lazy load translations for performance. Use professional translators for quality.

title: Payment Integration Builder
primary_use_case: Integrate [payment_provider] payment processing into [application_type]
prompt_text: Integrate [payment_provider] ([provider_options]: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree) payment processing into [application_type] for processing [payment_types] payments. The integration should include: (1) Payment provider SDK setup and configuration with API keys management (secret keys in environment variables, publishable keys for frontend), (2) Payment intent creation for one-time payments with amount, currency ([supported_currencies]), and payment method collection, (3) Payment method handling including credit/debit cards, digital wallets ([wallet_options]: Apple Pay, Google Pay), and saved payment methods with PCI compliance considerations, (4) Subscription management for recurring payments with plan creation, subscription creation, modification, cancellation, and prorating, (5) Payment processing flow with 3D Secure (3DS) authentication for card payments and handling authentication challenges, (6) Webhook integration for payment events ([webhook_events]: payment.succeeded, payment.failed, subscription.updated) with signature verification and idempotency handling, (7) Refund and dispute handling with partial/full refunds, refund status tracking, and dispute management, (8) Payment security with PCI DSS compliance, tokenization, and secure storage of payment data, (9) Error handling for declined payments, network errors, and provider errors with user-friendly error messages and retry logic, (10) Payment analytics and reporting with transaction logging, revenue tracking, and reconciliation. Support [payment_volume] transactions per day. Provide complete implementation code including API integration, webhook handlers, and frontend payment forms.

variations.short: Integrate [payment_provider] ([provider_options]): SDK setup, payment intents, payment methods ([wallet_options]), subscriptions, 3DS, webhooks ([webhook_events]), refunds, security (PCI), error handling, analytics. Handle [payment_types].
variations.detailed: Payment integration: [payment_provider] ([provider_options]) SDK, payment intents (one-time), payment methods (cards/[wallet_options]), subscriptions (create/modify/cancel), 3DS auth, webhooks ([webhook_events]) with verification, refunds/disputes, PCI compliance, error handling, analytics. [payment_volume] transactions/day, [supported_currencies].
variations.strict: Production Stripe integration: Stripe SDK (server + Elements), Payment Intents API, payment methods (cards/Apple Pay), Subscriptions API, 3DS2, webhook signature verification, refunds API, PCI compliance (no card storage), comprehensive error handling, transaction logging (PostgreSQL). Full code with tests.

tips: Never store card details directly. Use payment provider's secure forms. Verify webhook signatures. Handle 3DS authentication. Test with test cards. Implement idempotency. Log all transactions. Comply with PCI DSS. Handle refunds properly.

title: Serverless Function Builder (AWS Lambda/Cloud Functions)
primary_use_case: Build serverless functions using [serverless_platform] for [function_purpose]
prompt_text: Build serverless functions using [serverless_platform] ([platform_options]: AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, Azure Functions, Vercel Functions) for [function_purpose]. The implementation should include: (1) Function setup and configuration with runtime ([runtime]: Node.js, Python, Go), memory allocation ([memory_size] MB), timeout ([timeout] seconds), and environment variables, (2) Function handler implementation with proper event parsing, error handling, and response formatting following platform conventions, (3) API Gateway integration for HTTP endpoints with REST API configuration, CORS setup, request/response mapping, and authentication (API keys, IAM, Cognito), (4) Event source integrations for [event_sources]: S3 events, SQS messages, CloudWatch Events (scheduled), DynamoDB streams, with proper event parsing and error handling, (5) External service integrations with database connections ([database]: DynamoDB, RDS, MongoDB), API calls, and third-party services with connection pooling and timeout handling, (6) Environment configuration management using [config_method]: environment variables, AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, secrets management, with different configs for dev/staging/prod, (7) Logging and monitoring setup with CloudWatch Logs, X-Ray tracing, and custom metrics for function performance and errors, (8) Error handling and retry logic with dead letter queues (DLQ) for failed invocations and exponential backoff for retries, (9) Cold start optimization using provisioned concurrency, initialization outside handler, and minimal dependencies, (10) Deployment configuration with Infrastructure as Code ([iac_tool]: Serverless Framework, SAM, Terraform, CDK) including function definitions, IAM roles, and API Gateway setup. Handle [request_volume] requests per second. Provide complete function code, configuration files, and deployment scripts.

variations.short: Build serverless functions ([serverless_platform]/[platform_options]): handler ([runtime]), API Gateway, event sources ([event_sources]), DB integration ([database]), config ([config_method]), logging/monitoring, error handling/DLQ, cold start optimization, IaC ([iac_tool]).
variations.detailed: Serverless functions: [serverless_platform] ([platform_options]) setup ([runtime], [memory_size]MB, [timeout]s), handler implementation, API Gateway (REST/CORS/auth), event sources ([event_sources]), DB ([database]), config ([config_method]), CloudWatch/X-Ray, error handling/DLQ, optimization, deployment ([iac_tool]). Handle [request_volume] RPS.
variations.strict: Production AWS Lambda: Node.js 18 runtime, 512MB memory, 30s timeout, API Gateway REST API with CORS, S3/SQS/EventBridge triggers, DynamoDB with connection reuse, SSM Parameter Store config, CloudWatch Logs + X-Ray, DLQ (SQS), provisioned concurrency, Serverless Framework deployment. Full code + YAML.

tips: Keep functions small and focused. Minimize cold starts. Use environment variables for config. Implement proper error handling. Monitor function performance. Use dead letter queues. Optimize dependencies. Test locally before deploying.

title: Data Cleaning and Preprocessing Guide
primary_use_case: Clean and prepare raw datasets for analysis by identifying and handling missing values, outliers, duplicates, and data quality issues
user_role: Data Analyst, Data Scientist, Business Analyst
prompt_text: Analyze the provided dataset [dataset_name] and create a comprehensive data cleaning and preprocessing guide. Examine the dataset structure, data types, and identify key data quality issues including: missing values (nulls, NAs, empty strings), duplicate records, outliers using statistical methods (IQR, Z-score), inconsistent formatting (dates, currencies, categorical values), data type mismatches, and encoding issues. For each identified issue, provide specific recommendations including: imputation strategies for missing data (mean, median, mode, forward fill, or domain-specific methods), outlier treatment approaches (capping, removal, or transformation), deduplication methods, standardization techniques for categorical variables, and normalization/transformation needs for numerical features. Include code examples or step-by-step procedures for implementing each cleaning step. Specify which columns require special attention and why. Provide a data quality score before and after cleaning, and outline the expected impact of each cleaning step on downstream analysis. Consider the business context: [business_context] and ensure cleaning decisions align with analytical goals: [analysis_goals].

variations.short: Clean dataset [dataset_name]. Identify missing values, duplicates, outliers. Provide removal/imputation recommendations.
variations.detailed: Perform comprehensive data cleaning on [dataset_name]. Analyze data quality across all dimensions: completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, and timeliness. Create a detailed data profiling report showing distributions, missing value patterns, correlation analysis, and anomaly detection. Develop a step-by-step cleaning pipeline with validation checkpoints. Include data quality metrics (completeness %, accuracy score, consistency index) and document all transformations applied. Provide before/after comparisons and explain business rationale for each cleaning decision.
variations.strict: Execute rigorous data cleaning protocol for [dataset_name] following [industry_standard] standards. Apply statistical tests for normality, homogeneity of variance, and independence. Use [specific_methodology] for outlier detection. Document every transformation with justification. Create audit trail. Validate cleaned data against [validation_rules]. Generate compliance report.

tips: Always examine data distributions before deciding on imputation methods. Consider domain knowledge when handling outliers - some extreme values may be legitimate business cases. Preserve original data before applying transformations. Use data quality frameworks like DAMA-DMBOK for comprehensive assessment.

title: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
primary_use_case: Understand dataset characteristics, patterns, relationships, and distributions through comprehensive statistical and visual exploration
user_role: Data Scientist, Data Analyst, Research Analyst
output_type: EDA report with visualizations and statistical summaries
prompt_text: Conduct a comprehensive Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on the dataset [dataset_name] focusing on [analysis_objective]. Begin with univariate analysis: calculate descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis) for numerical variables, frequency distributions and mode for categorical variables, and identify data types and missing value patterns. Create appropriate visualizations including histograms, box plots, bar charts, and pie charts. Perform bivariate analysis: examine relationships between [key_variables] using correlation matrices, scatter plots, cross-tabulations, and grouped statistics. Identify potential interactions, collinearities, and interesting patterns. Conduct multivariate analysis where relevant, exploring complex relationships across multiple dimensions. Detect anomalies, outliers, and unusual patterns that warrant investigation. Summarize key findings including: data distribution characteristics, notable relationships or correlations, missing data patterns, potential data quality issues, and preliminary insights relevant to [business_question]. Provide recommendations for further analysis, feature engineering opportunities, and modeling approaches. Include code snippets or tool recommendations for creating visualizations and statistical tests.

variations.short: Run EDA on [dataset_name]. Show distributions, correlations, key patterns. Highlight insights for [objective].
variations.detailed: Execute comprehensive EDA for [dataset_name] using advanced techniques. Include statistical tests (normality, homogeneity), advanced visualizations (heatmaps, pair plots, violin plots), time-based analysis if applicable, geographic analysis if location data exists, and text analysis if text fields present. Perform feature importance analysis, interaction effects detection, and multi-dimensional pattern recognition. Create interactive dashboards. Generate automated insights using statistical significance testing. Document all findings with business context and actionable recommendations.
variations.strict: Perform EDA following [statistical_framework] methodology. Use [specific_tools] for analysis. Apply [hypothesis_testing_method] for pattern validation. Document all assumptions. Create reproducible analysis pipeline. Validate findings with [validation_criteria]. Generate publication-ready visualizations per [style_guide].

tips: Start with high-level overview before diving deep. Use appropriate visualizations for data types (continuous vs categorical). Look for both expected and unexpected patterns. Document assumptions and limitations. EDA is iterative - refine based on initial findings.

title: Statistical Hypothesis Testing
primary_use_case: Test statistical hypotheses to make data-driven decisions and validate assumptions using appropriate statistical tests
output_type: Hypothesis test results with statistical interpretation
prompt_text: Design and execute appropriate statistical hypothesis tests for the research question: [research_question]. Define the null hypothesis (H0) and alternative hypothesis (H1) clearly. Specify the significance level (alpha = [alpha_level], typically 0.05) and determine the appropriate test based on: data type (continuous vs categorical), number of groups being compared, sample size, distribution assumptions (normal vs non-normal), and whether samples are independent or paired. Select from tests including: t-tests (one-sample, independent, paired), ANOVA, chi-square tests, Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Kruskal-Wallis, or other non-parametric alternatives. Check test assumptions including normality (Shapiro-Wilk or Kolmogorov-Smirnov), homogeneity of variance (Levene's test), independence, and sample size requirements. Execute the test and report: test statistic value, degrees of freedom, p-value, confidence intervals, and effect size (Cohen's d, Cramér's V, or eta-squared). Interpret results in the context of [business_context], explaining what the findings mean practically. Provide recommendations for action based on statistical evidence. If assumptions are violated, suggest alternative approaches or transformations.

variations.short: Test hypothesis: [hypothesis]. Use [test_type]. Report p-value, interpret results for [context].
variations.detailed: Conduct comprehensive hypothesis testing framework for [research_question]. Perform assumption checking with multiple tests. Calculate effect sizes and power analysis. Run multiple comparison corrections if needed (Bonferroni, FDR). Provide Bayesian analysis alternative. Create visualizations (Q-Q plots, residual plots). Perform sensitivity analysis. Document all assumptions, limitations, and potential confounding factors. Provide practical significance interpretation alongside statistical significance.
variations.strict: Execute hypothesis test per [statistical_standard] (e.g., APA, ISO). Use [specific_software/methodology]. Pre-register analysis plan. Report all test statistics, effect sizes, confidence intervals per [reporting_guidelines]. Validate assumptions with [validation_tests]. Include power analysis. Document reproducibility steps.

tips: Always check test assumptions before interpreting results. Effect size is as important as p-value - statistical significance doesn't always mean practical significance. Consider multiple testing corrections when running multiple comparisons. Document all decisions transparently.

title: A/B Test Analysis
primary_use_case: Analyze A/B test results to determine statistical significance and business impact of experimental changes
user_role: Product Analyst, Data Scientist, Growth Analyst, Marketing Analyst
output_type: A/B test analysis report with statistical results and recommendations
prompt_text: Analyze the A/B test results for experiment [experiment_name] comparing variant A (control: [control_description]) and variant B (treatment: [treatment_description]). The primary metric is [primary_metric] with current values: Control group [control_value] (n=[control_sample_size]) and Treatment group [treatment_value] (n=[treatment_sample_size]). Calculate key statistics including: conversion rates for each variant, absolute and relative lift, statistical significance using appropriate test (chi-square for conversion rates, t-test for continuous metrics, or Mann-Whitney for non-parametric), confidence intervals, and minimum detectable effect. Check test validity: verify randomization was proper, sample sizes are adequate (power analysis), test duration was sufficient, and no external factors contaminated results. Analyze secondary metrics: [secondary_metrics] to understand broader impact. Segment results by [segmentation_variables] if applicable to identify heterogeneous effects. Calculate practical significance: expected business impact in terms of [business_kpi] (e.g., revenue, users, engagement). Provide clear recommendation: implement variant B, keep control, or run test longer, with justification. Include risk assessment and rollout strategy if recommending implementation. Address any concerns about statistical power, effect size, or test design issues.

variations.short: Analyze A/B test: Control [control_metric] vs Treatment [treatment_metric]. Calculate lift, p-value. Recommend action.
variations.detailed: Perform comprehensive A/B test analysis including: pre-test power analysis validation, multiple comparison corrections if multiple variants, Bayesian analysis for probability of success, confidence intervals for lift, segment-level analysis, time-series analysis of test results, novelty effect detection, and long-term impact estimation. Analyze all secondary metrics, user behavior changes, and potential negative impacts. Create visualizations showing distributions, confidence intervals, and trends. Provide detailed rollout plan with risk mitigation strategies.
variations.strict: Execute A/B test analysis per [company_standard] methodology. Use [specific_statistical_framework]. Validate randomization with [validation_tests]. Report per [reporting_template]. Include pre-registered analysis plan. Document all assumptions. Calculate required sample size post-hoc. Provide statistical and practical significance interpretation.

tips: Ensure adequate sample size before concluding. Check for novelty effects - early results may not persist. Analyze segments to find where effect is strongest. Consider long-term impact beyond immediate metrics. Document any test design issues for future improvements.

title: Dashboard Design Recommendations
primary_use_case: Design effective data dashboards that communicate key metrics and insights clearly to stakeholders
user_role: Business Intelligence Analyst, Data Analyst, Product Manager
output_type: Dashboard design specification with layout and visualization recommendations
prompt_text: Design a comprehensive dashboard for [dashboard_purpose] targeting [audience_type] users. Identify the key metrics and KPIs that should be prominently displayed based on [business_objectives]. Organize the dashboard layout following best practices: place most critical metrics in the top-left (primary focus area), use consistent color schemes and visual hierarchy, group related metrics together, and ensure responsive design for [device_types]. Recommend appropriate visualization types for each metric: line charts for trends over time, bar charts for comparisons, gauges or big numbers for KPIs, heatmaps for correlation or geographic data, tables for detailed data, and pie/donut charts sparingly for composition. Specify color coding: use [color_scheme] with semantic colors (red for alerts/warnings, green for positive, neutral for informational). Include interactive elements: filters for [filter_dimensions], drill-down capabilities, time range selectors, and export functionality. Define refresh frequency: [refresh_frequency] based on data update cadence. Consider user workflow: [user_workflow] and ensure dashboard supports key decisions. Provide recommendations for mobile optimization, accessibility (WCAG compliance), and performance optimization. Include sample layout mockup description and tool recommendations (Tableau, Power BI, Looker, custom).

variations.short: Design dashboard for [purpose] showing [key_metrics]. Recommend layout, charts, filters for [audience].
variations.detailed: Create comprehensive dashboard design specification including: user persona analysis, information architecture, wireframe mockups, detailed visualization specifications with exact chart types and configurations, color palette with hex codes, typography guidelines, interaction design patterns, responsive breakpoints, accessibility requirements (WCAG 2.1 AA), performance benchmarks, data refresh strategies, alert/threshold configurations, and user testing recommendations. Include multiple dashboard variants for different user roles and use cases.
variations.strict: Design dashboard per [design_system] standards. Follow [accessibility_guidelines]. Use [specific_tool] with [configuration]. Implement [security_protocols]. Validate against [usability_criteria]. Document all design decisions and rationale.

tips: Keep dashboards focused - less is more. Use consistent visual language across all charts. Ensure mobile responsiveness. Test with actual users before finalizing. Consider loading performance - limit data points and use efficient queries. Use progressive disclosure for detailed data.

title: KPI Definition and Metrics Framework
primary_use_case: Define and structure Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and metrics framework aligned with business objectives
user_role: Business Analyst, Strategy Manager, Operations Manager, Executive
output_type: KPI framework document with definitions, targets, and measurement approach
prompt_text: Develop a comprehensive KPI and metrics framework for [business_unit/function] aligned with strategic objectives: [strategic_objectives]. Define KPIs following the SMART framework (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound). For each KPI, specify: name and description, business rationale and alignment to [strategic_goals], calculation formula with data sources, target value and acceptable range, measurement frequency (daily, weekly, monthly), owner and stakeholders, leading vs lagging indicator classification, and baseline current performance. Organize KPIs hierarchically: strategic KPIs (executive level), operational KPIs (department level), and tactical metrics (team/individual level). Categorize by business area: [business_areas] such as revenue, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, product performance, or employee engagement. Define relationships between KPIs showing how operational metrics influence strategic ones. Establish data collection processes: identify data sources [data_sources], define data quality requirements, specify calculation methodology, and set up reporting cadence. Include governance: review frequency, accountability structure, and update procedures. Provide examples of good vs bad KPI definitions. Consider industry benchmarks and competitive positioning. Create a measurement plan with timelines and resource requirements.

variations.short: Define KPIs for [business_area] aligned with [objectives]. Include formula, targets, measurement approach.
variations.detailed: Create comprehensive KPI framework including: balanced scorecard approach, OKR integration, KPI tree mapping showing causal relationships, industry benchmarking data, predictive leading indicators, risk-adjusted metrics, composite index development, and automated calculation specifications. Include data dictionary, calculation validation rules, exception handling procedures, and change management plan. Develop KPI dashboard mockups and reporting templates. Provide training materials and governance framework.
variations.strict: Develop KPI framework per [industry_standard] (e.g., ISO, COSO). Align with [regulatory_requirements]. Use [specific_methodology] (e.g., Balanced Scorecard, OKR). Document per [documentation_standard]. Include audit trail requirements. Validate calculations with [validation_process].

tips: Focus on actionable KPIs that drive decisions, not just measurement. Ensure data availability before committing to KPIs. Balance leading and lagging indicators. Review and update KPIs regularly as business evolves. Avoid vanity metrics that don't impact outcomes.

title: Customer Segmentation Analysis
primary_use_case: Segment customers into distinct groups based on behavior, demographics, or value to enable targeted strategies
user_role: Marketing Analyst, Data Scientist, Product Manager, CRM Manager
industry: Retail, E-commerce, SaaS, Financial Services, Telecommunications
output_type: Segmentation analysis with segment profiles and recommendations
prompt_text: Perform customer segmentation analysis on [customer_dataset] using [segmentation_variables] such as demographics, purchase behavior, engagement metrics, product usage, or value indicators. Apply appropriate segmentation methodology: RFM analysis (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) for transactional data, K-means clustering for behavioral patterns, hierarchical clustering for interpretability, or rule-based segmentation for business logic. Determine optimal number of segments using elbow method, silhouette score, or business requirements: [target_segment_count]. For each identified segment, create detailed profiles including: segment size and percentage of total customer base, demographic characteristics (age, location, [demographic_variables]), behavioral patterns (purchase frequency, product preferences, channel usage, engagement level), value metrics (average revenue, lifetime value, profitability), and psychographic traits if available. Analyze segment differences using statistical tests to validate distinctiveness. Calculate segment-specific metrics: acquisition cost, retention rate, churn probability, and growth potential. Provide actionable recommendations for each segment: marketing messaging, product recommendations, pricing strategies, channel preferences, and engagement tactics. Identify high-value segments for prioritization and at-risk segments requiring intervention. Include visualization of segments using 2D/3D plots, and create segment personas for stakeholder communication.

variations.short: Segment customers from [dataset] using [variables]. Identify [N] segments. Profile each segment with characteristics and recommendations.
variations.detailed: Execute advanced customer segmentation including: multi-dimensional clustering with feature engineering, dynamic segmentation that updates over time, predictive segmentation using ML models, segment stability analysis, micro-segmentation for hyper-personalization, and segment evolution tracking. Include advanced analytics: segment profitability analysis, cross-segment migration patterns, segment-specific predictive models, and A/B testing framework for segment strategies. Create comprehensive segment playbooks with detailed personas, journey maps, and engagement strategies.
variations.strict: Perform segmentation per [methodology] (e.g., RFM, CLV-based). Use [statistical_validation] for segment quality. Validate with [validation_dataset]. Document all assumptions. Ensure segments are actionable and measurable. Comply with [privacy_regulations] for customer data usage.

tips: Start with business objectives to guide segmentation approach. Ensure segments are actionable - distinct enough to warrant different strategies. Validate segments with business stakeholders. Consider dynamic segmentation as customer behavior evolves. Balance granularity with practicality - too many segments become unmanageable.

title: Churn Prediction Analysis
primary_use_case: Predict which customers are likely to churn and identify factors driving churn to enable proactive retention
user_role: Data Scientist, Customer Success Manager, Retention Analyst
output_type: Churn prediction model with risk scores and retention recommendations
prompt_text: Build a churn prediction analysis for [customer_base] using historical data from [time_period]. Define churn based on [churn_definition] (e.g., no activity for X days, cancellation, non-renewal). Prepare features including: engagement metrics (login frequency, feature usage, session duration), transaction history (purchase frequency, recency, value), support interactions (ticket volume, resolution time, satisfaction), product usage patterns (feature adoption, usage trends), and demographic/firmographic data. Apply machine learning models: logistic regression for interpretability, random forest for feature importance, gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM) for accuracy, or neural networks for complex patterns. Train models using [training_period] and validate on [validation_period]. Evaluate model performance using metrics: AUC-ROC, precision, recall, F1-score, and calibration. Identify top churn drivers through feature importance analysis and SHAP values. Generate churn risk scores for each customer (0-100 scale) and segment into risk tiers: high-risk (score > [threshold_high]), medium-risk ([threshold_medium]-[threshold_high]), and low-risk (< [threshold_medium]). For high-risk customers, provide specific intervention recommendations: personalized offers, feature training, proactive support outreach, or win-back campaigns. Calculate expected impact: potential revenue saved, intervention cost, and ROI. Include model monitoring plan for ongoing prediction accuracy.

variations.short: Predict churn for [customer_base]. Use [features]. Identify high-risk customers and recommend retention actions.
