variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive churn prediction system including: multiple model ensemble, time-series features capturing behavior trends, early warning indicators (leading churn signals), segment-specific models, and real-time scoring pipeline. Include advanced analytics: churn reason analysis, competitive churn factors, seasonal patterns, and cohort-based churn rates. Create intervention playbooks with cost-benefit analysis, A/B testing framework for retention tactics, and success measurement framework. Implement model explainability and fairness analysis.
variations.strict: Build churn model per [ML_standards]. Use [specific_algorithm] with [validation_methodology]. Validate with [holdout_period]. Document all features and transformations. Ensure model interpretability per [regulatory_requirements]. Include bias testing and fairness metrics.

tips: Define churn clearly and consistently. Include both behavioral and transactional features. Focus on leading indicators that appear before churn happens. Validate model on recent data as patterns change. Balance precision and recall based on intervention costs. Monitor model performance over time.

title: Revenue Forecasting
primary_use_case: Forecast future revenue using historical data and business drivers to support planning and decision-making
user_role: Financial Analyst, FP&A Analyst, Business Analyst, Executive
output_type: Revenue forecast with confidence intervals and scenario analysis
prompt_text: Create a revenue forecast for [business_unit/product] covering [forecast_horizon] (e.g., next quarter, year) using historical revenue data from [historical_period]. Analyze historical trends: calculate growth rates, identify seasonality patterns, detect cyclical trends, and assess volatility. Consider business drivers: [business_drivers] such as customer acquisition, pricing changes, product launches, market conditions, competitive factors, and economic indicators. Apply forecasting methods: time series analysis (ARIMA, exponential smoothing), regression models with driver variables, machine learning approaches (prophet, LSTM), or bottom-up approaches (customer-level forecasting aggregated). For each method, evaluate accuracy using metrics: MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error), RMSE, and forecast bias. Select best-performing approach or ensemble methods. Generate point forecasts with confidence intervals (80% and 95%) and create scenarios: base case (most likely), optimistic (best case), and pessimistic (worst case) based on [scenario_assumptions]. Break down forecast by: [breakdown_dimensions] such as product lines, customer segments, geographic regions, or sales channels. Include sensitivity analysis showing impact of key assumptions. Provide recommendations for achieving forecast targets: required actions, resource needs, and risk mitigation strategies. Document assumptions, limitations, and update frequency.

variations.short: Forecast revenue for [period] using [historical_data]. Include trends, seasonality, confidence intervals, and scenarios.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive revenue forecasting framework including: multiple forecasting models with ensemble approach, driver-based modeling with econometric factors, customer cohort analysis, new vs existing customer revenue decomposition, churn impact modeling, pricing elasticity analysis, and market share projections. Include advanced analytics: Monte Carlo simulation for uncertainty quantification, scenario planning with multiple variables, real-time forecast updates, and accuracy tracking with forecast error analysis. Create interactive forecast dashboard with drill-down capabilities and sensitivity analysis tools.
variations.strict: Generate forecast per [accounting_standards] (e.g., GAAP, IFRS). Use [specific_methodology] validated by [validation_process]. Document all assumptions per [documentation_requirements]. Include audit trail. Validate against [benchmarks]. Report confidence intervals per [statistical_standards].

tips: Use multiple forecasting methods and compare accuracy. Include business context and drivers, not just historical trends. Account for known future events (product launches, market changes). Update forecasts regularly as new data arrives. Clearly communicate uncertainty through confidence intervals and scenarios.

title: Competitive Landscape Analysis
primary_use_case: Analyze competitive positioning, market share, and competitive dynamics to inform strategy
user_role: Strategy Analyst, Product Manager, Market Researcher, Business Development
output_type: Competitive analysis report with positioning matrix and strategic recommendations
prompt_text: Conduct a competitive landscape analysis for [company/product] in the [market/industry] space. Identify key competitors: direct competitors ([direct_competitors]), indirect competitors ([indirect_competitors]), and potential disruptors. For each competitor, analyze: market position and share, product/service offerings and features, pricing strategy and value proposition, target customer segments, go-to-market approach, strengths and competitive advantages, weaknesses and gaps, financial performance (revenue, growth, profitability if available), and recent strategic moves (funding, acquisitions, partnerships, product launches). Create competitive positioning matrix using dimensions: [positioning_dimensions] such as price vs quality, innovation vs reliability, or market coverage. Analyze competitive dynamics: market concentration (HHI index), barriers to entry, threat of substitutes, and competitive intensity. Identify market gaps and opportunities where [company] can differentiate. Assess competitive threats: emerging technologies, new entrants, changing customer preferences, or regulatory changes. Benchmark [company] against competitors across key dimensions: [benchmark_dimensions]. Provide strategic recommendations: positioning strategy, differentiation opportunities, competitive response tactics, and areas to avoid direct competition. Include data sources used and confidence levels for information.

variations.short: Analyze competitive landscape for [company] in [market]. Profile key competitors, create positioning matrix, identify opportunities.
variations.detailed: Perform comprehensive competitive intelligence including: detailed competitor profiles with financial analysis, feature comparison matrix, pricing analysis with elasticity modeling, customer sentiment analysis (reviews, social media), competitive product teardowns, patent and IP analysis, talent movement tracking, and competitive response simulation. Create dynamic competitive dashboard with real-time updates. Include scenario planning for competitive moves and counter-strategies.
variations.strict: Conduct analysis per [industry_research_standards]. Use [specific_frameworks] (e.g., Porter's Five Forces, SWOT). Validate all data sources. Document methodology per [documentation_requirements]. Ensure compliance with [competitive_intelligence_ethics] guidelines.

tips: Focus on actionable insights, not just data collection. Update analysis regularly as competitive landscape changes. Consider both direct and indirect competitors. Look for patterns in competitor behavior to predict future moves. Validate findings with customer and market research.

title: Market Sizing (TAM/SAM/SOM)
primary_use_case: Estimate Total Addressable Market (TAM), Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM), and Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM) for market opportunity assessment
user_role: Business Development, Strategy Analyst, Investment Analyst, Entrepreneur
output_type: Market sizing analysis with TAM/SAM/SOM calculations and methodology
prompt_text: Calculate market sizing for [product/service] in [target_market] using TAM/SAM/SOM framework. Define Total Addressable Market (TAM): the total market demand for [product_category] globally or in [geographic_scope]. Use top-down approach: identify total market size from industry reports, government data, or market research (cite sources: [data_sources]), then apply relevant filters. Alternatively, use bottom-up approach: estimate number of potential customers [customer_count] × average revenue per customer [ARPU] × penetration rate [penetration_rate]. Calculate Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM): the portion of TAM that [company] can realistically serve given [constraints] such as geographic focus, customer segments targeted, product capabilities, and regulatory limitations. Apply filters: [SAM_filters] to narrow from TAM. Calculate Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM): the realistic market share [company] can capture in [timeframe] (typically 1-5 years) based on competitive positioning, go-to-market capacity, and market penetration assumptions. Use market share assumptions: [market_share_assumptions] considering competitive landscape, brand strength, and execution capability. Present results with methodology transparency: show all assumptions, data sources, calculation steps, and confidence levels. Include sensitivity analysis: how results change with different assumptions. Break down by segments: [market_segments] if relevant. Provide context: growth rates, market trends, and factors affecting market size over time. Compare to similar companies or benchmarks if available.

variations.short: Calculate TAM/SAM/SOM for [product] in [market]. Show methodology, assumptions, and results.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive market sizing analysis including: multiple sizing methodologies (top-down, bottom-up, value-theory), segment-level breakdowns, geographic analysis, time-series projections with growth rates, competitive market share analysis, penetration rate modeling, and scenario analysis (conservative, base, optimistic). Include detailed assumptions documentation, data source validation, triangulation across multiple sources, and confidence intervals. Create market sizing model with adjustable parameters for sensitivity analysis.
variations.strict: Calculate market size per [industry_standard] methodology (e.g., Gartner, McKinsey framework). Use [validated_data_sources]. Document all assumptions per [documentation_requirements]. Validate calculations with [validation_method]. Include audit trail. Report per [presentation_standard].

tips: Use multiple methodologies and triangulate results. Be conservative with assumptions - investors prefer realistic over optimistic. Clearly document all assumptions and data sources. Consider market growth trends, not just current size. Validate with industry experts or customer research when possible.

title: SWOT Analysis Generator
primary_use_case: Generate comprehensive SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis for strategic planning
user_role: Strategy Manager, Business Analyst, Executive, Consultant
output_type: SWOT analysis matrix with strategic recommendations
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive SWOT analysis for [company/product/business_unit] in the context of [business_context] and [strategic_objective]. Analyze Strengths: internal positive attributes and capabilities that provide competitive advantage, including: core competencies, unique resources, brand strength, market position, financial resources, talented team, proprietary technology, customer relationships, and operational efficiencies. Analyze Weaknesses: internal limitations and areas for improvement, including: resource constraints, skill gaps, operational inefficiencies, financial limitations, technology debt, market position challenges, and organizational issues. Analyze Opportunities: external factors that could be leveraged for growth, including: market trends, emerging technologies, regulatory changes, competitor weaknesses, customer needs, partnership possibilities, market expansion, and industry shifts. Analyze Threats: external challenges that could harm the business, including: competitive pressure, market changes, regulatory risks, economic conditions, technology disruption, supply chain risks, and changing customer preferences. For each category, prioritize items by importance and impact. Identify strategic implications: how strengths can be leveraged, how weaknesses can be addressed, how opportunities can be captured, and how threats can be mitigated. Create action items linking SWOT elements: SO strategies (strengths-opportunities), WO strategies (weaknesses-opportunities), ST strategies (strengths-threats), and WT strategies (weaknesses-threats). Provide timeline and resource requirements for key actions.

variations.short: Create SWOT analysis for [entity]. List top strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats. Provide strategic recommendations.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive SWOT analysis including: quantitative assessment of each factor (impact × probability), stakeholder perspectives (internal vs external view), time-based analysis (current vs future), competitive benchmarking within SWOT framework, and detailed action plans with owners, timelines, and success metrics. Include risk assessment for threats, opportunity prioritization matrix, and resource allocation recommendations. Create visual SWOT matrix with strategic initiatives mapped.
variations.strict: Generate SWOT per [strategic_framework] methodology. Use [specific_templates]. Validate with [stakeholder_group]. Document per [documentation_standard]. Include [required_elements]. Ensure alignment with [strategic_planning_process].

tips: Be honest and objective - weaknesses and threats are as important as strengths. Focus on actionable insights, not just listing items. Consider both internal and external perspectives. Update SWOT regularly as business environment changes. Link SWOT elements to create strategic initiatives.

title: Sentiment Analysis Framework
primary_use_case: Analyze sentiment from text data (reviews, social media, feedback) to understand customer opinions and emotions
user_role: Data Scientist, Marketing Analyst, Customer Success Manager, Product Manager
industry: Retail, SaaS, Hospitality, Consumer Goods, Media
output_type: Sentiment analysis results with scores, themes, and insights
prompt_text: Perform sentiment analysis on [text_data_source] containing [data_description] (e.g., customer reviews, social media posts, support tickets, survey responses) from [time_period]. Preprocess text data: remove noise, handle special characters, normalize text, and tokenize. Apply sentiment classification: use rule-based approaches (lexicon-based with VADER, TextBlob), machine learning models (Naive Bayes, SVM, logistic regression), or advanced NLP models (BERT, RoBERTa, GPT-based sentiment analysis). Classify sentiment into categories: positive, negative, neutral, or fine-grained (very positive, positive, neutral, negative, very negative). Calculate sentiment scores: polarity scores (-1 to +1) and confidence levels. Analyze sentiment distribution: overall sentiment breakdown, trends over time, sentiment by [segmentation_variables] such as product, customer segment, channel, or topic. Extract key themes and topics using topic modeling (LDA, NMF) or keyword extraction, and analyze sentiment within each theme. Identify drivers of negative sentiment: common complaints, pain points, and issues mentioned. Identify drivers of positive sentiment: what customers love, key differentiators. Perform aspect-based sentiment analysis: analyze sentiment for specific aspects like [product_aspects] (e.g., price, quality, service, features). Generate insights: sentiment trends, improvement opportunities, competitive comparisons if applicable, and actionable recommendations. Create visualizations: sentiment distribution charts, trend lines, word clouds, and heatmaps by topic/aspect.

variations.short: Analyze sentiment of [text_data]. Classify positive/negative/neutral. Identify key themes and insights.
variations.detailed: Execute advanced sentiment analysis including: emotion detection (joy, anger, fear, etc.), sarcasm detection, multilingual sentiment analysis, real-time streaming analysis, aspect-level sentiment with entity extraction, competitor sentiment comparison, influencer sentiment analysis, and predictive sentiment modeling. Include advanced NLP: transformer models fine-tuned on domain data, contextual sentiment understanding, and multi-modal sentiment (text + images). Create comprehensive dashboard with drill-down capabilities and alerting for sentiment shifts.
variations.strict: Perform sentiment analysis per [NLP_standards]. Use [validated_models] with [accuracy_thresholds]. Validate with [ground_truth_dataset]. Document preprocessing steps. Ensure reproducibility. Comply with [data_privacy_regulations] for text data processing.

tips: Consider context and domain-specific language. Sarcasm and irony can be challenging - use advanced models when needed. Combine multiple approaches for better accuracy. Validate results with human review sample. Track sentiment over time to identify trends and measure impact of changes.

title: Survey Data Analyzer
primary_use_case: Analyze survey responses to extract insights, patterns, and actionable findings from structured and unstructured data
user_role: Research Analyst, Data Analyst, UX Researcher, HR Analyst
output_type: Survey analysis report with statistical summaries and insights
prompt_text: Analyze survey data from [survey_name] with [response_count] responses collected from [target_population] during [collection_period]. Examine response quality: calculate response rate ([responses]/[invitations]), check for completion rates, identify partial responses, assess data quality (duplicates, invalid entries), and analyze response patterns for bias. For quantitative questions: calculate descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, standard deviation) for rating scales, frequency distributions and percentages for multiple choice, and cross-tabulations for relationships between [key_variables]. Perform statistical tests: chi-square for categorical relationships, t-tests or ANOVA for group comparisons, correlation analysis for continuous variables. For qualitative/open-ended questions: perform thematic analysis to identify common themes, code responses into categories, extract key quotes, and quantify themes where possible. Analyze response patterns: identify segments with different response patterns using [segmentation_variables], compare responses across [comparison_groups] (e.g., demographics, user types), and detect response biases or non-response patterns. Create visualizations: bar charts, pie charts, histograms, box plots, heatmaps for cross-tabs, and word clouds for open-ended responses. Generate insights: key findings, surprising patterns, areas of concern, opportunities, and actionable recommendations. Include confidence intervals and margin of error calculations. Address limitations: sample representativeness, potential biases, and generalizability.

variations.short: Analyze survey with [N] responses. Calculate statistics, identify themes in open-ends, provide key insights.
variations.detailed: Perform comprehensive survey analysis including: advanced statistical modeling (regression, factor analysis), text analytics for open-ended responses with sentiment analysis, response quality scoring, weighting for representativeness, longitudinal analysis if multiple waves, benchmark comparisons, and predictive modeling. Include advanced visualizations: interactive dashboards, Sankey diagrams for flow questions, network analysis for relationship questions. Create detailed findings report with executive summary, methodology, and appendices.
variations.strict: Analyze survey per [research_methodology] standards. Use [statistical_software] with [validation_procedures]. Ensure [sample_representativeness] criteria met. Document methodology per [reporting_standards]. Include margin of error calculations. Validate findings with [validation_method].

tips: Check response quality before analysis - low quality data leads to poor insights. Use appropriate statistical tests based on question types and data distribution. Don't over-interpret small sample sizes. Consider response bias and non-response patterns. Present findings clearly with visualizations for stakeholders.

title: Funnel Analysis and Optimization
primary_use_case: Analyze conversion funnels to identify drop-off points and optimize conversion rates at each stage
user_role: Product Analyst, Growth Analyst, Marketing Analyst, Sales Operations
output_type: Funnel analysis report with conversion rates and optimization recommendations
prompt_text: Analyze the [funnel_name] conversion funnel with stages: [funnel_stages] (e.g., Awareness → Interest → Consideration → Purchase → Retention). Calculate key metrics: conversion rate at each stage (users progressing to next stage / users at current stage), drop-off rate (users leaving at each stage), overall funnel conversion rate (end stage / initial stage), and time-to-convert between stages. Identify critical drop-off points: stages with highest percentage drop-off, absolute volume of users lost, and impact on final conversion. Analyze drop-off drivers: examine user behavior data, survey feedback, technical issues (errors, load times), friction points (form complexity, required information), and user characteristics of those who drop off vs convert. Segment analysis: compare funnel performance across [segmentation_variables] such as traffic source, device type, user segment, geographic region, or campaign. Calculate value metrics: revenue per stage, cost per acquisition at each stage, and ROI by stage. Perform cohort analysis: track conversion rates over time to identify trends. Benchmark against industry standards or historical performance. Provide optimization recommendations: quick wins (low effort, high impact), medium-term improvements, and strategic changes. Prioritize recommendations by potential impact (estimated conversion lift) and implementation effort. Include A/B testing suggestions for key hypotheses. Create visual funnel diagram showing conversion rates and drop-offs.

variations.short: Analyze [funnel] with stages [stages]. Calculate conversion rates, identify drop-offs, recommend optimizations.
variations.detailed: Execute comprehensive funnel analysis including: micro-conversion tracking, user path analysis (not just linear funnel), attribution modeling, predictive drop-off modeling, real-time funnel monitoring, multi-touchpoint analysis, and advanced segmentation with ML-based cohorts. Include optimization framework: experimentation roadmap, predictive impact modeling, and ROI calculations. Create interactive funnel dashboard with drill-down capabilities and automated alerting for funnel degradation.
variations.strict: Analyze funnel per [analytics_standards]. Use [specific_tool] with [configuration]. Validate data quality per [validation_rules]. Document methodology. Ensure statistical significance for recommendations. Report per [reporting_template].

tips: Look beyond overall conversion rate - stage-by-stage analysis reveals specific problems. Consider user paths, not just linear funnels. Test hypotheses with A/B tests before major changes. Monitor funnels continuously - they degrade over time. Focus on high-impact stages first.

title: Cohort Analysis Builder
primary_use_case: Analyze user behavior and retention patterns by grouping users into cohorts based on acquisition time or characteristics
user_role: Data Analyst, Product Analyst, Growth Analyst
industry: SaaS, E-commerce, Mobile Apps, Subscription Services
output_type: Cohort analysis tables and visualizations with retention curves
prompt_text: Build a cohort analysis for [user_base] grouping users by [cohort_definition] (e.g., signup month, acquisition channel, first purchase date, or user segment). Define cohort periods: [cohort_period] (weekly, monthly, quarterly). For each cohort, track metrics over time: retention rate (users active in period N / cohort size), retention curve showing how retention changes over time periods, cumulative metrics (total revenue, total sessions) per cohort, and average metrics per user (ARPU, sessions per user) by period. Create cohort retention table: rows = cohorts, columns = time periods since cohort start, cells = retention rate or metric value. Identify patterns: which cohorts perform best/worst, trends in cohort quality over time, impact of [cohort_variables] on retention, and seasonality effects. Calculate cohort-specific metrics: lifetime value (LTV) by cohort, payback period, and retention decay rate. Compare cohorts: statistical tests to identify significant differences, benchmark against best-performing cohort, and analyze what makes successful cohorts different. Perform survival analysis: time-to-churn or time-to-first-value by cohort. Provide insights: factors driving cohort differences, recommendations for improving future cohorts, and predictions for current cohorts' future performance. Create visualizations: retention heatmap, retention curves by cohort, and cohort comparison charts.

variations.short: Create cohort analysis grouping by [cohort_var]. Track retention, LTV, and key metrics over time. Compare cohorts.
variations.detailed: Develop advanced cohort analysis including: multi-dimensional cohorting (time + segment), behavioral cohorting (first action), predictive cohort modeling, cohort migration analysis, and cohort-based forecasting. Include advanced metrics: cohort-based unit economics, cohort contribution margin, and cohort-based growth accounting. Create interactive cohort dashboard with filtering, drill-down, and export capabilities. Include automated insights and anomaly detection.
variations.strict: Build cohort analysis per [analytics_methodology]. Use [specific_definition] for cohort assignment. Validate data per [validation_rules]. Document all calculations. Ensure cohorts are comparable. Report per [standard_format].

tips: Choose cohort definition based on business question - time-based for retention, behavior-based for adoption. Ensure cohorts are large enough for statistical significance. Account for seasonality when comparing cohorts. Look for both absolute performance and trends. Use cohort analysis to inform acquisition and product strategies.

title: Unit Economics Calculator
primary_use_case: Calculate and analyze unit economics (CAC, LTV, payback period) to assess business model viability and profitability
user_role: Financial Analyst, Business Analyst, Founder, Investor
output_type: Unit economics report with calculations and benchmarks
prompt_text: Calculate unit economics for [business_model] using data from [time_period]. Define the unit: [unit_definition] (e.g., customer, transaction, subscription). Calculate Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): total sales and marketing spend [total_S&M_spend] / number of new customers acquired [new_customers] in period. Break down CAC by channel: [acquisition_channels] to identify most efficient channels. Calculate Customer Lifetime Value (LTV): average revenue per customer per period [ARPU] × gross margin % [gross_margin] × average customer lifetime [lifetime_months] months. Alternatively, use cohort-based LTV from historical data. Calculate key ratios: LTV:CAC ratio (target: >3:1), payback period (CAC / (ARPU × gross margin)), and contribution margin per customer. Analyze by segment: calculate unit economics for [customer_segments] to identify most profitable segments. Include variable costs: cost of goods sold (COGS), variable service costs, payment processing fees, and other per-unit costs. Calculate contribution margin: revenue per unit - variable costs per unit. Assess profitability: contribution margin should exceed CAC within payback period. Benchmark against industry standards: [industry_benchmarks]. Perform sensitivity analysis: how unit economics change with different assumptions (pricing, retention, acquisition cost). Identify improvement opportunities: reduce CAC through channel optimization, increase LTV through upsells/retention, or improve margins. Provide recommendations with expected impact on unit economics.

variations.short: Calculate unit economics: CAC, LTV, payback period for [business]. Analyze by segment, provide benchmarks and recommendations.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive unit economics framework including: cohort-based LTV calculation, predictive LTV modeling, multi-product unit economics, geographic unit economics, channel-level profitability analysis, and time-series tracking. Include advanced metrics: blended vs paid CAC, LTV:CAC by cohort, payback period distributions, and unit economics under different scenarios. Create financial model with unit economics as foundation for growth projections.
variations.strict: Calculate unit economics per [accounting_standards]. Use [specific_methodology] validated by [validation_process]. Document all assumptions per [documentation_requirements]. Include audit trail. Validate calculations with [validation_method]. Report per [financial_reporting_standards].

tips: Use consistent time periods for CAC and LTV calculations. Include all acquisition costs in CAC (not just ad spend). Use cohort data for accurate LTV when available. Segment analysis reveals which customers are profitable. Monitor unit economics over time as they change with scale and optimization.

title: Pricing Strategy Analysis
primary_use_case: Analyze pricing strategies, elasticity, and optimization opportunities to maximize revenue and profitability
user_role: Pricing Analyst, Product Manager, Revenue Manager, Business Analyst
output_type: Pricing analysis with elasticity estimates and optimization recommendations
prompt_text: Analyze pricing strategy for [product/service] in [market_context]. Examine current pricing: list prices for [pricing_tiers], actual transaction prices (accounting for discounts), pricing by [segmentation_variables] (customer segment, channel, geography), and pricing trends over [time_period]. Compare to competitors: benchmark against [competitor_pricing] to assess positioning (premium, parity, value). Calculate price elasticity: analyze historical data for price-demand relationships, estimate elasticity coefficient (percentage change in demand / percentage change in price), segment elasticity by [customer_segments], and identify price-sensitive vs price-insensitive segments. Analyze pricing impact: revenue impact of price changes, volume impact, and profit impact considering margins. Evaluate pricing models: assess current model ([current_model] - e.g., subscription, usage-based, freemium) against alternatives, analyze conversion rates across pricing tiers, and identify optimal price points using techniques like Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter or conjoint analysis if data available. Perform what-if analysis: model revenue/profit impact of different pricing scenarios (price increases, decreases, new tiers, bundling). Analyze customer value perception: survey data or behavioral indicators of price sensitivity, willingness to pay analysis, and value drivers that justify pricing. Provide recommendations: optimal pricing strategy, price point recommendations, pricing model improvements, discount strategy, and implementation plan. Include risk assessment: competitive response, customer churn risk, and market share impact.

variations.short: Analyze pricing for [product]. Compare to competitors, estimate elasticity, recommend optimal pricing strategy.
variations.detailed: Execute comprehensive pricing analysis including: advanced elasticity modeling with machine learning, dynamic pricing optimization, price discrimination strategies, bundling analysis, psychological pricing factors, A/B testing framework for pricing, and predictive revenue modeling. Include competitive intelligence: pricing monitoring, competitive response modeling, and market share impact analysis. Create pricing optimization model with scenario planning and sensitivity analysis.
variations.strict: Analyze pricing per [pricing_methodology] framework. Use [specific_analytical_tools]. Validate elasticity estimates with [validation_method]. Document all assumptions. Ensure compliance with [pricing_regulations]. Report per [standard_format].

tips: Price elasticity varies by segment - analyze separately. Consider both revenue and profit impact. Test pricing changes before full rollout. Monitor competitive response. Balance short-term revenue with long-term customer relationships. Consider value-based pricing, not just cost-plus.

title: Customer Lifetime Value Estimator
primary_use_case: Estimate Customer Lifetime Value (LTV/CLV) to understand long-term customer value and inform acquisition and retention strategies
user_role: Data Scientist, Marketing Analyst, Financial Analyst, Growth Analyst
output_type: LTV estimates with confidence intervals and segment breakdowns
prompt_text: Calculate Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) for [customer_base] using [calculation_method]. Historical method: analyze cohort data from [historical_period], calculate average revenue per customer per period [ARPU], estimate average customer lifetime [lifetime] based on retention/churn rates, and LTV = ARPU × lifetime × gross margin %. Predictive method: build survival analysis model to predict customer lifetime, use machine learning (regression, random forest) to predict future revenue, account for revenue trends (increasing/decreasing over time), and incorporate discount rate [discount_rate] for present value. Calculate LTV components: average order value (AOV), purchase frequency, customer lifespan (1 / churn rate), gross margin %, and retention rate. Segment LTV: calculate by [segmentation_variables] such as acquisition channel, customer segment, product tier, geographic region, or cohort. Analyze LTV drivers: identify factors that correlate with higher LTV (product usage, engagement, support interactions, etc.). Calculate confidence intervals: provide ranges for LTV estimates accounting for uncertainty in lifetime and revenue predictions. Benchmark against industry: compare to [industry_benchmarks]. Perform sensitivity analysis: how LTV changes with different assumptions (retention rates, revenue growth, margins). Provide actionable insights: which segments have highest LTV (focus acquisition), which have lowest (improve or deprioritize), and how to increase LTV (upsells, retention, pricing). Include LTV:CAC ratio analysis to assess unit economics health.

variations.short: Calculate LTV for [customers]. Use [method]. Segment by [variables]. Provide insights and recommendations.
variations.detailed: Develop advanced LTV modeling including: probabilistic LTV using survival analysis, machine learning models for predictive LTV, real-time LTV scoring, LTV decomposition (acquisition, expansion, retention components), and LTV optimization modeling. Include advanced analytics: LTV by customer journey stage, predictive churn impact on LTV, and LTV-based customer scoring. Create LTV dashboard with cohort tracking and predictive analytics.
variations.strict: Calculate LTV per [financial_modeling_standards]. Use [specific_methodology] validated by [validation_process]. Document all assumptions per [documentation_requirements]. Include statistical confidence intervals. Validate with [validation_dataset]. Report per [financial_reporting_standards].

tips: Use cohort data when available for most accurate LTV. Account for revenue trends - not all customers have constant ARPU. Consider discount rates for long-term businesses. Segment analysis reveals where to focus. Update LTV regularly as business evolves. Validate predictive models with holdout data.

title: Regression Analysis Interpreter
primary_use_case: Interpret regression analysis results to understand relationships between variables and make data-driven decisions
user_role: Data Scientist, Statistician, Research Analyst, Business Analyst
output_type: Regression interpretation report with coefficients, significance, and practical implications
prompt_text: Interpret regression analysis results for [regression_model] predicting [dependent_variable] using [independent_variables]. Examine model fit: R-squared (proportion of variance explained), adjusted R-squared (accounting for degrees of freedom), F-statistic and p-value (overall model significance), and residual analysis (check assumptions: normality, homoscedasticity, independence). Interpret coefficients: for each [independent_variable], explain the coefficient value, direction (positive/negative relationship), statistical significance (p-value, confidence intervals), and practical significance (effect size). For continuous variables: coefficient represents change in [dependent_variable] for one-unit increase in [independent_variable], holding others constant. For categorical variables: coefficient represents difference from reference category. Calculate standardized coefficients (beta weights) to compare effect sizes across variables with different scales. Identify key drivers: rank variables by importance (coefficient magnitude × variable range, or standardized coefficients). Check for multicollinearity: variance inflation factors (VIF) - values >10 indicate issues. Examine residuals: patterns may indicate missing variables or model misspecification. Provide practical interpretation: what the model tells us about [business_question], which factors matter most, expected impact of changes to [key_variables], and predictions for [scenario]. Address limitations: model assumptions, generalizability, and causal inference caveats (correlation vs causation). Provide recommendations: actionable insights, variables to focus on, and model improvements.

variations.short: Interpret regression predicting [Y] from [X variables]. Explain coefficients, significance, R-squared. Provide insights.
variations.detailed: Provide comprehensive regression interpretation including: interaction effects analysis, non-linear relationships, model diagnostics (leverage, influence, Cook's distance), robust standard errors, bootstrap confidence intervals, and model comparison (nested models, AIC/BIC). Include advanced interpretation: marginal effects, predicted values with confidence intervals, and scenario analysis. Create visualizations: coefficient plots, residual plots, partial regression plots, and prediction intervals.
variations.strict: Interpret regression per [statistical_standards] (e.g., APA, journal guidelines). Use [specific_software] with [validation_procedures]. Report all statistics per [reporting_requirements]. Validate assumptions with [diagnostic_tests]. Document methodology. Ensure reproducibility.

tips: Distinguish statistical significance from practical significance. Check model assumptions before interpreting. Be cautious about causal claims - regression shows association, not necessarily causation. Consider interaction effects and non-linear relationships. Use confidence intervals, not just point estimates.

title: Time Series Analysis Guide
primary_use_case: Analyze time series data to identify trends, seasonality, and patterns for forecasting and decision-making
user_role: Data Scientist, Financial Analyst, Operations Analyst, Business Analyst
output_type: Time series analysis report with decomposition and forecasting
prompt_text: Perform time series analysis on [time_series_data] covering [time_period] with [frequency] (daily, weekly, monthly, etc.) measuring [metric]. Examine data characteristics: plot time series to visualize trends, identify missing values and outliers, check for stationarity (constant mean and variance over time) using tests like Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF), and assess data quality. Decompose time series: separate into components - trend (long-term direction), seasonality (recurring patterns), cyclical (irregular cycles), and residual (random noise). Use decomposition methods: moving averages, STL decomposition, or X-13ARIMA-SEATS. Analyze patterns: calculate growth rates (period-over-period, year-over-year), identify seasonal patterns (seasonal indices, peak/off-peak periods), detect structural breaks or regime changes, and analyze volatility patterns. Perform statistical analysis: autocorrelation function (ACF) and partial autocorrelation (PACF) to identify ARIMA model parameters, test for unit roots, and identify optimal differencing. Model selection: fit appropriate models (ARIMA, exponential smoothing, Prophet, or machine learning approaches) and compare using AIC/BIC or cross-validation. Generate forecasts: create [forecast_horizon] period ahead forecasts with confidence intervals, provide point forecasts and prediction intervals, and assess forecast accuracy using metrics (MAPE, RMSE, MAE). Identify anomalies: detect unusual patterns, outliers, or structural breaks. Provide insights: key trends, seasonal patterns, forecast implications, and recommendations. Include visualizations: time series plots, decomposition charts, ACF/PACF plots, and forecast plots.

variations.short: Analyze time series [data] for [metric]. Identify trends, seasonality. Create [N]-period forecast with confidence intervals.
variations.detailed: Execute comprehensive time series analysis including: multivariate time series with VAR models, state space models, Bayesian time series, regime-switching models, and machine learning approaches (LSTM, transformer models). Include advanced techniques: change point detection, anomaly detection with isolation forests, ensemble forecasting, and real-time updating models. Create interactive dashboard with drill-down capabilities and automated alerting.
variations.strict: Perform analysis per [time_series_methodology] standards. Use [specific_software] with [validation_procedures]. Validate stationarity assumptions. Document all transformations. Ensure reproducibility. Report per [statistical_reporting_standards].

tips: Check for stationarity - many time series methods require it. Account for seasonality - it's often a key driver. Use multiple models and compare performance. Validate forecasts on holdout data. Consider external factors and structural breaks. Update models regularly as new data arrives.

title: Data Visualization Recommender
primary_use_case: Recommend appropriate data visualizations based on data characteristics and analysis objectives
user_role: Data Analyst, Business Intelligence Analyst, Data Scientist, Consultant
output_type: Visualization recommendations with rationale and implementation guidance
prompt_text: Recommend appropriate data visualizations for [analysis_objective] using dataset [dataset_description] with variables: [variable_types] (e.g., continuous, categorical, time-based, geographic). Analyze data characteristics: number of variables, data types, distribution shapes, relationships of interest, and audience [target_audience]. For univariate analysis: recommend histograms or density plots for continuous variables to show distributions, bar charts or pie charts for categorical variables to show frequencies, and box plots to show distributions with outliers. For bivariate analysis: recommend scatter plots for two continuous variables to show relationships, line charts for time series data, bar charts for categorical vs continuous comparisons, heatmaps for correlation matrices, and grouped/stacked bar charts for categorical relationships. For multivariate analysis: recommend parallel coordinates, radar charts, small multiples, or faceted plots. Consider visualization goals: comparison (bar charts, line charts), distribution (histograms, box plots), relationship (scatter plots, heatmaps), composition (pie charts, stacked bars), or trends over time (line charts, area charts). Specify design recommendations: color schemes ([color_palette]), chart sizing and aspect ratios, axis labels and titles, legends, and annotations. Recommend tools: [tool_preferences] (Tableau, Power BI, Python matplotlib/seaborn, R ggplot2, D3.js). Provide implementation guidance: code snippets or step-by-step instructions, data preparation requirements, and best practices. Consider accessibility: colorblind-friendly palettes, sufficient contrast, and clear labeling. Include examples and rationale for each recommendation.

variations.short: Recommend visualizations for [data] showing [relationships]. Suggest chart types, tools, and design best practices.
variations.detailed: Provide comprehensive visualization strategy including: interactive visualization recommendations, animation for time-based data, geospatial visualizations if applicable, 3D visualizations where appropriate, and dashboard layout recommendations. Include advanced techniques: statistical overlays (regression lines, confidence intervals), small multiples for comparisons, and storytelling through visualization sequence. Provide tool-specific implementation guides and code templates.
variations.strict: Recommend visualizations per [design_system] standards. Follow [accessibility_guidelines] (WCAG 2.1). Use [specific_tools] with [configuration]. Ensure [brand_guidelines] compliance. Validate against [usability_criteria].

tips: Match visualization type to your question and data. Less is more - avoid clutter. Use color meaningfully and consistently. Consider your audience's data literacy. Test visualizations with actual users. Ensure accessibility for all viewers.

title: Root Cause Analysis (5 Whys / Fishbone)
primary_use_case: Identify root causes of problems or issues using structured analytical frameworks
user_role: Operations Manager, Quality Analyst, Process Improvement Specialist, Problem Solver
output_type: Root cause analysis report with identified causes and solutions
prompt_text: Perform root cause analysis for [problem_description] that occurred in [context] affecting [impact_area]. Define the problem clearly: what happened, when it occurred, who was affected, and the impact (quantify if possible: [impact_metrics]). Apply 5 Whys technique: start with the problem statement and ask 'Why?' five times, drilling down from symptoms to root cause. Document each level: Problem → Why 1 → Why 2 → Why 3 → Why 4 → Root Cause. Create Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram: identify main categories of potential causes - [cause_categories] such as People, Process, Technology, Materials, Environment, Methods, or Management. For each category, brainstorm contributing factors and sub-factors. Organize causes hierarchically showing relationships. Validate root causes: gather evidence [evidence_sources] to support identified causes, verify with data or observations, and distinguish between symptoms and true root causes. Prioritize causes: assess impact (high/medium/low) and likelihood, identify which causes are most critical to address, and consider interdependencies between causes. Develop solutions: for each root cause, propose corrective actions, preventive measures to avoid recurrence, and process improvements. Assess solution feasibility: evaluate effort required, resources needed, expected effectiveness, and implementation timeline. Create action plan: assign owners, set timelines, define success metrics, and establish monitoring. Include verification: how to confirm root cause was addressed and problem is resolved.

variations.short: Analyze root cause of [problem] using 5 Whys and Fishbone. Identify solutions and action plan.
variations.detailed: Execute comprehensive root cause analysis including: multiple analysis frameworks (5 Whys, Fishbone, Fault Tree Analysis, Failure Mode Analysis), data-driven validation with statistical analysis, stakeholder interviews, process mapping to identify systemic issues, and historical pattern analysis. Include advanced techniques: Bayesian analysis for cause probability, simulation modeling, and predictive root cause analysis. Create detailed action plan with risk mitigation and success measurement framework.
variations.strict: Perform analysis per [quality_standard] (e.g., ISO, Six Sigma DMAIC). Use [specific_methodology] validated by [validation_process]. Document per [documentation_requirements]. Include [required_elements]. Ensure [compliance_requirements].

tips: Distinguish symptoms from root causes - keep asking why until you reach the fundamental cause. Involve people close to the problem - they have valuable insights. Validate hypotheses with data, not just assumptions. Focus on systemic causes, not blame. Document the analysis for future reference.

title: Risk Assessment Matrix
primary_use_case: Assess and prioritize risks by evaluating likelihood and impact to inform risk management strategies
user_role: Risk Manager, Project Manager, Compliance Officer, Executive
output_type: Risk assessment matrix with prioritized risks and mitigation strategies
prompt_text: Create a risk assessment matrix for [project/initiative/business_area] in context of [business_context]. Identify risks: brainstorm potential risks across categories [risk_categories] such as operational, financial, strategic, compliance, technology, market, or reputational. For each identified risk, document: risk description, potential causes, potential consequences, and affected areas. Assess likelihood: rate each risk's probability of occurring using scale [likelihood_scale] (e.g., Very Low, Low, Medium, High, Very High) or numerical (1-5). Base assessment on: historical data, expert judgment, industry benchmarks, or predictive indicators. Assess impact: rate severity of consequences if risk materializes using scale [impact_scale] (e.g., Negligible, Low, Medium, High, Critical) or numerical (1-5). Consider impact dimensions: financial loss, operational disruption, reputation damage, regulatory consequences, or strategic impact. Calculate risk score: multiply likelihood × impact to get risk rating. Create risk matrix: 2D grid with likelihood on one axis, impact on other, plot each risk. Categorize risks: High (red zone - immediate attention), Medium (yellow zone - monitor), Low (green zone - acceptable). Prioritize risks: rank by risk score, identify top risks requiring immediate action, and consider risk interdependencies. Develop mitigation strategies: for high-priority risks, define risk mitigation actions (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept), assign owners, set timelines, and estimate costs. Define monitoring: establish risk indicators, review frequency, and escalation procedures. Include risk appetite: define acceptable risk levels for [organization].

variations.short: Create risk matrix for [project]. Identify risks, assess likelihood/impact, prioritize, and recommend mitigations.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive risk assessment including: quantitative risk analysis with Monte Carlo simulation, scenario analysis, stress testing, risk correlation analysis, and dynamic risk modeling. Include advanced techniques: Bayesian risk assessment, predictive risk indicators, and real-time risk monitoring. Create risk dashboard with automated alerting and integration with risk management systems.
variations.strict: Assess risks per [risk_management_standard] (e.g., ISO 31000, COSO ERM). Use [specific_methodology] validated by [validation_process]. Document per [documentation_requirements]. Include [regulatory_requirements]. Ensure [compliance_standards].

tips: Involve diverse stakeholders to identify comprehensive risk list. Use consistent scales for likelihood and impact. Update risk assessments regularly as conditions change. Focus mitigation efforts on high-priority risks. Consider both probability and impact - a low-probability high-impact risk may need attention. Document assumptions and rationale.

title: Cost-Benefit Analysis Framework
primary_use_case: Evaluate the financial viability of projects, initiatives, or decisions by comparing costs and benefits
user_role: Financial Analyst, Project Manager, Business Analyst, Executive
output_type: Cost-benefit analysis report with NPV, ROI, and recommendations
prompt_text: Perform a cost-benefit analysis for [project/initiative] over [time_horizon] period. Define the initiative: [initiative_description] with objectives [objectives]. Identify and quantify costs: one-time costs ([one_time_costs] such as implementation, setup, training), recurring costs ([recurring_costs] such as maintenance, licenses, personnel), opportunity costs (alternatives foregone), and indirect costs (overhead allocation). Identify and quantify benefits: direct financial benefits ([direct_benefits] such as revenue increase, cost savings), indirect benefits ([indirect_benefits] such as productivity gains, risk reduction), qualitative benefits ([qualitative_benefits] such as improved satisfaction, brand value), and avoided costs (prevented losses). Assign monetary values: estimate dollar amounts for all quantifiable items, use market rates or internal estimates, and document assumptions for qualitative benefits. Time-value considerations: apply discount rate [discount_rate]% to calculate present value of future cash flows, calculate Net Present Value (NPV) = sum of discounted benefits - sum of discounted costs, calculate Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR) = present value of benefits / present value of costs, and calculate payback period (time to recover initial investment). Perform sensitivity analysis: test how results change with different assumptions (costs ±20%, benefits ±20%, discount rate variations), identify critical assumptions, and assess risk. Compare alternatives: if evaluating multiple options, compare NPV, BCR, and payback periods. Include non-financial factors: strategic alignment, risk considerations, implementation feasibility, and organizational readiness. Provide recommendation: proceed, modify, or reject, with clear justification. Include implementation considerations: resource requirements, timeline, and success factors.

variations.short: Analyze costs and benefits of [initiative] over [period]. Calculate NPV, BCR, payback. Provide recommendation.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive cost-benefit analysis including: probabilistic modeling with Monte Carlo simulation, scenario analysis (best/base/worst case), real options analysis for flexibility value, social cost-benefit analysis if applicable, and lifecycle cost analysis. Include advanced financial metrics: IRR (Internal Rate of Return), modified payback, and risk-adjusted NPV. Create detailed financial model with sensitivity analysis dashboard and interactive scenario planning.
variations.strict: Perform analysis per [financial_analysis_standards] (e.g., GAAP, government guidelines). Use [specific_methodology] validated by [validation_process]. Document all assumptions per [documentation_requirements]. Include [regulatory_requirements]. Validate calculations. Report per [financial_reporting_standards].

tips: Include all relevant costs and benefits, not just obvious ones. Use realistic estimates - be conservative with benefits, thorough with costs. Consider time value of money for multi-year projects. Perform sensitivity analysis on key assumptions. Document all assumptions clearly. Consider qualitative factors alongside financial metrics.

title: ROI Calculator and Business Case
primary_use_case: Calculate return on investment for business initiatives and build comprehensive business cases
user_role: Business Analyst, Finance Manager, Product Manager, Executive
output_type: Structured report with calculations, charts, and recommendations
prompt_text: Analyze the return on investment (ROI) for [project/initiative name] by calculating key financial metrics including net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), payback period, and total cost of ownership (TCO). Consider the following inputs: initial investment of [amount], expected annual revenue increase of [amount], cost savings of [amount] per year, implementation timeline of [duration], discount rate of [percentage], and ongoing operational costs of [amount] annually. Factor in [risk factors] and [market conditions]. Calculate ROI over [time horizon] years. Provide a detailed breakdown showing year-by-year cash flows, cumulative returns, and sensitivity analysis for key variables. Include a comparison against [alternative options] and industry benchmarks. Present findings in a business case format suitable for [stakeholder audience] with clear recommendations on whether to proceed, defer, or reject the initiative.

variations.short: Calculate ROI for [project] with investment [amount], annual revenue [amount], and [duration] timeline. Show NPV, IRR, and payback period.
variations.detailed: Conduct a comprehensive ROI analysis for [project/initiative] including detailed financial modeling, risk assessment, scenario planning, competitive analysis, and strategic alignment evaluation. Provide executive summary, detailed calculations, visualizations, and actionable recommendations.
variations.strict: Using standard financial formulas (NPV = Σ(CFt/(1+r)^t) - Initial Investment, IRR where NPV=0, Payback Period = Initial Investment / Annual Cash Flow), calculate ROI metrics for [project] with provided inputs. Show all calculations step-by-step. No assumptions beyond provided data.

tips: Include risk-adjusted returns, consider opportunity costs, use appropriate discount rates, and validate assumptions with historical data or industry standards.

title: Product Analytics Interpreter
primary_use_case: Interpret product usage data and translate metrics into actionable insights
user_role: Product Manager, Data Analyst, Product Analyst
output_type: Analysis report with insights, trends, and recommendations
prompt_text: Analyze product analytics data for [product/feature name] covering the period from [start date] to [end date]. Review key metrics including daily/monthly active users ([DAU/MAU values]), feature adoption rates ([feature names] with [adoption percentages]), user retention cohorts ([cohort data]), conversion funnel metrics ([funnel stages] with [conversion rates]), session duration ([average duration]), and user engagement scores ([engagement metrics]). Identify trends, anomalies, and patterns in the data. Compare performance across [user segments], [geographic regions], or [device types]. Highlight which features drive the most value, where users drop off, and what behaviors correlate with [success metric]. Provide insights on [specific business question] and recommend [number] actionable improvements. Include visualizations suggestions and prioritize recommendations by potential impact.

variations.short: Analyze product metrics: [DAU], [retention rate], [feature adoption]. Identify top issues and 3 improvement recommendations.
variations.detailed: Conduct deep-dive product analytics analysis including cohort analysis, funnel optimization, feature usage patterns, user segmentation analysis, A/B test results interpretation, and predictive modeling for user behavior. Provide comprehensive insights with statistical significance testing.
variations.strict: Using provided product analytics data ([dataset]), calculate exact metrics: retention rate = (Users at end / Users at start) × 100, conversion rate = (Completed actions / Total users) × 100. Report only findings directly supported by data. No speculation.

tips: Focus on actionable insights over vanity metrics, use cohort analysis for retention, segment users meaningfully, and correlate metrics with business outcomes.

title: Web Analytics / GA4 Analysis

Analyze traffic sources showing organic search ([percentage]), paid search ([percentage]), direct ([percentage]), social media ([percentage]), referral ([percentage]), and other channels. Examine top-performing pages ([page URLs] with [metrics]), user demographics ([age groups], [gender distribution], [geographic locations]), device breakdown ([desktop/mobile/tablet percentages]), and user flow through [key conversion paths]. Identify trends, anomalies, and opportunities. Compare performance against [previous period] or [industry benchmarks]. Answer specific questions about [business objective] and provide [number] prioritized recommendations for improving [target metric]. Include suggestions for A/B testing opportunities.

Provide detailed insights with statistical analysis and competitive benchmarking.

title: Social Media Analytics
primary_use_case: Analyze social media performance across platforms and extract actionable insights

Analyze top-performing content types ([content categories] with [performance metrics]), best posting times ([time slots] with [engagement data]), hashtag performance ([hashtags] with [reach/engagement]), audience demographics ([age, gender, location data]), sentiment analysis ([positive/negative/neutral percentages]), and competitor comparison ([competitor accounts] with [comparative metrics]). Identify content themes that resonate, optimal posting frequency, and engagement patterns. Answer questions about [specific campaign] or [business goal]. Provide [number] actionable recommendations for improving [target metric] and content strategy suggestions for [upcoming period].

Provide detailed insights with competitive benchmarking.

title: SEO Content Gap Analysis
primary_use_case: Identify content opportunities by comparing your content against competitors and search intent
user_role: SEO Specialist, Content Strategist, Digital Marketing Manager

Analyze keyword coverage showing which keywords [competitors] rank for that you don't ([keyword list] with [search volumes] and [difficulty scores]), content topics covered by competitors but missing from your site ([topic list] with [relevance scores]), content depth comparison ([your content length] vs [competitor content length] for [topics]), backlink profiles ([your backlinks] vs [competitor backlinks]), and SERP feature opportunities ([feature types] like featured snippets, People Also Ask, etc.). Review search intent alignment for [target keywords] and identify content formats that perform well ([content types] with [performance metrics]). Prioritize opportunities by [search volume], [competition difficulty], [business relevance], and [content creation effort]. Provide a prioritized list of [number] content opportunities with recommended content types, target keywords, content angles, and estimated impact. Include suggestions for optimizing existing content.

variations.short: Find content gaps: compare [your site] vs [competitors] for [keywords]. List top 5 missing content opportunities.
variations.detailed: Conduct deep SEO content gap analysis including semantic keyword research, content cluster analysis, topical authority mapping, user intent analysis, content freshness comparison, technical SEO gaps, and content performance prediction. Provide comprehensive content strategy roadmap.
variations.strict: Using provided keyword data ([dataset]) and competitor content inventory ([dataset]), identify exact gaps: keywords competitors rank for (position < 20) that you don't. Calculate opportunity score = (Search Volume × (1 - Competition) × Relevance). Report only data-supported opportunities.

tips: Focus on high-intent keywords, consider content clusters, analyze search intent, and prioritize by business value and feasibility.

title: Email Campaign Performance Analysis

Analyze performance by [segments: demographics, behavior, acquisition source, etc.] showing [segment names] with [respective metrics]. Compare subject line performance ([subject lines] with [open rates]), send time analysis ([time slots] with [engagement metrics]), content type performance ([content formats] with [CTR/conversion]), and device breakdown ([desktop/mobile percentages] with [engagement]). Identify trends, anomalies, and patterns. Compare against [previous campaigns] or [industry benchmarks]. Answer questions about [specific campaign element] and provide [number] prioritized recommendations for improving [target metric]. Include A/B test suggestions and segmentation opportunities.

variations.short: Analyze email campaign: [open rate], [CTR], [conversion rate]. Identify top 3 optimization opportunities.
variations.detailed: Conduct comprehensive email analysis including advanced segmentation analysis, predictive modeling for optimal send times, content performance deep-dive, subscriber lifecycle analysis, deliverability assessment, and revenue attribution modeling. Provide detailed insights with statistical significance testing.

title: Supply Chain Analytics

prompt_text: Analyze supply chain performance for [company/product line] covering [time period]. Analyze performance across [suppliers/vendors] showing [supplier names] with [performance metrics], [geographic regions] with [logistics metrics], [product categories] with [inventory metrics], and [time periods] with [trend data]. Identify bottlenecks in [supply chain stages: procurement, manufacturing, warehousing, distribution], cost drivers, and risk factors ([risk types] with [impact assessments]). Compare against [industry benchmarks] or [target KPIs]. variations.short: Analyze supply chain: [on-time delivery], [inventory turnover], [supplier performance]. Identify top 3 optimization opportunities.
variations.detailed: Conduct comprehensive supply chain analysis including network optimization modeling, demand forecasting accuracy, supplier risk assessment, cost-to-serve analysis, end-to-end visibility mapping, and predictive analytics for disruptions. Provide detailed insights with scenario planning.
variations.strict: Using provided supply chain data ([dataset]), calculate exact metrics: inventory turnover = (COGS / Average Inventory), on-time delivery = (On-time orders / Total orders) × 100. Report only data-supported findings. No assumptions.

title: Inventory Optimization

user_role: Inventory Manager, Supply Chain Analyst, Operations Manager
output_type: Inventory optimization report with recommended stock levels and cost analysis
prompt_text: Optimize inventory levels for [product categories/SKUs] considering [business objectives: minimize stockouts, reduce carrying costs, optimize working capital]. Analyze current inventory metrics including current stock levels ([SKU names] with [quantities]), average demand ([demand values] with [time periods]), demand variability ([coefficient of variation] or [standard deviation]), lead times ([lead time values] by [suppliers]), carrying costs ([percentage] of inventory value), stockout costs ([cost per occurrence]), and service level targets ([target percentage]). Perform ABC analysis classifying items by [value/volume criteria] into categories A ([items] with [percentage] of value), B ([items]), and C ([items]). Calculate optimal reorder points using [method: fixed order quantity, continuous review, etc.] considering [safety stock requirements] and [demand uncertainty]. Determine economic order quantities (EOQ) where applicable. Analyze inventory turnover ratios ([current ratios] vs [target ratios]) and days of inventory on hand ([current days] vs [target days]). Identify slow-moving ([SKUs] with [metrics]) and obsolete inventory ([items] with [values]). Provide recommendations for [number] SKUs with highest impact potential, including recommended stock levels, reorder points, order quantities, and expected cost savings. Include risk assessment for recommended changes.

variations.short: Optimize inventory for [SKUs]: current [stock levels], demand [values], lead time [duration]. Recommend reorder points and quantities.
variations.detailed: Conduct comprehensive inventory optimization including multi-echelon optimization, stochastic demand modeling, seasonality analysis, supplier reliability factors, multi-product constraints, and dynamic reorder policies. Provide detailed optimization model with sensitivity analysis.
variations.strict: Using provided inventory data ([dataset]), calculate exact metrics: EOQ = √((2 × Demand × Order Cost) / Carrying Cost), Reorder Point = (Average Demand × Lead Time) + Safety Stock, Safety Stock = Z × √(Lead Time) × Standard Deviation of Demand. Report only calculated values.

tips: Consider demand variability, lead time uncertainty, service level requirements, and balance multiple objectives. Use appropriate inventory models for your context.

title: Workforce Analytics / Headcount Planning

title: NPS Score Analysis
primary_use_case: Analyze Net Promoter Score data to understand customer loyalty and identify improvement opportunities
user_role: Customer Success Manager, Product Manager, Marketing Manager, CX Analyst
output_type: NPS analysis report with score breakdown, trends, and action recommendations
prompt_text: Analyze Net Promoter Score (NPS) data for [company/product/service] covering [time period]. Correlate NPS with [business metrics: retention, revenue, usage, etc.] showing [correlation findings]. Compare against [previous periods], [competitors], or [industry benchmarks]. Identify drivers of promoter scores ([factors] with [impact]) and root causes of detractor scores ([issues] with [severity]). Answer questions about [specific segment] or [improvement area]. Provide [number] prioritized recommendations for improving NPS, including [specific actions] targeting [detractor drivers] and [enhancement opportunities] for [promoter factors]. Include target NPS goals and action plan.

variations.short: Analyze NPS: current score [value], breakdown [promoters/passives/detractors %]. Identify top 3 improvement areas.
variations.detailed: Conduct comprehensive NPS analysis including predictive modeling for churn risk, sentiment analysis of verbatims, correlation analysis with business outcomes, cohort analysis, competitive benchmarking, and action prioritization matrix. Provide detailed customer experience strategy.

tips: Focus on actionable feedback themes, segment meaningfully, track trends over time, and correlate NPS with business outcomes to prioritize actions.

title: Feature Prioritization (RICE/ICE)
primary_use_case: Prioritize product features or initiatives using RICE or ICE scoring frameworks
user_role: Product Manager, Product Owner, Strategy Manager
output_type: Prioritized feature list with scores and recommendations
prompt_text: Prioritize [product features/initiatives] using [RICE/ICE framework] to determine which features should be built first. For each feature, gather inputs: [Feature names] with [descriptions]. For RICE scoring, collect Reach ([number of users/events affected] per [time period]), Impact ([score 0.25 to 3.0] representing [minimal to massive impact]), Confidence ([percentage] representing [certainty level]), and Effort ([person-months] or [story points]). For ICE scoring, collect Impact ([score 1-10]), Confidence ([score 1-10]), and Ease ([score 1-10]). Calculate RICE scores using formula: RICE = (Reach × Impact × Confidence) / Effort. Calculate ICE scores using formula: ICE = (Impact + Confidence + Ease) / 3. Rank features by score and group into [priority tiers: Must Have, Should Have, Could Have, Won't Have]. Consider [business constraints: budget, timeline, dependencies, strategic alignment]. Analyze trade-offs between [high-scoring features] and [strategic initiatives]. Answer questions about [specific feature] or [prioritization criteria]. title: Correlation vs Causation Evaluator

Analyze potential confounding variables including [confounder names] with [their relationships to variables A and B]. Consider temporal ordering: does [variable A] occur before [variable B] ([timeline analysis])? Evaluate alternative explanations: [alternative hypothesis 1] with [evidence], [alternative hypothesis 2] with [evidence], and [reverse causation possibility] with [evidence]. Assess study design: [observational/experimental] study with [design details] and [control mechanisms]. Review [existing research/literature] on this relationship. Apply causal inference criteria: [temporal precedence], [covariation], [elimination of alternatives], and [theoretical plausibility]. Determine if [experimental design: randomized controlled trial, A/B test, etc.] would be needed to establish causation. Provide conclusion: [correlation only / likely causation / insufficient evidence] with [confidence level] and [reasoning]. Recommend [next steps: additional analysis, experiments, etc.] to strengthen causal claims.

variations.short: Evaluate if [variable A] causes [variable B]: correlation [r value], study type [design]. Conclude correlation vs causation.

tips: Always consider confounding variables, require temporal precedence and elimination of alternatives for causation, and use appropriate statistical methods for causal inference.

Assess model performance: for classification, calculate Accuracy = ([TP] + [TN]) / ([TP] + [TN] + [FP] + [FN]) = [percentage], Precision = [TP] / ([TP] + [FP]) = [percentage], Recall = [TP] / ([TP] + [FN]) = [percentage], F1-Score = 2 × ([Precision] × [Recall]) / ([Precision] + [Recall]) = [value], and AUC-ROC = [value]. For regression, calculate RMSE = √(Σ([Predicted] - [Actual])² / [N]) = [value], MAE = Σ|[Predicted] - [Actual]| / [N] = [value], R² = [value], and MAPE = (Σ|[Predicted] - [Actual]| / [Actual]) / [N] × 100 = [percentage]. Perform cross-validation: [K-fold] cross-validation showing [mean] ± [std] for [metrics] indicating [stability assessment]. Analyze prediction errors: error distribution showing [patterns], [systematic biases] in [predictions], and [outliers] with [characteristics]. Assess model calibration: predicted probabilities [well-calibrated/overconfident/underconfident] showing [calibration curve data]. Analyze feature importance: [features] contribute [percentages] to predictions. Test on [holdout set] showing [performance] vs [training performance] indicating [overfitting assessment]. Compare against [baseline models] or [alternative models] showing [relative performance]. Answer questions about [specific metric] or [model aspect]. Provide assessment: model is [suitable/needs improvement] for [use case] with [confidence level]. Include [number] recommendations for [model improvement], [feature engineering], or [deployment considerations].

variations.short: Evaluate [model] performance: Accuracy [%], Precision [%], Recall [%], F1 [value]. Assess overfitting and recommend improvements.
variations.detailed: Conduct comprehensive model evaluation including advanced metrics (log-loss, Brier score), learning curves, confusion matrix analysis, error analysis by segment, fairness metrics, explainability assessment, and production monitoring framework. Provide detailed model validation report.
variations.strict: Using provided predictions ([dataset]) and actuals ([dataset]), calculate exact metrics: Accuracy = (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN), Precision = TP / (TP + FP), Recall = TP / (TP + FN), RMSE = √(Σ(Predicted - Actual)² / N). Report only calculated values.

tips: Use appropriate metrics for your problem type, validate on independent test set, check for overfitting, analyze errors systematically, and consider business context in evaluation.

title: Marketing Strategy Builder
primary_use_case: Develop comprehensive marketing strategies for new products or services
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive marketing strategy for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] targeting [TARGET AUDIENCE] in the [INDUSTRY] sector. The strategy should include: (1) Executive summary outlining key objectives and expected outcomes, (2) Market analysis covering competitive landscape, market size, and growth trends, (3) Target audience segmentation with detailed personas and their pain points, (4) Positioning strategy that differentiates [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] from competitors, (5) Marketing mix including product features, pricing strategy, distribution channels, and promotional tactics, (6) Channel strategy detailing digital and traditional marketing channels with budget allocation, (7) Content marketing plan with themes, formats, and publishing schedule, (8) Key performance indicators (KPIs) and success metrics, (9) Timeline with milestones for the next [TIMEFRAME], and (10) Budget breakdown by channel and activity. Consider [SPECIFIC CONSTRAINTS] and leverage [KEY STRENGTHS] of the brand.

variations.short: Develop a marketing strategy for [PRODUCT] targeting [AUDIENCE] including positioning, channels, and KPIs.
variations.detailed: Create an exhaustive marketing strategy document for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] targeting [TARGET AUDIENCE] in [INDUSTRY]. Include comprehensive market analysis, competitive positioning, detailed audience personas, full marketing mix (4Ps), multi-channel strategy with budget allocation, content calendar, performance metrics, risk assessment, contingency plans, and a 12-month implementation roadmap with quarterly milestones.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY a marketing strategy following this exact structure: (1) Executive Summary (200 words), (2) Market Analysis (300 words), (3) Target Audience (200 words), (4) Positioning (150 words), (5) Marketing Mix (400 words), (6) Channel Strategy (300 words), (7) Content Plan (200 words), (8) KPIs (100 words), (9) Timeline (150 words), (10) Budget (200 words). Total: 2,250 words maximum.

tips: Provide specific industry context and competitor names for more accurate strategies. Include budget constraints and timeline expectations for realistic recommendations.

title: Brand Positioning Statement Creator
primary_use_case: Develop clear and compelling brand positioning statements
prompt_text: Create a brand positioning statement for [BRAND NAME] that clearly articulates its unique value in the [INDUSTRY] market. The positioning statement should follow this structure: (1) Target Audience: Define the primary customer segment including demographics, psychographics, and behavioral characteristics, (2) Frame of Reference: Identify the category or competitive set in which [BRAND NAME] competes, (3) Point of Difference: Highlight the unique benefits and attributes that distinguish [BRAND NAME] from competitors, focusing on [KEY DIFFERENTIATORS], (4) Reason to Believe: Provide credible evidence and proof points that support the positioning claims, (5) Brand Promise: Articulate the core promise [BRAND NAME] makes to customers. Additionally, create three alternative positioning angles: (a) functional positioning emphasizing product benefits, (b) emotional positioning focusing on feelings and experiences, and (c) symbolic positioning highlighting identity and status. Ensure the statement is memorable, credible, and actionable for marketing teams. Consider [BRAND VALUES] and [TARGET MARKET CONDITIONS].

variations.short: Write a brand positioning statement for [BRAND] targeting [AUDIENCE] with unique differentiators.
variations.detailed: Develop a comprehensive brand positioning framework for [BRAND NAME] including: detailed target audience analysis with personas, competitive landscape mapping, unique value proposition development, emotional and functional benefit articulation, brand archetype identification, messaging hierarchy, proof points and evidence, alternative positioning options, implementation guidelines for marketing teams, and measurement criteria for positioning effectiveness.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY a positioning statement in this format: 'For [TARGET AUDIENCE] who [NEED/PAIN POINT], [BRAND NAME] is the [CATEGORY] that [BENEFIT] because [REASON TO BELIEVE].' Maximum 50 words. Then provide three variations: functional (30 words), emotional (30 words), symbolic (30 words).

tips: Include specific competitor names and customer research insights for more precise positioning. Test the statement by checking if it's clear, distinctive, and defensible.

title: Customer Persona Generator
