variations.short: Create a customer persona for [SEGMENT] including demographics, goals, pain points, and buying behavior.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive customer persona document for [PERSONA NAME] including: comprehensive demographic and psychographic profiles, detailed professional background, deep-dive into goals and motivations with psychological drivers, extensive pain point analysis with root causes, complete information diet and media consumption patterns, thorough buying behavior analysis with decision-making frameworks, technology stack and tool preferences, authentic voice samples and communication patterns, full customer journey map with emotions and actions at each stage, and recommendations for marketing and product strategies.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY a persona using this template: Name: [NAME], Age: [AGE], Title: [TITLE], Goals: [3 goals], Pain Points: [3 pain points], Quote: '[QUOTE]', Preferred Channels: [3 channels]. Maximum 200 words total.

tips: Use real customer interview data when available. Include specific examples and scenarios to make personas more actionable for teams.

Consider [BUDGET CONSTRAINTS] and [TIMELINE REQUIREMENTS].

variations.short: Develop a go-to-market strategy for [PRODUCT] including target market, pricing, channels, and launch plan.
variations.detailed: Create an exhaustive go-to-market strategy document for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] including: comprehensive market opportunity analysis with TAM/SAM/SOM calculations, detailed product-market fit assessment, multi-segment target customer analysis, thorough competitive intelligence with battle cards, sophisticated pricing strategy with multiple models and scenarios, complete distribution channel strategy with partner programs, full sales strategy including team structure and compensation, comprehensive marketing plan with brand positioning and multi-channel campaigns, customer success framework with onboarding and retention, detailed launch timeline with dependencies and critical path, success metrics dashboard, risk assessment matrix, and resource requirements.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY a GTM strategy with these sections: (1) Market Opportunity (150 words), (2) Target Customers (100 words), (3) Pricing (100 words), (4) Channels (150 words), (5) Sales Strategy (100 words), (6) Marketing Plan (150 words), (7) Launch Timeline (100 words), (8) Metrics (50 words). Total: 800 words maximum.

tips: Include specific market research data and customer validation insights. Align GTM strategy with company resources and capabilities for realistic execution.

title: SEO Strategy and Content Plan
primary_use_case: Develop SEO strategies and content plans for organic growth
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive SEO strategy and content plan for [WEBSITE/BRAND NAME] in the [INDUSTRY] sector. The strategy should include: (1) SEO Audit: Current performance analysis, technical SEO issues, on-page optimization gaps, and backlink profile assessment, (2) Keyword Research: Target keyword identification including primary keywords ([PRIMARY KEYWORDS]), long-tail keywords, semantic keywords, and competitor keywords with search volume and difficulty scores, (3) Content Gap Analysis: Comparison with competitors' content, identification of content opportunities, and content refresh recommendations, (4) Content Strategy: Content pillars, content types (blog posts, guides, videos, infographics), content formats, and content themes aligned with [BUSINESS GOALS], (5) Content Calendar: 90-day content publishing schedule with topics, keywords, content types, and publishing dates, (6) On-Page SEO: Title tag optimization, meta descriptions, header structure, internal linking strategy, and schema markup recommendations, (7) Technical SEO: Site speed optimization, mobile responsiveness, crawlability improvements, and site structure enhancements, (8) Link Building Strategy: Outreach targets, content for link acquisition, and relationship-building tactics, (9) Local SEO (if applicable): Google Business Profile optimization, local citations, and location-based content, (10) Measurement and KPIs: Key metrics including organic traffic, keyword rankings, backlinks, and conversions. Consider [TARGET AUDIENCE] and [COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE].

variations.short: Create an SEO strategy for [BRAND] including keyword research, content plan, and optimization recommendations.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive SEO and content strategy including: comprehensive technical SEO audit with crawl analysis, extensive keyword research with competitor analysis and search intent mapping, detailed content gap analysis with opportunity scoring, complete content strategy with pillar pages and topic clusters, 12-month content calendar with editorial guidelines, thorough on-page optimization recommendations, comprehensive technical SEO roadmap, advanced link building strategy with outreach templates, local SEO optimization (if applicable), performance tracking dashboard, and competitive analysis framework.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY an SEO strategy with: (1) Top 20 target keywords with search volume, (2) Content calendar (10 topics with keywords), (3) Top 5 technical SEO fixes, (4) Top 5 on-page optimizations, (5) KPIs (5 metrics). Maximum 500 words.

tips: Use actual keyword research tools data when available. Focus on user intent and content quality over keyword stuffing. Regularly update strategy based on performance data.

title: Email Drip Campaign Designer
primary_use_case: Design automated email sequences for lead nurturing and customer engagement
prompt_text: Design a comprehensive email drip campaign for [CAMPAIGN PURPOSE] targeting [TARGET AUDIENCE] over [CAMPAIGN DURATION]. The campaign should align with [BRAND VOICE] and [BUSINESS OBJECTIVES].

variations.short: Create a [NUMBER]-email drip campaign for [AUDIENCE] with subject lines, content, and send schedule.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive email drip campaign including: comprehensive campaign strategy with multiple objectives, detailed audience segmentation with personas, complete email sequence with 10+ emails, full email copy for each message with subject lines and CTAs, A/B testing framework, advanced automation triggers and workflows, sophisticated segmentation rules, detailed design specifications, compliance checklist, performance dashboard, and optimization playbook.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY a [NUMBER]-email sequence. Each email must include: Subject: [SUBJECT], Send Day: [DAY], Body: [150 words], CTA: [CTA TEXT]. Maximum 200 words per email description.

tips: Focus on providing value in each email, not just selling. Use behavioral triggers to send relevant emails at the right time. Test subject lines and send times for optimal performance.

title: Influencer Outreach Strategy

The strategy should include: (1) Campaign Objectives: Goals (awareness, engagement, conversions), target metrics, and expected ROI, (2) Influencer Identification: Criteria for selecting influencers including follower count range ([FOLLOWER RANGE]), engagement rates, audience demographics, content quality, brand alignment, and niche relevance, (3) Influencer Tiers: Categorization into macro-influencers, micro-influencers, and nano-influencers with budget allocation, (4) Content Strategy: Types of content (posts, stories, videos, reels), content themes, key messages, and brand guidelines, (5) Outreach Plan: Initial contact templates, follow-up sequences, negotiation strategies, and relationship-building tactics, (6) Compensation Structure: Payment models (flat fee, commission, product exchange), rate ranges, and contract terms, (7) Campaign Timeline: Pre-campaign preparation, campaign execution schedule, and post-campaign activities, (8) Content Approval Process: Review workflow, revision guidelines, and approval timelines, (9) Measurement Framework: KPIs (reach, engagement, clicks, conversions), tracking methods, and reporting structure, (10) Legal Considerations: FTC disclosure requirements, contract essentials, and usage rights. tips: Focus on authentic partnerships over transactional relationships. Micro-influencers often have higher engagement rates. Ensure clear expectations and deliverables in contracts.

title: Event Marketing Plan

Consider [BUDGET] and [EVENT TYPE].

variations.short: Create an event marketing plan for [EVENT] including pre-event promotion, on-site activities, and post-event follow-up.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive event marketing plan including: comprehensive objectives with multi-funnel goals, detailed audience analysis with personas, complete pre-event marketing timeline (90+ days) with multi-channel strategy, extensive content calendar across all channels, full partnership and sponsorship activation plan, detailed on-site marketing and engagement strategy, comprehensive post-event follow-up sequence, complete budget breakdown with ROI projections, success metrics dashboard, and contingency planning.

title: Referral Program Designer

The program should include: (1) Program Objectives: Goals (customer acquisition, retention, LTV increase), target referral rates, and expected program ROI, (2) Incentive Structure: Rewards for referrers ([REFERRER REWARD]) and referees ([REFEREE REWARD]), reward types (discounts, credits, cash, products), reward timing (immediate vs. after conversion), and reward tiers for multiple referrals, (3) Program Mechanics: How referrals are tracked (unique links, codes, forms), referral process flow, eligibility criteria, and program terms and conditions, (4) Marketing and Promotion: How to communicate the program to existing customers, promotional materials (emails, in-app messages, social posts), program landing page, and ongoing promotion strategy, (5) Technology Requirements: Referral tracking system, reward fulfillment process, and program management tools, (6) Program Rules: Eligibility requirements, reward limits, expiration policies, and fraud prevention measures, (7) Success Metrics: Key performance indicators (referral rate, conversion rate, cost per acquisition, program ROI), tracking methods, and reporting structure, (8) Program Launch: Launch timeline, initial promotion campaign, and early adopter strategy, (9) Optimization Plan: A/B testing opportunities, program iterations, and continuous improvement approach. Consider [BUDGET] and [CUSTOMER BASE SIZE].

variations.short: Design a referral program for [COMPANY] with incentives, mechanics, and promotion plan.
variations.detailed: Create an exhaustive referral program including: comprehensive objectives with multi-funnel analysis, sophisticated incentive structure with multiple reward tiers, complete program mechanics with technical specifications, extensive marketing and promotion strategy, detailed technology requirements and integration plan, comprehensive program rules and compliance, success metrics dashboard, full launch plan, optimization framework, and competitive analysis.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Incentive structure (referrer + referee rewards), (2) Referral process (3 steps), (3) Top 5 promotion channels, (4) Top 5 success metrics. Maximum 300 words.

tips: Make the referral process simple and frictionless. Offer rewards valuable to both referrer and referee. Track and optimize based on which customers refer most and convert best.

title: Brand Voice Guidelines Creator

The guidelines should include: (1) Brand Personality: Core personality traits ([TRAIT 1], [TRAIT 2], [TRAIT 3]), brand archetype, and personality dimensions, (2) Voice Characteristics: How the brand sounds (conversational, professional, playful, authoritative), voice attributes with examples, and voice principles, (3) Tone Variations: How tone adapts across different contexts (customer support vs. marketing vs. sales), tone guidelines for various scenarios, and tone matrix, (4) Language Guidelines: Word choice preferences, words to use and avoid, industry terminology, and jargon usage, (5) Writing Style: Sentence structure preferences, paragraph length, use of humor, formality level, and punctuation style, (6) Content Examples: Do's and don'ts with before/after examples, sample copy for different channels (email, social, website, support), and example scenarios, (7) Channel-Specific Guidelines: Adaptations for email, social media, website, support, sales, and internal communications, (8) Audience Considerations: How voice adapts for different audience segments while maintaining brand consistency, (9) Implementation: How teams should use these guidelines, training recommendations, and review processes. variations.detailed: Develop exhaustive brand voice guidelines including: comprehensive brand personality framework with archetype analysis, detailed voice characteristics with extensive examples, complete tone variation matrix for all scenarios, extensive language guidelines with word lists, comprehensive writing style guide, extensive content examples across all channels, channel-specific adaptations, audience segment considerations, implementation playbook, training materials, and brand voice audit checklist.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) 5 personality traits (one sentence each), (2) Voice characteristics (3 attributes, 50 words total), (3) Do's and don'ts (3 each), (4) Example copy (100 words). Maximum 300 words.

title: Sales Pitch Script Generator

The script should include: (1) Opening Hook: Attention-grabbing opening that addresses [PROSPECT PAIN POINT] or creates curiosity, establishing rapport and setting the agenda, (2) Problem Identification: Questions to uncover pain points, challenges, and current frustrations related to [PROBLEM AREA], demonstrating understanding of their situation, (3) Solution Presentation: How [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] addresses identified problems, key features and benefits aligned with their needs, and value proposition articulation, (4) Proof and Credibility: Social proof (case studies, testimonials, customer success stories), relevant statistics, and credibility markers, (5) Objection Handling: Anticipated objections ([COMMON OBJECTION 1], [COMMON OBJECTION 2]) with prepared responses and reframing techniques, (6) Closing Techniques: Trial closes, assumptive closes, and call-to-action with next steps, (7) Follow-Up Plan: What happens after the pitch, follow-up sequence, and commitment to next steps, (8) Script Variations: 30-second elevator pitch, 2-minute pitch, 5-minute pitch, and 15-minute presentation version, (9) Delivery Tips: Body language, tone, pacing, and engagement techniques, (10) Customization Guide: How to adapt the script for different prospect types and industries. The script should align with [SALES METHODOLOGY].

variations.short: Create a sales pitch script for [PRODUCT] targeting [PROSPECT TYPE] with opening, solution, and close.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive sales pitch script including: multiple opening hooks for different scenarios, comprehensive problem identification framework with discovery questions, detailed solution presentation with feature-benefit mapping, extensive proof library with case studies, complete objection handling playbook, multiple closing techniques, full follow-up sequence, script variations for all timeframes, delivery coaching guide, customization framework, and role-play scenarios.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) 30-second pitch (exactly 30 seconds when spoken), (2) Opening hook (2 sentences), (3) Key value proposition (3 bullets), (4) Closing question. Maximum 200 words.

The sequence should include: (1) Research Framework: What to research about prospects before sending (company news, role, pain points, mutual connections), (2) Email 1 - Initial Outreach: Subject line optimized for [OPEN RATE GOAL], personalized opening referencing [RESEARCH ELEMENT], value proposition, clear call-to-action, and email length ([WORD COUNT]), (3) Email 2 - Follow-Up: Timing ([DAYS] after first email), subject line variations, additional value or angle, and gentle reminder, (4) Email 3 - Final Follow-Up: Timing, subject line, final value proposition or case study, and soft close, (5) Personalization Elements: How to personalize each email using [PERSONALIZATION FIELDS], research insights, and industry-specific angles, (6) A/B Testing Opportunities: Subject lines, send times, email length, and CTAs to test, (7) Compliance: CAN-SPAM compliance, unsubscribe options, and best practices, (8) Response Handling: Templates for common responses (interested, not interested, timing), (9) Sequence Variations: Different sequences for different personas, industries, or use cases, (10) Success Metrics: Open rates, reply rates, meeting booked rates, and optimization recommendations. variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive cold email sequence including: comprehensive research framework, complete 5+ email sequence with full copy, extensive personalization guide, A/B testing framework, compliance checklist, response handling templates, multiple sequence variations for different scenarios, success metrics dashboard, deliverability best practices, and optimization playbook.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY a 3-email sequence. Each email: Subject: [SUBJECT], Body: [100 words], CTA: [CTA]. Maximum 150 words per email.

title: Objection Handling Playbook
primary_use_case: Develop strategies and scripts for handling sales objections
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive objection handling playbook for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] sales team. The playbook should include: (1) Common Objections Catalog: List of [TOP 10 OBJECTIONS] categorized by type (price, timing, authority, need, competitor), (2) Objection Handling Framework: The LAER method (Listen, Acknowledge, Explore, Respond) or similar methodology, (3) Response Templates: For each objection, provide (a) acknowledgment statement showing empathy, (b) probing questions to understand root cause, (c) reframing technique, (d) value reinforcement, and (e) trial close, (4) Price Objections: Specific responses for 'too expensive', 'budget constraints', 'need to think about it', with value justification and payment options, (5) Timing Objections: Responses for 'not the right time', 'busy right now', 'end of quarter', with urgency creation and risk of delay, (6) Authority Objections: Handling 'I need to check with [DECISION MAKER]', 'not my decision', with stakeholder mapping and champion building, (7) Need/Objection: Addressing 'we're happy with current solution', 'don't see the need', with problem discovery and ROI demonstration, (8) Competitor Objections: Responses for 'considering [COMPETITOR]', 'already using [COMPETITOR]', with differentiation and migration path, (9) Role-Play Scenarios: Practice scenarios for each objection type, (10) Escalation Guidelines: When to escalate objections and how to involve management. Base responses on [PRODUCT VALUE PROPS] and [COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGES].

variations.short: Create an objection handling playbook with responses for [TOP 5 OBJECTIONS] using [FRAMEWORK].
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive objection handling playbook including: comprehensive objection catalog with 20+ objections, detailed handling framework with multiple methodologies, extensive response templates for all objection types, role-play scenarios, escalation procedures, objection prevention strategies, training materials, objection tracking system, and continuous improvement process.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY responses for [OBJECTION]. Format: (1) Acknowledge (1 sentence), (2) Question (1 question), (3) Response (3 sentences), (4) Trial close (1 question). Maximum 150 words per objection.

tips: Listen first, then respond. Many objections are smokescreens for real concerns. Use questions to uncover the true objection before responding.

title: Sales Discovery Call Framework
primary_use_case: Create frameworks and scripts for sales discovery calls
prompt_text: Develop a comprehensive sales discovery call framework for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] targeting [TARGET PROSPECT TYPE]. The framework should include: (1) Pre-Call Preparation: Research checklist (company background, prospect role, recent news, mutual connections, LinkedIn profile), agenda setting, and goal definition, (2) Call Opening: Introduction, rapport building, agenda setting ([DURATION] minutes), permission to ask questions, and expectations setting, (3) Discovery Questions Framework: BANT qualification (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline) questions, open-ended questions to uncover pain points, questions about current situation and processes, questions about goals and desired outcomes, and questions about decision-making process, (4) Question Categories: Situation questions (current state), problem questions (pain points), implication questions (impact of problems), and need-payoff questions (value of solution), (5) Active Listening Techniques: Note-taking, paraphrasing, summarizing, and building on responses, (6) Qualification Criteria: How to assess fit, budget, authority, need, and timeline during the call, (7) Value Proposition Tailoring: How to connect [PRODUCT FEATURES] to discovered needs and present relevant benefits, (8) Objection Anticipation: Common objections that may arise and how to address them, (9) Call Closing: Summary of key points, next steps, commitment to action, and scheduling follow-up, (10) Post-Call: Follow-up email template, CRM notes template, and handoff process. Align with [SALES METHODOLOGY].

variations.short: Create a discovery call framework with opening, [NUMBER] key questions, qualification criteria, and closing.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive discovery call framework including: comprehensive pre-call preparation guide, detailed opening script with variations, extensive question bank (50+ questions) organized by category, active listening techniques, complete qualification framework, value proposition tailoring guide, objection handling integration, closing techniques, post-call templates, and call analysis rubric.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Opening script (50 words), (2) Top 10 discovery questions, (3) Qualification checklist (5 criteria), (4) Closing script (50 words). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Ask open-ended questions and listen more than you talk. Take notes and reference them throughout. Qualify early to avoid wasting time on bad-fit prospects.

title: Competitive Battle Card Creator
primary_use_case: Create competitive intelligence battle cards for sales teams
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive competitive battle card for [COMPETITOR NAME] to help [PRODUCT NAME] sales team win deals. The battle card should include: (1) Competitor Overview: Company background, market position, funding status, and key executives, (2) Product/Service Analysis: Core offerings, key features, product strengths, and product weaknesses, (3) Pricing Strategy: Pricing model, price points, packaging options, and discounting practices, (4) Target Market: Primary customer segments, vertical focus, and company size targeting, (5) Sales Strategy: Sales model, sales process, and go-to-market approach, (6) Competitive Positioning: How they position themselves, key messaging, and brand perception, (7) Our Advantages: Where [PRODUCT NAME] is superior ([ADVANTAGE 1], [ADVANTAGE 2], [ADVANTAGE 3]), feature comparisons, and differentiation points, (8) Their Advantages: Where [COMPETITOR NAME] is stronger, and how to acknowledge but reframe, (9) Objection Handling: Common objections when competing against [COMPETITOR NAME] and how to respond, (10) Win Strategies: Specific tactics to win against this competitor, proof points, case studies, and talking points, (11) Loss Analysis: Why deals are lost to this competitor and how to prevent, (12) Quick Reference: One-page summary with key talking points and objection responses. Base this on [COMPETITIVE RESEARCH] and [SALES FEEDBACK].

variations.short: Create a battle card for [COMPETITOR] including their strengths, our advantages, and win strategies.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive battle card including: comprehensive competitor analysis, detailed product comparison matrix, extensive pricing analysis, complete market positioning, full sales strategy assessment, comprehensive differentiation analysis, extensive objection handling guide, win/loss analysis, quick reference guide, and regular update process.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Top 3 competitor strengths, (2) Top 3 our advantages, (3) Top 3 win strategies, (4) Top 3 objection responses. Maximum 200 words.

tips: Keep battle cards concise and scannable. Update regularly based on sales feedback and competitive intelligence. Focus on differentiation, not competitor bashing.

title: Sales Forecast Model
primary_use_case: Develop sales forecasting models and methodologies
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive sales forecast model for [COMPANY NAME] to predict revenue for [FORECAST PERIOD]. The model should include: (1) Forecast Methodology: Approach (bottom-up, top-down, or hybrid), forecast cadence ([FREQUENCY]), and confidence levels, (2) Data Sources: CRM data, historical performance, pipeline data, win rates, sales cycle length, and external factors, (3) Pipeline Analysis: Current pipeline value, stage distribution, weighted pipeline by probability, and pipeline health indicators, (4) Historical Trends: Past performance analysis, seasonality patterns, growth trends, and conversion rates by stage, (5) Deal Probability Framework: Probability percentages by sales stage ([STAGE 1]: [PROBABILITY]%, [STAGE 2]: [PROBABILITY]%, etc.), factors affecting probability, and deal scoring criteria, (6) Sales Rep Forecast: Individual rep forecasts, quota attainment, historical accuracy, and capacity planning, (7) Product/Service Mix: Forecast by product line, service type, or solution category, (8) Customer Segmentation: Forecast by customer segment, new vs. existing customers, and expansion revenue, (9) Risk Assessment: Best case, expected case, and worst case scenarios, risk factors, and contingency planning, (10) Forecast Accuracy: How to measure accuracy, historical accuracy rates, and improvement strategies, (11) Reporting Structure: Forecast dashboard, key metrics, and communication cadence. Consider [SALES CYCLE LENGTH] and [BUSINESS MODEL].

variations.short: Create a sales forecast model using [METHODOLOGY] with pipeline analysis, probability framework, and scenarios.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive sales forecast model including: comprehensive methodology selection, extensive data integration framework, detailed pipeline analysis with advanced analytics, historical trend analysis with predictive modeling, sophisticated probability framework, individual rep forecasting, product mix analysis, customer segmentation, risk modeling with Monte Carlo simulation, accuracy measurement system, and comprehensive reporting dashboard.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Forecast methodology (50 words), (2) Probability by stage (5 stages), (3) Key assumptions (5 items), (4) Risk scenarios (best/expected/worst). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Use historical data to inform probabilities. Regularly update forecasts based on actual performance. Include both quantitative and qualitative factors in your model.

title: Account Plan Builder
primary_use_case: Develop strategic account plans for key customers
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive account plan for [ACCOUNT NAME] to drive growth and retention. The plan should include: (1) Account Overview: Company background, industry, size, revenue, key business initiatives, and strategic priorities, (2) Stakeholder Map: Key decision makers, influencers, champions, blockers, their roles, relationships, and influence levels, (3) Current State Analysis: Current products/services used, usage levels, satisfaction scores, contract value, renewal date, and relationship health, (4) Opportunity Assessment: Expansion opportunities (upsell, cross-sell), new use cases, additional departments, and growth potential, (5) Goals and Objectives: Account goals for [TIMEFRAME], revenue targets, expansion targets, and success metrics, (6) Relationship Strategy: How to strengthen relationships with key stakeholders, engagement plan, and communication cadence, (7) Value Delivery Plan: How to demonstrate ongoing value, success metrics, ROI tracking, and business reviews, (8) Competitive Landscape: Current competitors in account, competitive threats, and differentiation strategy, (9) Action Plan: Specific activities, owners, timelines, and milestones for [QUARTER/YEAR], (10) Risk Assessment: Churn risks, competitive threats, budget constraints, and mitigation strategies, (11) Success Metrics: KPIs to track (revenue growth, NPS, usage, engagement), and (12) Review Cadence: Regular plan review schedule and update process. Consider [ACCOUNT HISTORY] and [COMPANY PRIORITIES].

variations.short: Create an account plan for [ACCOUNT] including stakeholder map, opportunities, goals, and action plan.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive account plan including: comprehensive account intelligence, detailed stakeholder mapping with relationship analysis, complete current state assessment, extensive opportunity identification, strategic goals with OKRs, relationship building strategy, value delivery framework, competitive analysis, detailed action plan with milestones, risk mitigation plan, success metrics dashboard, and regular review process.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Top 5 stakeholders with roles, (2) Top 3 opportunities, (3) Goals (3 items), (4) Action plan (5 activities). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Involve the customer in plan development. Focus on their business outcomes, not just your products. Regularly update plans based on account changes.

title: Proposal Pricing Strategy
primary_use_case: Develop pricing strategies for sales proposals and quotes
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive proposal pricing strategy for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] when responding to [PROSPECT TYPE] requests. The strategy should include: (1) Pricing Objectives: Goals (maximize revenue, win deal, establish value), target margin, and pricing philosophy, (2) Pricing Model Options: Different pricing approaches (per user, per feature, value-based, tiered, usage-based), when to use each, and pros/cons, (3) Base Pricing Structure: Standard pricing tiers, package options, add-on products/services, and pricing components, (4) Value-Based Pricing Framework: How to price based on customer value and ROI, value calculation methodology, and ROI demonstration, (5) Discount Strategy: When to discount, discount approval levels, maximum discount thresholds, and discount justification, (6) Proposal Structure: How to present pricing (total cost, cost breakdown, ROI analysis, payment terms), pricing presentation best practices, and value framing, (7) Negotiation Preparation: Pricing negotiation ranges, concessions strategy, trade-offs, and walk-away points, (8) Competitive Pricing: How pricing compares to [COMPETITOR 1], [COMPETITOR 2], and positioning strategy, (9) Payment Terms: Payment options (upfront, monthly, annual), payment terms, and incentives for longer commitments, (10) Pricing Scenarios: Different pricing options for different deal sizes, use cases, and customer segments, (11) Approval Process: Who approves pricing, approval workflow, and documentation requirements. Consider [PRODUCT COSTS] and [MARKET CONDITIONS].

variations.short: Create a pricing strategy for [PRODUCT] including pricing models, discount strategy, and proposal structure.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive pricing strategy including: comprehensive pricing objectives, detailed pricing model analysis, complete base pricing structure, sophisticated value-based pricing framework, extensive discount strategy, proposal presentation guide, negotiation playbook, competitive pricing analysis, payment terms optimization, pricing scenario modeling, and approval workflow.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Pricing model recommendation (50 words), (2) Base pricing (3 tiers), (3) Discount strategy (3 rules), (4) Proposal structure (5 elements). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Price based on value, not cost. Present pricing with ROI justification. Have a clear discount strategy to avoid unnecessary price erosion.

title: Customer Success Playbook
primary_use_case: Develop customer success strategies and playbooks
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive customer success playbook for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] to ensure customer satisfaction, retention, and growth. The playbook should include: (1) Customer Success Philosophy: Core principles, success definition, and role of customer success, (2) Customer Journey Mapping: Key stages (onboarding, adoption, expansion, renewal), milestones, touchpoints, and success criteria for each stage, (3) Onboarding Playbook: Welcome process, setup steps, training plan, success milestones, and time-to-value targets, (4) Adoption Strategy: How to drive product adoption, feature adoption goals, usage benchmarks, and adoption campaigns, (5) Health Scoring: Customer health score framework, risk indicators, health score calculation, and early warning signals, (6) Engagement Framework: Regular touchpoint schedule, communication cadence, business review process, and value demonstration, (7) Expansion Opportunities: How to identify expansion opportunities, upsell/cross-sell triggers, expansion playbooks, and expansion targets, (8) Renewal Strategy: Renewal process, renewal timeline, risk mitigation, and retention tactics, (9) At-Risk Management: How to identify at-risk customers, intervention playbooks, escalation process, and recovery strategies, (10) Success Metrics: Key metrics (NPS, CSAT, retention rate, expansion rate, product adoption), tracking methods, and reporting, (11) Playbook by Customer Segment: Different approaches for [SEGMENT 1], [SEGMENT 2], and [SEGMENT 3]. Consider [PRODUCT COMPLEXITY] and [CUSTOMER TYPE].

variations.short: Create a customer success playbook including onboarding, adoption, health scoring, and renewal strategies.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive customer success playbook including: comprehensive philosophy and framework, detailed customer journey mapping, complete onboarding playbook, extensive adoption strategy, sophisticated health scoring system, comprehensive engagement framework, detailed expansion playbooks, complete renewal strategy, at-risk management system, success metrics dashboard, segment-specific playbooks, and continuous improvement process.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Onboarding steps (5 steps), (2) Health score factors (5 factors), (3) Engagement cadence (3 touchpoints), (4) Success metrics (5 metrics). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Focus on customer outcomes, not just product usage. Proactively identify and address risks. Measure what matters to customers, not just what's easy to track.

title: Support Ticket Response Templates
primary_use_case: Create templates for common customer support scenarios
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive library of customer support ticket response templates for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] covering common scenarios. The templates should include: (1) Template Structure: Greeting, acknowledgment, solution/response, next steps, closing, and signature, (2) Common Issue Categories: Technical issues ([ISSUE TYPE 1], [ISSUE TYPE 2]), billing questions, account access, feature requests, and general inquiries, (3) Response Templates: For each category, provide templates including (a) initial response acknowledging the issue, (b) troubleshooting steps if applicable, (c) resolution or next steps, (d) follow-up if needed, and (e) escalation template if issue cannot be resolved, (4) Tone Guidelines: Empathetic, helpful, professional tone with [BRAND VOICE] characteristics, (5) Personalization Placeholders: [CUSTOMER NAME], [ISSUE DETAILS], [RESOLUTION STEPS], [TICKET NUMBER], and other customizable fields, (6) Escalation Templates: When and how to escalate, escalation communication templates, and handoff notes, (7) Follow-Up Templates: Thank you messages, satisfaction surveys, and check-in messages, (8) Multi-Channel Adaptations: Email templates, chat templates, and social media response templates, (9) Quality Standards: Response time expectations, resolution targets, and quality checklist, (10) Template Usage Guidelines: When to use templates vs. custom responses, customization best practices, and approval process. Templates should reflect [SUPPORT PHILOSOPHY].

variations.short: Create support response templates for [TOP 5 ISSUE TYPES] with personalized placeholders.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive template library including: comprehensive template structure, extensive issue categorization, complete response templates for all scenarios, tone guidelines, personalization framework, escalation templates, follow-up templates, multi-channel adaptations, quality standards, usage guidelines, and template management process.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY templates for [ISSUE TYPE]. Format: Subject: [SUBJECT], Body: [150 words with placeholders], Closing: [CLOSING]. Maximum 200 words per template.

tips: Always personalize templates - never send templated responses as-is. Use templates as starting points and customize based on the specific situation. Maintain empathy and helpfulness.

title: Customer Escalation Handling Guide
primary_use_case: Develop processes and scripts for handling escalated customer issues
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive customer escalation handling guide for [COMPANY NAME] support team. The guide should include: (1) Escalation Criteria: When to escalate (severity levels, customer type, issue type, business impact), escalation triggers, and escalation matrix, (2) Escalation Process: Step-by-step escalation workflow, who to escalate to ([ESCALATION LEVEL 1], [ESCALATION LEVEL 2]), notification process, and timeline expectations, (3) Initial Response: How to acknowledge escalation, empathy statements, commitment to resolution, and setting expectations, (4) Investigation Framework: How to gather information, questions to ask, documentation requirements, and root cause analysis, (5) Communication Plan: How to communicate with customer during escalation, update frequency, communication channels, and status updates, (6) Resolution Strategies: Common resolution approaches, compensation options, goodwill gestures, and resolution approval process, (7) Escalation Scripts: Phone call scripts, email templates, and meeting agendas for escalated situations, (8) Stakeholder Management: How to involve internal stakeholders (product, engineering, management), communication with stakeholders, and coordination, (9) Post-Resolution: Follow-up process, customer satisfaction check, lessons learned, and process improvement, (10) Escalation Prevention: How to prevent escalations, early warning signs, proactive intervention, and training, (11) Escalation Tracking: How to track escalations, metrics to monitor, and reporting. Consider [ESCALATION HISTORY] and [CUSTOMER EXPECTATIONS].

variations.short: Create an escalation guide with criteria, process, response scripts, and resolution strategies.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive escalation guide including: comprehensive escalation criteria and matrix, detailed escalation workflow, complete initial response framework, extensive investigation methodology, comprehensive communication plan, resolution strategy playbook, escalation scripts and templates, stakeholder management framework, post-resolution process, escalation prevention strategies, and tracking system.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Escalation criteria (5 triggers), (2) Escalation process (5 steps), (3) Initial response script (100 words), (4) Resolution strategies (3 options). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Respond quickly to escalations. Show empathy and take ownership. Keep customers informed throughout the process. Learn from each escalation to prevent future ones.

title: Help Center Article Generator
primary_use_case: Create help center articles and knowledge base content
prompt_text: Generate a comprehensive help center article for [TOPIC] related to [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME]. The article should include: (1) Article Structure: Clear title, introduction, step-by-step instructions, screenshots/visuals placeholders, troubleshooting section, related articles, and last updated date, (2) Introduction: What the article covers, who it's for, prerequisites, and expected outcome, (3) Step-by-Step Instructions: Numbered steps with clear actions, expected results, and visual cues ([SCREENSHOT 1], [SCREENSHOT 2]), (4) Detailed Explanations: Why each step matters, what users should expect, and common variations, (5) Troubleshooting Section: Common issues users might encounter, error messages and solutions, workarounds, and when to contact support, (6) Best Practices: Tips for optimal results, recommendations, and related features to explore, (7) Visual Elements: Where screenshots, diagrams, or videos should be placed, alt text suggestions, and visual descriptions, (8) SEO Optimization: Keywords to include, meta description, and search optimization, (9) User-Friendly Language: Clear, simple language avoiding jargon, explanations of technical terms, and examples, (10) Related Content: Links to related articles, related features, and next steps, (11) Feedback Mechanism: How users can provide feedback, report issues, or request updates. The article should be written for [USER SKILL LEVEL] users.

variations.short: Create a help article for [TOPIC] with introduction, step-by-step instructions, and troubleshooting.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive help article including: comprehensive structure, detailed introduction, extensive step-by-step instructions with visuals, troubleshooting guide, best practices, visual element specifications, SEO optimization, user-friendly language guidelines, related content mapping, feedback mechanism, and article maintenance process.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Title and intro (50 words), (2) Steps (5 numbered steps, 20 words each), (3) Troubleshooting (3 issues with solutions), (4) Related articles (3 links). Maximum 250 words.

tips: Write for your least technical user. Use clear headings and short paragraphs. Include screenshots and examples. Test articles with real users and update based on feedback.

title: Churn Prevention Strategy
primary_use_case: Develop strategies to prevent customer churn and improve retention
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive churn prevention strategy for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] to reduce customer attrition and improve retention. The strategy should include: (1) Churn Analysis: Historical churn patterns, churn reasons analysis, customer segments with highest churn, and churn timing patterns, (2) Early Warning System: Customer health indicators, risk signals ([RISK SIGNAL 1], [RISK SIGNAL 2]), predictive churn models, and monitoring dashboards, (3) At-Risk Customer Identification: How to identify at-risk customers, risk scoring methodology, risk categories, and alert triggers, (4) Intervention Playbooks: Specific playbooks for different risk levels (low, medium, high), intervention steps, outreach templates, and success criteria, (5) Root Cause Analysis: Common churn reasons (price, product fit, poor experience, competition), how to identify root causes, and prevention strategies, (6) Retention Tactics: Win-back campaigns, discount offers, feature enablement, success manager assignment, and value reinforcement, (7) Proactive Engagement: Regular check-ins, value reviews, feature adoption campaigns, and success milestones, (8) Product Improvements: Product gaps leading to churn, feature requests from churned customers, and product roadmap priorities, (9) Customer Feedback: How to collect feedback from at-risk customers, feedback analysis, and action planning, (10) Success Metrics: Churn rate, retention rate, customer lifetime value, intervention success rate, and time-to-intervention, (11) Continuous Improvement: Regular strategy review, A/B testing of interventions, and optimization based on results. Consider [CUSTOMER BASE] and [CHURN HISTORY].

variations.short: Create a churn prevention strategy with early warning signals, intervention playbooks, and retention tactics.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive churn prevention strategy including: comprehensive churn analysis, sophisticated early warning system, detailed at-risk identification framework, extensive intervention playbooks, root cause analysis methodology, comprehensive retention tactics, proactive engagement framework, product improvement recommendations, customer feedback system, success metrics dashboard, and continuous improvement process.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Top 5 churn indicators, (2) Intervention playbook (3 steps), (3) Retention tactics (3 tactics), (4) Success metrics (5 metrics). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Prevent churn before it happens by identifying at-risk customers early. Address root causes, not just symptoms. Personalize interventions based on why customers are at risk.

title: Customer Feedback Synthesis
primary_use_case: Analyze and synthesize customer feedback into actionable insights
prompt_text: Synthesize customer feedback from [FEEDBACK SOURCES] for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] into actionable insights. The synthesis should include: (1) Feedback Collection Overview: Sources analyzed (surveys, support tickets, reviews, interviews, NPS comments), time period ([DATE RANGE]), volume of feedback, and collection methods, (2) Feedback Categorization: Themes and categories identified ([THEME 1], [THEME 2], [THEME 3]), sentiment analysis (positive, negative, neutral), and priority classification, (3) Key Insights: Major findings, patterns, trends, and surprising discoveries, (4) Pain Points: Top customer pain points, frequency of mentions, impact on experience, and affected customer segments, (5) Positive Feedback: What customers love, strengths to leverage, success stories, and positive trends, (6) Feature Requests: Most requested features, request frequency, potential impact, and feasibility assessment, (7) Sentiment Analysis: Overall sentiment score, sentiment trends over time, sentiment by customer segment, and sentiment by product area, (8) Customer Quotes: Representative quotes for each theme, powerful testimonials, and concerning feedback, (9) Actionable Recommendations: Prioritized recommendations for product improvements, service enhancements, and process changes, (10) Impact Assessment: Potential impact of addressing feedback, effort required, and ROI estimates, (11) Follow-Up Plan: How to validate insights, additional research needed, and communication plan. Analyze feedback from [NUMBER] customers.

variations.short: Synthesize customer feedback identifying top themes, pain points, and actionable recommendations.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive feedback synthesis including: comprehensive feedback collection overview, detailed categorization with sentiment analysis, extensive key insights with trend analysis, complete pain point analysis, positive feedback compilation, feature request prioritization, sophisticated sentiment analysis, representative customer quotes, prioritized actionable recommendations, impact assessment, and follow-up plan.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Top 3 themes with frequency, (2) Top 3 pain points, (3) Top 3 recommendations, (4) Overall sentiment score. Maximum 300 words.

tips: Look for patterns, not just individual comments. Quantify feedback when possible. Prioritize based on impact and frequency. Share insights with relevant teams.

title: Upsell/Cross-sell Strategy
primary_use_case: Develop strategies for upselling and cross-selling to existing customers
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive upsell and cross-sell strategy for [PRODUCT/SERVICE NAME] to increase revenue from existing customers. The strategy should include: (1) Strategy Objectives: Goals (increase ARPU, expand accounts, increase LTV), revenue targets, and success metrics, (2) Opportunity Identification: How to identify upsell/cross-sell opportunities, trigger events ([TRIGGER 1], [TRIGGER 2]), customer signals, and ideal customer profiles, (3) Product/Service Mapping: Upsell opportunities (upgrade to higher tier, add users, add features), cross-sell opportunities (related products, complementary services), and product bundles, (4) Customer Segmentation: Which customers are best candidates, segmentation criteria, and approach by segment, (5) Timing Strategy: When to approach customers (usage milestones, contract renewal, feature requests), optimal timing, and timing to avoid, (6) Value Proposition: How to frame upsells/cross-sells in terms of customer value, ROI justification, and benefit articulation, (7) Sales Approach: How to present offers, conversation frameworks, objection handling, and closing techniques, (8) Pricing Strategy: Pricing for upgrades, discount strategies, payment terms, and value-based pricing, (9) Campaign Framework: Automated campaigns, personalized outreach, in-app messaging, and sales-led approaches, (10) Success Metrics: Upsell rate, cross-sell rate, expansion revenue, average deal size, and conversion rates, (11) Implementation Plan: Rollout plan, team training, tools needed, and timeline. Consider [CUSTOMER BASE] and [PRODUCT PORTFOLIO].

variations.short: Create an upsell/cross-sell strategy with opportunity identification, timing, value propositions, and success metrics.
variations.detailed: Develop an exhaustive upsell/cross-sell strategy including: comprehensive objectives, detailed opportunity identification framework, complete product/service mapping, customer segmentation analysis, sophisticated timing strategy, value proposition development, complete sales approach, pricing strategy, campaign framework, success metrics dashboard, and implementation plan.
variations.strict: Generate ONLY: (1) Top 3 upsell opportunities, (2) Top 3 cross-sell opportunities, (3) Timing strategy (3 triggers), (4) Success metrics (5 metrics). Maximum 300 words.

tips: Focus on customer value, not just revenue. Time offers based on customer needs and milestones. Make upsells/cross-sells feel like natural next steps, not sales pitches.

title: Interview Question Generator
primary_use_case: Generate structured interview questions for job candidates
prompt_text: Generate a comprehensive set of interview questions for a [job_title] position in the [industry] industry. The candidate should have [years_of_experience] years of experience and possess skills in [key_skills]. Create questions that assess [assessment_criteria] including technical competency, cultural fit, problem-solving abilities, and communication skills. Include [number_of_questions] questions total, divided into categories: behavioral questions (using STAR method), technical questions specific to [technical_domain], situational questions relevant to [work_scenarios], and questions about [company_values]. Each question should be designed to reveal the candidate's [specific_qualities] and ability to handle [challenge_types]. Format the questions with clear instructions for interviewers on what to look for in responses and how to evaluate answers using a [rating_scale] point scale.

variations.short: Create [number] interview questions for [job_title] focusing on [key_skills].
variations.detailed: Develop a comprehensive interview question bank for a [job_title] role requiring [years_of_experience] years of experience in [industry]. Include behavioral questions using STAR methodology, technical questions covering [technical_areas], situational scenarios involving [common_challenges], and culture-fit questions aligned with [company_values]. Provide evaluation rubrics, sample ideal answers, and red flags to watch for. Organize questions by interview round (phone screen, technical, final) and include follow-up probing questions.
variations.strict: Generate exactly [number] interview questions for [job_title] position. Requirements: [number] behavioral (STAR format), [number] technical ([specific_technologies]), [number] situational ([scenarios]). Each question must include: question text, evaluation criteria, ideal answer components, and rating scale (1-5). No questions about [prohibited_topics]. Format as JSON with categories.

tips: Customize questions based on your company's values and the specific role requirements. Include a mix of open-ended and scenario-based questions. Always ensure questions comply with employment law and avoid discriminatory topics.

title: Employee Handbook Section Writer
primary_use_case: Create comprehensive employee handbook sections
user_role: HR Director, Legal Counsel, Operations Manager
prompt_text: Write a comprehensive employee handbook section covering [policy_topic] for [company_name], a [company_type] operating in [industry] with [number_of_employees] employees located in [jurisdiction]. The section should include: an introduction explaining the purpose and scope of [policy_topic], detailed policy statements covering [specific_policy_areas], procedures for [implementation_steps], employee responsibilities and expectations regarding [employee_obligations], consequences for policy violations including [disciplinary_actions], and contact information for questions about [policy_topic]. The language should be clear, professional, and compliant with [applicable_laws] including [specific_regulations]. Include examples of [acceptable_behaviors] and [unacceptable_behaviors]. The tone should be [tone_style] while maintaining legal accuracy. Ensure the section aligns with our company values of [company_values] and supports our commitment to [organizational_goals].

variations.short: Write an employee handbook section on [policy_topic] for [company_type].
variations.detailed: Create a comprehensive employee handbook section for [policy_topic] that includes: executive summary, policy statement, detailed procedures, roles and responsibilities, compliance requirements under [laws], examples and scenarios, frequently asked questions, revision history, and approval signatures. Tailor for [industry] industry, [jurisdiction] jurisdiction, and [company_size] organization. Include legal disclaimers, cross-references to related policies, and implementation timeline.
variations.strict: Generate employee handbook section on [policy_topic]. Must include: [required_sections]. Word count: [number] words minimum. Must reference [specific_laws]. Format: [format_requirements]. Tone: [tone]. Prohibited content: [restrictions]. Include [mandatory_disclaimers].

tips: Always have legal counsel review handbook sections before publication. Use clear, jargon-free language. Include specific examples and scenarios. Ensure compliance with local, state, and federal employment laws.

title: Compensation Benchmarking Analysis
primary_use_case: Analyze and benchmark compensation against market rates
prompt_text: Conduct a comprehensive compensation benchmarking analysis for [job_titles] positions at [company_name] in the [industry] industry. Analyze compensation data including base salary ranges of [$min_range] to [$max_range], bonus structures averaging [bonus_percentage]%, equity compensation of [equity_details], and total compensation packages. Compare our current compensation against market data from [data_sources] for [geographic_markets] markets, considering factors such as [company_size] company size, [revenue_range] revenue range, [funding_stage] stage, and [years_in_business] years in operation. Evaluate compensation competitiveness using [percentile_analysis] percentile analysis (25th, 50th, 75th, 90th percentiles). Assess internal equity by comparing compensation across [departments] departments and [experience_levels] experience levels. Identify [compensation_gaps] gaps where our pay is below market by [percentage]% or more, and areas where we may be overpaying. Provide recommendations for [adjustment_strategies] including merit increases, market adjustments, and retention bonuses. Consider [budget_constraints] budget constraints and [retention_priorities] retention priorities. Include a risk assessment of [turnover_risks] if compensation remains uncompetitive.

variations.short: Benchmark compensation for [job_title] in [location] against market rates.
variations.detailed: Perform an in-depth compensation benchmarking analysis covering: market data collection from [sources], statistical analysis (mean, median, percentiles), internal equity review, external competitiveness assessment, pay gap identification, total rewards comparison (base, variable, equity, benefits), cost modeling for adjustments, risk analysis for retention, multi-year trend analysis, and strategic recommendations with implementation timeline and budget impact. title: Product-Market Fit Assessment
primary_use_case: Evaluate product-market fit using quantitative and qualitative metrics
prompt_text: Conduct a comprehensive product-market fit assessment for [product_name] using multiple frameworks and data sources. The assessment should include: Sean Ellis Test Results analyzing survey responses to 'How would you feel if you could no longer use [product_name]?' with target of 40%+ answering 'Very disappointed', including breakdown by user segment ([segment_1], [segment_2]) and analysis of why users would be disappointed; Retention Cohort Analysis examining Day 1, Day 7, Day 30, and Day 90 retention rates, identifying retention curves, power user patterns, and churn indicators, with benchmarks against industry standards for [industry_type]; Net Promoter Score (NPS) Analysis calculating NPS from customer surveys, segmenting promoters ([nps_score_1]), passives, and detractors, and analyzing feedback themes; Usage Intensity Metrics measuring active users (DAU/MAU ratio), session frequency, feature adoption rates for [feature_1] and [feature_2], and time-to-value indicators; Market Demand Indicators assessing search volume trends for [keyword_1] and [keyword_2], competitive landscape maturity, and early adopter behavior patterns; Customer Acquisition Metrics evaluating CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost) trends, organic vs paid acquisition mix, and viral coefficient if applicable; Revenue Metrics analyzing MRR/ARR growth, revenue per user trends, and expansion revenue from [revenue_stream_1] and [revenue_stream_2]; Qualitative Signals gathering evidence from customer interviews, support tickets, and sales conversations indicating strong product-market fit (e.g., [signal_1], [signal_2]) or lack thereof; Fit Score Calculation providing an overall product-market fit score (0-100) with component scores for Value Proposition ([score_1]), Market Timing ([score_2]), and Execution ([score_3]); Gap Analysis identifying specific areas where product-market fit is weak, such as [gap_1] and [gap_2], with prioritized recommendations; Action Plan outlining steps to improve product-market fit, including product changes ([action_1]), market positioning adjustments ([action_2]), and go-to-market refinements ([action_3]).

tips: Product-market fit is not binary—assess by segment. Track metrics over time. Combine quantitative and qualitative data.

Targeting Rules specifying user segments for gradual rollout, such as users in [region_1], users with [attribute_1], or users in cohort [cohort_1], with exclusion rules for [excluded_segment_1]; Success Criteria defining metrics to monitor during rollout, including [metric_1] (target: [target_1]), [metric_2] (target: [target_2]), error rates (threshold: <[error_threshold]%), and user feedback scores (target: >[feedback_threshold]); Rollback Triggers identifying conditions that would trigger immediate rollback, such as error rate exceeding [rollback_error_rate]%, critical bug discovery ([bug_severity]), or negative impact on [critical_metric] exceeding [impact_threshold]%; title: Customer Feedback Prioritizer

prompt_text: Create a systematic framework for prioritizing customer feedback and feature requests for [product_name]. The framework should include: Feedback Collection Sources identifying where feedback comes from, such as support tickets ([ticket_system]), user interviews ([interview_count] interviews), surveys ([survey_response_rate]% response rate), in-app feedback ([feedback_widget]), app store reviews ([review_platform]), and sales conversations ([sales_notes]); Feedback Categorization organizing requests into themes like [theme_1] (usability improvements), [theme_2] (new features), [theme_3] (bug fixes), [theme_4] (performance), and [theme_5] (integrations), with subcategories for each theme; Scoring Framework applying weighted criteria: User Impact Score (1-10) based on number of users affected ([user_count]), frequency of request ([request_frequency]), and user segment importance ([segment_value]); Business Impact Score (1-10) considering revenue potential ([revenue_impact]), retention impact ([retention_impact]), competitive advantage ([competitive_value]), and strategic alignment ([strategic_alignment]); Effort Score (1-10) estimating development complexity ([complexity_level]), time required ([time_estimate]), resource needs ([resource_requirements]), and technical dependencies ([dependencies]); Priority Calculation using formula: Priority Score = (User Impact × [weight_1] + Business Impact × [weight_2] - Effort × [weight_3]) / 10, with weights [weight_1], [weight_2], [weight_3] reflecting organizational priorities; Request Details for each prioritized item including original feedback source ([source_1]), user quotes ([quote_1], [quote_2]), affected user segments ([segment_1], [segment_2]), and business context ([business_context]); Implementation Roadmap mapping high-priority items ([priority_item_1], [priority_item_2]) to upcoming sprints or quarters, considering dependencies and resource availability; Communication Plan outlining how customers will be informed about prioritization decisions, including public roadmap updates ([roadmap_url]), direct responses to feedback ([response_template]), and feature announcement strategy ([announcement_plan]); title: MVP Scope Definer
primary_use_case: Define minimum viable product scope and boundaries

The scope definition should include: Product Vision Statement articulating the core value proposition ([value_proposition]) and target user problem ([user_problem]) that the MVP addresses; Success Criteria defining what 'viable' means with measurable outcomes: user validation ([validation_metric] users validate [hypothesis]), engagement threshold ([engagement_target]), and learning objectives ([learning_goal_1], [learning_goal_2]); Core User Journey mapping the essential path from [entry_point] to [value_moment], identifying the minimum steps required: [step_1], [step_2], [step_3], and [step_4], excluding nice-to-have features; Must-Have Features listing only features critical for value delivery: [must_have_feature_1] (enables [outcome_1]), [must_have_feature_2] (enables [outcome_2]), and [must_have_feature_3] (enables [outcome_3]), with clear rationale for inclusion; Explicitly Out-of-Scope Features documenting what will NOT be included in MVP, such as [out_of_scope_1], [out_of_scope_2], and [out_of_scope_3], with reasoning and future consideration timeline; Technical Constraints defining minimum technical requirements: platform support ([platform_1] only, [platform_2] deferred), performance targets ([performance_minimum]), scalability limits ([user_limit] users), and integration scope ([integration_1] required, [integration_2] deferred); Design Scope specifying design fidelity level ([fidelity_level]), user experience polish level ([polish_level]), and accessibility baseline ([accessibility_level]); Timeline and Resources estimating MVP development timeline ([timeline_estimate]), team size ([team_size]), and budget constraints ([budget_limit]); Post-MVP Roadmap providing high-level view of what comes after MVP: Phase 2 features ([phase2_feature_1], [phase2_feature_2]) and Phase 3 features ([phase3_feature_1]), with prioritization rationale.

Communication Strategy detailing messages for different audiences: user announcements ([announcement_channels]), in-app notifications ([notification_timing]), email campaigns ([email_schedule]), support documentation ([support_docs_url]), and direct outreach to power users ([power_user_outreach]); Risk Mitigation identifying potential issues ([risk_1], [risk_2]) with mitigation strategies ([mitigation_1], [mitigation_2]) and rollback procedures if needed ([rollback_plan]); Success Metrics defining how deprecation success will be measured: migration completion rate ([target_migration_rate]%), user satisfaction ([satisfaction_target]), and support ticket volume ([ticket_threshold]); title: Technical Debt Prioritizer
primary_use_case: Prioritize technical debt and refactoring work
prompt_text: Create a systematic framework for prioritizing technical debt items for [product_name] that balances engineering health with product delivery. The framework should include: Debt Inventory cataloging technical debt items: [debt_item_1] (type: [debt_type_1], location: [code_location_1]), [debt_item_2] (type: [debt_type_2], location: [code_location_2]), and [debt_item_3] (type: [debt_type_3], location: [code_location_3]), with descriptions of the debt and its origins; Impact Assessment evaluating each debt item on multiple dimensions: Development Velocity Impact (1-10) measuring how debt slows feature development ([velocity_impact_1], [velocity_impact_2]), Bug Risk (1-10) assessing likelihood of bugs ([bug_risk_1], [bug_risk_2]), Maintenance Cost (1-10) evaluating ongoing maintenance burden ([maintenance_cost_1], [maintenance_cost_2]), and Scalability Risk (1-10) assessing growth limitations ([scalability_risk_1], [scalability_risk_2]); Effort Estimation for addressing each debt item: time required ([time_estimate_1], [time_estimate_2]), team skills needed ([required_skills_1], [required_skills_2]), complexity level ([complexity_level_1], [complexity_level_2]), and dependencies ([dependency_1], [dependency_2]); Business Impact considering how debt affects product: user-facing issues ([user_impact_1], [user_impact_2]), revenue risk ([revenue_risk_1]), compliance concerns ([compliance_risk_1]), and security vulnerabilities ([security_risk_1]); Priority Scoring using weighted formula: Priority Score = (Impact Score × [impact_weight] - Effort Score × [effort_weight]) / 10, where Impact Score combines velocity, bug risk, maintenance, and scalability impacts, with weights [impact_weight] and [effort_weight] reflecting team priorities; Debt Categories organizing items into groups: Critical ([critical_debt_1], [critical_debt_2]) requiring immediate attention, High Priority ([high_priority_debt_1]) affecting near-term goals, Medium Priority ([medium_priority_debt_1]) for planned refactoring, and Low Priority ([low_priority_debt_1]) for future consideration; Refactoring Strategy outlining approach for high-priority items: incremental refactoring ([incremental_approach]), big bang rewrite ([rewrite_approach]), or gradual migration ([migration_approach]), with rationale; Integration with Product Roadmap showing how debt work fits into sprints: Sprint [sprint_number] allocating [debt_percentage]% capacity to [debt_item_1], balancing with feature work; Success Metrics defining how debt reduction success will be measured: code quality metrics ([quality_metric_1], [quality_metric_2]), velocity improvements ([velocity_improvement_target]), and bug reduction ([bug_reduction_target]); Prevention Strategy outlining practices to prevent future debt: code review standards ([review_standards]), architecture decisions ([architecture_process]), and technical spike allocation ([spike_allocation]).

title: User Flow Mapper
primary_use_case: Map user flows and journey paths
prompt_text: Map the complete user flow for [user_goal] in [product_name], identifying all steps, decision points, and outcomes. The flow map should include: Flow Overview defining the primary user goal ([user_goal]), starting point ([entry_point]), and desired outcome ([desired_outcome]); Step-by-Step Flow detailing each stage: Step 1 ([step1_action]) leading to [step1_outcome], Step 2 ([step2_action]) with decision point ([decision_point_1]), Step 3 ([step3_action]) branching based on [decision_criteria], Step 4 ([step4_action]), and Step 5 ([step5_action]) reaching [final_outcome]; Touchpoints listing all interactions: screens ([screen_1], [screen_2], [screen_3]), forms ([form_1], [form_2]), notifications ([notification_1], [notification_2]), and external systems ([external_system_1]); User Emotions and Pain Points identifying feelings at each stage: frustration points ([friction_point_1], [friction_point_2]), moments of delight ([delight_moment_1], [delight_moment_2]), and anxiety triggers ([anxiety_trigger_1]); Technical Requirements noting system needs: data collection ([data_collection_points]), validation ([validation_points]), integrations ([integration_points]), and error handling ([error_handling_requirements]); title: Information Architecture Planner
primary_use_case: Plan information architecture and navigation structure
prompt_text: Design the information architecture for [product_name] that organizes content logically and supports user goals. The IA plan should include: IA Goals defining what the architecture should achieve: findability ([findability_goal]), usability ([usability_goal]), and scalability ([scalability_goal]); Content Inventory cataloging all content types: pages ([page_type_1], [page_type_2], [page_type_3]), features ([feature_1], [feature_2], [feature_3]), content sections ([content_section_1], [content_section_2]), and functional areas ([functional_area_1], [functional_area_2]); User Mental Models analyzing how users think about the product: user expectations ([user_expectation_1], [user_expectation_2]), industry conventions ([industry_convention_1]), and cognitive load considerations ([cognitive_load_consideration]); Primary Navigation Structure defining top-level categories: Category 1 ([category1_name]) containing [category1_items], Category 2 ([category2_name]) containing [category2_items], Category 3 ([category3_name]) containing [category3_items], with rationale for each grouping; Secondary Navigation outlining sub-navigation patterns: breadcrumbs ([breadcrumb_usage]), sidebars ([sidebar_navigation]), footer navigation ([footer_navigation]), and contextual navigation ([contextual_nav]); Content Hierarchy establishing information priority: primary content ([primary_content]), secondary content ([secondary_content]), and tertiary content ([tertiary_content]), with visual hierarchy implications; Labeling Strategy defining naming conventions: primary labels ([primary_label_1], [primary_label_2], [primary_label_3]), alternative labels considered ([alternative_label_1], [alternative_label_2]), and terminology consistency ([terminology_standard]); User Flows Through IA mapping how users navigate to complete tasks: Flow 1 ([flow1_goal]) via [flow1_path], Flow 2 ([flow2_goal]) via [flow2_path], Flow 3 ([flow3_goal]) via [flow3_path], identifying optimal paths; Search and Discovery strategies for helping users find content: search functionality ([search_implementation]), filters ([filter_categories]), tags ([tag_system]), and recommendations ([recommendation_engine]); Mobile IA Considerations adapting structure for mobile: navigation patterns ([mobile_nav_pattern]), content prioritization ([mobile_priority]), and progressive disclosure ([progressive_disclosure_strategy]); Scalability Planning ensuring IA can grow: content categories ([expandable_categories]), new feature integration ([feature_integration_approach]), and maintenance strategy ([maintenance_approach]); Validation Methods outlining how IA will be tested: card sorting ([card_sort_participants]), tree testing ([tree_test_scenarios]), and user testing ([user_test_plan]); title: Color Palette and Typography Advisor
primary_use_case: Recommend color palettes and typography systems
prompt_text: Provide comprehensive color palette and typography recommendations for [product_name] that ensure accessibility, brand alignment, and visual hierarchy. The recommendations should include: Brand Context understanding the product's brand identity ([brand_personality]), target audience ([target_audience]), industry ([industry_type]), and existing brand guidelines ([brand_guidelines_reference]); Color Palette Strategy defining the color system: primary color ([primary_color] with hex #[hex_1], usage: [primary_usage]), secondary colors ([secondary_color_1] #[hex_2], [secondary_color_2] #[hex_3]), accent colors ([accent_color_1] #[hex_4], [accent_color_2] #[hex_5]), neutral grays ([gray_scale] from #[gray_light] to #[gray_dark]), semantic colors for success ([success_color] #[hex_6]), warning ([warning_color] #[hex_7]), error ([error_color] #[hex_8]), and info ([info_color] #[hex_9]); Accessibility Compliance ensuring WCAG AA compliance: contrast ratios for text on backgrounds ([contrast_ratio_1]:1 for [use_case_1], [contrast_ratio_2]:1 for [use_case_2]), color-blind considerations ([colorblind_safe_palette]), and alternative indicators ([alternative_indicators] beyond color alone); Color Usage Guidelines specifying when to use each color: primary for [primary_use_cases], secondary for [secondary_use_cases], semantic colors for [semantic_use_cases], and neutrals for [neutral_use_cases]; Typography System defining font choices: primary font ([primary_font_family]) for [primary_font_usage], secondary font ([secondary_font_family]) for [secondary_font_usage], monospace font ([monospace_font]) for [monospace_usage], and font sources ([font_source_1], [font_source_2]); Type Scale establishing hierarchy: H1 ([h1_size], [h1_weight], [h1_line_height]), H2 ([h2_size], [h2_weight], [h2_line_height]), H3 ([h3_size], [h3_weight], [h3_line_height]), Body ([body_size], [body_weight], [body_line_height]), Small ([small_size], [small_weight], [small_line_height]), and Caption ([caption_size], [caption_weight], [caption_line_height]); Typography Usage Guidelines explaining when to use each level: headings for [heading_usage], body for [body_usage], and small text for [small_text_usage]; Responsive Typography defining how type scales across breakpoints: mobile ([mobile_base_size]), tablet ([tablet_base_size]), and desktop ([desktop_base_size]); Design Tokens providing implementation values: color tokens ([color_token_format]), typography tokens ([typography_token_format]), and spacing tokens ([spacing_token_format]); Implementation Guidance specifying tools and methods: design tool setup ([design_tool_config]), code implementation ([code_implementation_approach]), and documentation ([token_documentation_location]); Testing Recommendations outlining validation methods: contrast testing ([contrast_testing_tool]), readability testing ([readability_testing]), and visual testing ([visual_testing_approach]).

title: Responsive Design Breakpoint Planner
primary_use_case: Plan responsive design breakpoints and layouts
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive responsive design breakpoint strategy for [product_name] that ensures optimal experiences across all devices. The plan should include: Device Landscape Analysis examining target devices: mobile phones ([mobile_range]px width range, [mobile_usage]% of traffic), tablets ([tablet_range]px width range, [tablet_usage]% of traffic), laptops ([laptop_range]px width range, [laptop_usage]% of traffic), and desktops ([desktop_range]px width range, [desktop_usage]% of traffic); Breakpoint Strategy defining breakpoints: Mobile ([mobile_breakpoint]px and below, [mobile_layout_approach]), Tablet Portrait ([tablet_portrait_breakpoint]px, [tablet_portrait_layout]), Tablet Landscape ([tablet_landscape_breakpoint]px, [tablet_landscape_layout]), Desktop Small ([desktop_small_breakpoint]px, [desktop_small_layout]), Desktop Large ([desktop_large_breakpoint]px and above, [desktop_large_layout]); Layout Adaptations specifying how layouts change: navigation ([nav_mobile] on mobile, [nav_desktop] on desktop), content columns ([mobile_columns] columns mobile, [desktop_columns] columns desktop), spacing ([mobile_spacing] mobile, [desktop_spacing] desktop), and typography ([mobile_type_scale] mobile, [desktop_type_scale] desktop); Component Behavior defining responsive components: grid systems ([grid_mobile] mobile, [grid_desktop] desktop), cards ([card_mobile], [card_desktop]), forms ([form_mobile], [form_desktop]), tables ([table_mobile], [table_desktop]), and images ([image_mobile], [image_desktop]); Touch Target Guidelines ensuring mobile usability: minimum touch target size ([touch_target_size]px), spacing between targets ([touch_spacing]px), and gesture support ([gesture_requirements]); Performance Considerations optimizing for mobile: image optimization ([image_strategy]), lazy loading ([lazy_loading_approach]), and code splitting ([code_splitting_strategy]); Testing Strategy outlining device testing: physical devices ([physical_devices_list]), emulators ([emulator_tools]), browser testing ([browser_testing_list]), and orientation testing ([orientation_testing]); Progressive Enhancement approach ensuring core functionality works everywhere: base experience ([base_experience]), enhanced experience ([enhanced_experience]), and feature detection ([feature_detection_approach]); Implementation Guidelines specifying technical approach: CSS approach ([css_methodology] - mobile-first or desktop-first), framework ([css_framework]), and tooling ([build_tools]); Maintenance Plan outlining ongoing optimization: analytics monitoring ([analytics_setup]), A/B testing ([ab_testing_plan]), and iteration strategy ([iteration_approach]).
