title: Onboarding UX Flow Designer
primary_use_case: Design user onboarding experiences
prompt_text: Design a comprehensive onboarding flow for [product_name] that guides new users to their first value moment quickly and effectively. The flow should include: Onboarding Goals defining what success looks like: activation metric ([activation_metric]% complete [activation_action]), time to value ([time_to_value] minutes), and learning objectives ([learning_objective_1], [learning_objective_2], [learning_objective_3]); User Segmentation identifying different user types: [user_type_1] with goals ([goal_1]) needing [onboarding_path_1], [user_type_2] with goals ([goal_2]) needing [onboarding_path_2], and [user_type_3] with goals ([goal_3]) needing [onboarding_path_3]; Welcome Experience creating first impression: welcome screen ([welcome_message]), value proposition ([value_prop_message]), and progress indicator ([progress_indicator_design]); Step-by-Step Flow outlining onboarding stages: Step 1 ([step1_name]) - [step1_description] with [step1_interaction], Step 2 ([step2_name]) - [step2_description] with [step2_interaction], Step 3 ([step3_name]) - [step3_description] with [step3_interaction], Step 4 ([step4_name]) - [step4_description] with [step4_interaction], and Step 5 ([step5_name]) - [step5_description] leading to [first_value_moment]; Progressive Disclosure managing information: essential info first ([essential_info]), advanced features later ([advanced_features]), and contextual help ([contextual_help_locations]); Interactive Elements engaging users: tooltips ([tooltip_locations]), guided tours ([tour_steps]), interactive demos ([demo_interactions]), and checkpoints ([checkpoint_moments]); Personalization Opportunities customizing experience: user preferences ([preference_collection]), use case selection ([use_case_selection]), and personalized recommendations ([personalization_approach]); Friction Reduction minimizing barriers: optional vs required fields ([required_fields_only]), social login ([social_login_options]), and skip options ([skip_opportunities]); Success Moments creating delight: completion celebration ([celebration_moment]), achievement badges ([badge_system]), and next steps guidance ([next_steps_guidance]); Analytics and Measurement tracking progress: completion rates ([completion_tracking]), drop-off points ([dropoff_analysis]), and time metrics ([time_tracking]); Optimization Strategy outlining iteration approach: A/B tests ([ab_test_ideas]), user feedback ([feedback_collection]), and continuous improvement ([improvement_process]).

title: Error State and Empty State Designer
primary_use_case: Design error and empty states for better UX
prompt_text: Design comprehensive error and empty states for [feature/area_name] that turn negative experiences into positive ones. The designs should include: Empty State Strategy defining when users see empty states: first use ([first_use_empty_state]), no results ([no_results_empty_state]), no data ([no_data_empty_state]), and cleared content ([cleared_content_empty_state]); Empty State Components specifying elements: illustration or icon ([empty_illustration]), headline ([empty_headline]), description ([empty_description]), and primary CTA ([empty_cta] with action [empty_action]); Error State Categories organizing error types: validation errors ([validation_error_design]), system errors ([system_error_design]), network errors ([network_error_design]), permission errors ([permission_error_design]), and not found errors ([not_found_error_design]); Error State Components defining elements: error icon ([error_icon]), error message ([error_message_format]), explanation ([error_explanation]), and recovery actions ([recovery_action_1], [recovery_action_2]); Tone and Messaging establishing voice: empty states ([empty_state_tone] - helpful and encouraging), error states ([error_state_tone] - clear and supportive), avoiding blame ([no_blame_language]), and providing guidance ([guidance_language]); Visual Design specifying appearance: empty state visuals ([empty_visual_style]), error state visuals ([error_visual_style]), color usage ([error_color_scheme]), and iconography ([icon_style]); Actionable Guidance providing next steps: empty state actions ([empty_state_cta_1], [empty_state_cta_2]), error recovery ([error_recovery_steps]), and help resources ([help_resources]); Contextual Help offering assistance: tooltips ([help_tooltips]), links to docs ([documentation_links]), and support contact ([support_options]); Micro-interactions adding polish: loading states ([loading_animation]), error animations ([error_animation]), and success feedback ([success_feedback]); Accessibility ensuring inclusive design: error announcements ([screen_reader_announcements]), focus management ([focus_handling]), and color contrast ([contrast_compliance]); Testing Strategy validating designs: user testing ([usability_testing]), error scenario testing ([error_testing]), and empty state testing ([empty_state_testing]).

title: Notification Strategy Designer
primary_use_case: Design notification systems and communication strategies
prompt_text: Design a comprehensive notification strategy for [product_name] that keeps users informed without overwhelming them. The strategy should include: Notification Goals defining objectives: user engagement ([engagement_goal]), information delivery ([information_goal]), and action prompting ([action_goal]); Notification Types categorizing messages: transactional ([transactional_examples] - order confirmations, receipts), promotional ([promotional_examples] - offers, updates), system ([system_examples] - maintenance, outages), and social ([social_examples] - mentions, comments); Channel Strategy selecting delivery methods: in-app notifications ([in_app_usage]), email ([email_usage]), push notifications ([push_usage]), SMS ([sms_usage]), and browser notifications ([browser_notification_usage]); Priority Levels establishing urgency: critical ([critical_criteria] - immediate delivery), high ([high_criteria] - timely delivery), medium ([medium_criteria] - batch delivery), and low ([low_criteria] - digest delivery); Timing Strategy optimizing send times: immediate ([immediate_triggers]), scheduled ([scheduled_times]), timezone-aware ([timezone_considerations]), and frequency limits ([frequency_limits] per [time_period]); Personalization tailoring content: user preferences ([preference_settings]), behavior-based ([behavior_triggers]), and segment-based ([segment_targeting]); Content Guidelines establishing messaging standards: tone ([notification_tone]), length ([message_length]), clarity ([clarity_requirements]), and CTAs ([cta_guidelines]); User Control providing preferences: notification center ([notification_center_design]), preference management ([preference_ui]), opt-out options ([opt_out_options]), and quiet hours ([quiet_hours_setting]); Delivery Rules defining logic: deduplication ([deduplication_rules]), batching ([batching_strategy]), and throttling ([throttling_rules]); Analytics tracking performance: open rates ([open_rate_tracking]), click rates ([click_rate_tracking]), opt-out rates ([opt_out_tracking]), and engagement impact ([engagement_impact_measurement]); Testing Strategy validating approach: A/B tests ([ab_test_scenarios]), user research ([user_research_plan]), and iteration process ([iteration_approach]).

title: Business Model Canvas Generator
primary_use_case: Create business model canvases for products and startups
prompt_text: Generate a comprehensive Business Model Canvas for [product/business_name] following the standard nine-block framework. Customer Segments identifying target customers: primary segment ([primary_segment] with needs [need_1], [need_2]), secondary segment ([secondary_segment] with needs [need_3]), and niche segments ([niche_segment_1], [niche_segment_2]); Channels describing how value is delivered: distribution channels ([channel_1], [channel_2], [channel_3]), sales channels ([sales_channel_1], [sales_channel_2]), and communication channels ([communication_channel_1], [communication_channel_2]); Key Resources listing essential assets: physical ([physical_resource_1], [physical_resource_2]), intellectual ([intellectual_resource_1], [intellectual_resource_2]), human ([human_resource_1], [human_resource_2]), and financial ([financial_resource_1]); title: Pitch Deck Structure Builder
primary_use_case: Create pitch deck structures for fundraising and presentations

Solution Slide presenting the approach: product overview ([product_overview]), key features ([feature_1], [feature_2], [feature_3]), unique approach ([unique_value]), and solution validation ([solution_validation]); Market Opportunity analyzing size: TAM ([tam_size]), SAM ([sam_size]), SOM ([som_size]), market growth ([growth_rate]%), and market trends ([trend_1], [trend_2]); Business Model explaining monetization: revenue model ([revenue_model]), pricing strategy ([pricing_strategy]), unit economics ([unit_economics]), and revenue projections ([revenue_projection]); title: Value Proposition Canvas
primary_use_case: Create value proposition canvases for products
prompt_text: Create a Value Proposition Canvas for [product_name] aligning customer jobs, pains, and gains with product features and benefits. The canvas should include: Customer Profile - Customer Jobs defining tasks: functional jobs ([functional_job_1], [functional_job_2], [functional_job_3]), social jobs ([social_job_1], [social_job_2]), and emotional jobs ([emotional_job_1], [emotional_job_2]); Customer Profile - Pains identifying frustrations: undesired outcomes ([undesired_outcome_1], [undesired_outcome_2]), obstacles ([obstacle_1], [obstacle_2]), and risks ([risk_1], [risk_2]), with severity ratings ([severity_1]/10, [severity_2]/10, [severity_3]/10); Customer Profile - Gains defining desired outcomes: required gains ([required_gain_1], [required_gain_2]), expected gains ([expected_gain_1], [expected_gain_2]), desired gains ([desired_gain_1], [desired_gain_2]), and unexpected gains ([unexpected_gain_1]), with importance ratings ([importance_1]/10, [importance_2]/10, [importance_3]/10); Value Map - Products & Services listing offerings: products ([product_1], [product_2]), services ([service_1], [service_2]), and features ([feature_1], [feature_2], [feature_3]); Value Map - Pain Relievers addressing frustrations: how product relieves pain 1 ([pain_reliever_1] addressing [pain_1]), pain reliever 2 ([pain_reliever_2] addressing [pain_2]), and pain reliever 3 ([pain_reliever_3] addressing [pain_3]); Value Map - Gain Creators delivering benefits: how product creates gain 1 ([gain_creator_1] delivering [gain_1]), gain creator 2 ([gain_creator_2] delivering [gain_2]), and gain creator 3 ([gain_creator_3] delivering [gain_3]); Fit Assessment evaluating alignment: pain relief fit ([pain_fit_score]/10 - how well pains are addressed), gain creation fit ([gain_fit_score]/10 - how well gains are created), and overall fit ([overall_fit_score]/10); Value Proposition Statement crafting the message: [product_name] helps [target_customer] [achieve_job] by [key_benefit], unlike [competitor] we [differentiator]; Prioritization ranking importance: top pain ([top_pain] severity [severity]/10), top gain ([top_gain] importance [importance]/10), and focus areas ([focus_area_1], [focus_area_2]); Communication Plan sharing results: stakeholder updates ([update_frequency]), result presentations ([presentation_format]), and documentation ([documentation_location]); Success Metrics measuring framework effectiveness: experiment velocity ([experiments_per_quarter]), learning rate ([learnings_per_experiment]), decision quality ([decision_quality_metric]), and business impact ([business_impact_metric]).

title: First Principles Thinking Analyzer
primary_use_case: Break down complex problems into fundamental truths and rebuild solutions from scratch
output_type: Structured analysis with fundamental truths, assumptions, and reconstructed solution
prompt_text: Apply first principles thinking to analyze [PROBLEM/QUESTION]. Start by identifying and listing all fundamental truths and facts about [DOMAIN/CONTEXT]. Then, systematically identify all assumptions, conventions, and inherited beliefs that may not be necessary. Challenge each assumption by asking 'Why?' repeatedly until you reach irreducible truths. Once you have the fundamental building blocks, reconstruct a solution or approach from these first principles. Consider: What are the absolute certainties? What assumptions are we making? What would a solution look like if we started from scratch? What constraints are real vs. perceived? Provide a step-by-step breakdown showing the deconstruction process and the reconstruction of a novel approach based purely on fundamental truths.

variations.short: Break down [PROBLEM] using first principles. List fundamental truths, challenge assumptions, rebuild solution.
variations.detailed: Conduct a comprehensive first principles analysis of [PROBLEM/QUESTION] in [DOMAIN/CONTEXT]. Begin by documenting all known fundamental truths, laws, and facts that are universally accepted. Then perform assumption archaeology: identify every assumption, convention, industry standard, and inherited belief. For each assumption, apply the '5 Whys' technique to drill down to root causes. Categorize assumptions as: necessary constraints, unnecessary constraints, or false constraints. Map relationships between fundamental truths. Now reconstruct a solution architecture using only verified first principles. Consider alternative approaches that violate conventional wisdom but align with fundamental truths. Evaluate the reconstructed solution against original assumptions to identify innovation opportunities. Provide a visual breakdown showing the deconstruction layers and reconstruction logic.
variations.strict:
STRICT MODE: First Principles Analysis

Input: [PROBLEM]
Domain: [DOMAIN]

Step 1: Fundamental Truths (List only verifiable facts)
Step 2: Assumption Inventory (List all assumptions)
Step 3: Assumption Validation (Mark: Verified/Unverified/False)
Step 4: First Principles Reconstruction (Build solution using only Step 1 truths)
Step 5: Gap Analysis (Compare reconstructed vs. conventional approach)

Output format: JSON with sections: fundamental_truths[], assumptions[], reconstruction[], innovations[]

tips: Start with 'What do we know for certain?' rather than 'What do we think?' Use Socratic questioning. Be ruthless in eliminating assumptions.

title: Bayesian Reasoning Assistant
primary_use_case: Apply Bayesian reasoning to update beliefs with new evidence and make probabilistic decisions
output_type: Prior probabilities, likelihoods, posterior probabilities, and updated beliefs
prompt_text: Apply Bayesian reasoning to [DECISION/PROBLEM]: [DESCRIBE]. Start by establishing prior probabilities: what do we believe before seeing new evidence? Express these as probabilities (0-1) or odds. Identify the new evidence: [DESCRIBE EVIDENCE]. Determine the likelihood: probability of observing this evidence if the hypothesis is true, and if it's false. Calculate the posterior probability using Bayes' theorem: P(H|E) = P(E|H) × P(H) / P(E). Update beliefs based on the evidence. Consider base rates: what's the overall frequency in the population? Avoid base rate neglect. Calculate multiple scenarios with different prior beliefs to see sensitivity. Consider the strength of evidence: strong vs. weak evidence. Provide confidence intervals or ranges. Explain the reasoning in intuitive terms. Show how beliefs should update rationally. Consider what additional evidence would be most valuable to gather.

variations.short: Apply Bayes' theorem to [PROBLEM]. Set priors, calculate likelihoods, update to posteriors with evidence.
variations.detailed: Conduct a comprehensive Bayesian analysis for [DECISION/PROBLEM] in [CONTEXT]. Establish prior probability distribution: use historical data, expert judgment, or uniform priors if no information. Specify hypotheses: [H1, H2, H3...]. For each piece of evidence, calculate likelihood ratios: P(Evidence|Hypothesis) / P(Evidence|Not Hypothesis). Apply Bayes' theorem iteratively as new evidence arrives. Consider base rate information and avoid base rate fallacy. Perform sensitivity analysis: vary priors ±20% and observe impact on posteriors. Calculate Bayes factors to compare hypotheses. Use conjugate priors where appropriate (Beta-Binomial, Normal-Normal, etc.). Provide Bayesian credible intervals. Consider multiple sources of evidence and combine them. Address the problem of the priors: how to set them objectively vs. subjectively. Calculate expected value of information: what evidence would be most valuable? Provide intuitive explanations using natural frequencies or visualizations. Include decision analysis using expected utility.

tips: Start with reasonable priors based on base rates. Update incrementally with each piece of evidence. Consider the strength and reliability of evidence.

Consider what risks were underestimated. Identify what could have been done differently. Then, for each failure scenario, develop prevention strategies: what can we do now to prevent this? user_role: Operations Manager, Productivity Specialist, Analyst, Automation Engineer
output_type: Complete workflow automation design with steps, tools, and implementation plan
prompt_text: Design an automated workflow for [PROCESS/TASK]: [DESCRIBE CURRENT MANUAL PROCESS]. Identify the current manual steps: [LIST STEPS]. For each step, determine: can it be automated? What triggers it? What's the input? What's the output? What tools/apps are involved? Design the automated workflow: (1) Trigger (what starts it - time, event, webhook, etc.), (2) Steps (each automated action), (3) Conditions (if/then logic), (4) Integrations (which tools connect), (5) Error handling (what if something fails?), and (6) Notifications (who needs to know?). Consider tools: Zapier, Make.com, n8n, Microsoft Power Automate, or custom scripts. Map the workflow visually or in step-by-step format. Estimate time saved. Identify potential issues or edge cases. Provide implementation steps: setup order, testing plan, and rollback plan. Include monitoring and maintenance considerations.

variations.short: Design automation for [PROCESS]. Map current steps, design automated workflow with triggers, steps, tools, error handling.
variations.detailed: Create comprehensive workflow automation design for [PROCESS] in [CONTEXT]. Document current state: manual process steps (detailed task list), time per step, frequency, pain points, error rates, and stakeholders involved. Analyze automation potential: identify automatable steps (rule-based, repetitive, high volume), semi-automated steps (human decision points), and manual-only steps (complex judgment). Design automated workflow architecture: trigger events (scheduled, event-based, webhook, manual, API call), workflow steps (actions, transformations, decisions), data flow (inputs, transformations, outputs), integrations (APIs, webhooks, connectors), conditional logic (if/then/else, loops, parallel paths), error handling (retries, fallbacks, alerts), and notifications (success, failure, status updates). Select automation platform: evaluate Zapier, Make.com, n8n, Microsoft Power Automate, custom scripts (Python, Node.js), or hybrid approach. Create detailed workflow diagram: visual representation with decision points, parallel paths, and error handling. Estimate ROI: time saved per occurrence, frequency, cost savings, error reduction, and scalability benefits. Develop implementation plan: phase 1 (MVP automation), phase 2 (enhancements), testing strategy (unit tests, integration tests, user acceptance), rollback plan, documentation, training, and monitoring (success rates, error logs, performance metrics). Include maintenance: update procedures, change management, and optimization opportunities.

title: Zapier/Make.com Integration Planner
primary_use_case: Plan and design integrations using Zapier or Make.com to connect apps and automate workflows
user_role: Automation Specialist, Operations Manager, Developer, Power User
output_type: Integration plan with Zapier/Make.com workflow design
prompt_text: Design a Zapier/Make.com integration to [OBJECTIVE]: [DESCRIBE WHAT YOU WANT TO AUTOMATE]. Apps involved: [LIST APPS]. Current manual process: [DESCRIBE]. Design the integration workflow: (1) Trigger app and trigger event (what starts it?), (2) Data mapping (which fields map where?), (3) Filters (what conditions must be met?), (4) Actions (what happens in each app?), (5) Error handling (what if something fails?), and (6) Testing (how to verify it works?). For Zapier: specify trigger, action apps, field mappings, and filters. For Make.com: design the scenario with modules, routers, and data transformations. Consider: authentication setup, rate limits, data formats, webhook configurations, and error scenarios. Provide step-by-step setup instructions. Include testing checklist. Estimate costs (Zapier tasks or Make.com operations). Suggest optimizations to reduce task/operation usage.

variations.short: Design Zapier/Make.com integration for [OBJECTIVE] connecting [APPS]. Map triggers, actions, data flow, error handling.
variations.detailed: Create comprehensive Zapier/Make.com integration plan for [OBJECTIVE] in [CONTEXT]. Analyze requirements: source apps (where data comes from), destination apps (where data goes), data flow (unidirectional, bidirectional, sync), frequency (real-time, scheduled, on-demand), data volume (tasks/operations per month), and transformation needs (data formatting, calculations, filtering). Design integration architecture: trigger selection (webhook, polling, scheduled, instant), action modules (create, update, search, delete operations), data mapping (field-by-field mapping, transformations, default values), conditional logic (filters, routers, if/then conditions), error handling (retry logic, error notifications, fallback actions), and data validation (required fields, format checks, business rules). Platform selection: Zapier (ease of use, app ecosystem, pricing) vs. Make.com (complexity handling, cost efficiency, customization). Create detailed workflow: visual flow diagram, step-by-step module configuration, data transformation formulas, filter conditions, and error paths. Estimate costs: Zapier (tasks per month, premium apps), Make.com (operations, data transfer). Optimize for cost: batch processing, webhook optimization, filter early to reduce operations. Provide setup guide: account setup, app connections (OAuth, API keys), webhook configuration, testing procedures (test data, edge cases, error scenarios), and deployment (staging → production). Include monitoring: success rates, error logs, performance metrics, and cost tracking. Document maintenance: update procedures, change management, and troubleshooting guide.

title: Email Automation Sequence Builder
primary_use_case: Design automated email sequences for marketing, onboarding, or communication workflows
user_role: Marketer, Growth Manager, Customer Success Manager, Communicator
output_type: Complete email sequence with triggers, content, timing, and conditions
prompt_text: Design an email automation sequence for [PURPOSE]: [DESCRIBE - e.g., welcome series, abandoned cart, onboarding]. Target audience: [DESCRIBE]. Goals: [ENGAGE/EDUCATE/SELL/RETAIN]. Design the sequence: (1) Trigger (what starts it - signup, purchase, inactivity, etc.), (2) Email sequence (list each email with subject, content outline, timing), (3) Conditions (who gets which emails - segments, behavior), (4) Personalization (what to customize - name, product, behavior), and (5) Exit conditions (when to stop - purchase, unsubscribe, etc.). For each email, provide: subject line, preview text, body content outline, CTA, send timing (delay from trigger or previous email), and conditions for sending. Consider email best practices: value-first content, clear CTAs, mobile optimization, personalization, and unsubscribe options. Include A/B testing suggestions. Provide implementation steps for your email platform (Mailchimp, SendGrid, etc.).

variations.short: Design email sequence for [PURPOSE] targeting [AUDIENCE]. Include trigger, emails with subjects/content/timing, conditions, personalization.
variations.detailed: Create comprehensive email automation sequence for [PURPOSE] in [CONTEXT] targeting [AUDIENCE SEGMENT]. Define sequence objectives: primary goal (conversion, engagement, education), success metrics (open rate, click rate, conversion rate), and KPIs. Design trigger strategy: entry trigger (what starts sequence - signup, purchase, download, page visit), segment criteria (who qualifies - demographics, behavior, preferences), and timing (immediate, delayed, scheduled). Create email sequence architecture: email 1 (immediate, welcome/introduction, sets expectations), email 2-3 (value delivery, education, engagement), email 4-5 (deepening relationship, social proof), email 6+ (nurturing, offers, re-engagement), and exit emails (win-back, final offer). For each email, develop: subject line (multiple options for A/B testing), preview text, email structure (header, body sections, CTA, footer), content (personalized copy, value proposition, storytelling), visual elements (images, layout, branding), CTA (clear, action-oriented, prominent), send timing (hours/days from trigger or previous), conditions (behavioral triggers, segment rules), personalization variables ([Name], [Product], [Behavior], [Location]), and exit conditions (purchase, unsubscribe, inactivity). Design segmentation: different sequences for different personas, behavior-based branching (if clicked X, send Y), and lifecycle stage (new, active, at-risk). Include optimization: A/B testing plan (subject lines, send times, content), performance monitoring (open rates, click rates, conversions), and iteration strategy. Provide platform-specific implementation: Mailchimp, SendGrid, HubSpot, Marketo, or custom. Include compliance: CAN-SPAM, GDPR, unsubscribe handling, and consent management.

title: Data Entry Automation Script
primary_use_case: Create scripts to automate data entry tasks across applications
user_role: Developer, Data Analyst, Operations Manager, Power User
output_type: Automation script with code, setup instructions, and usage guide
prompt_text: Create a data entry automation script for [TASK]: [DESCRIBE - e.g., transfer data from X to Y, fill forms, update records]. Source: [DESCRIBE DATA SOURCE]. Destination: [DESCRIBE WHERE DATA GOES]. Data format: [DESCRIBE]. Requirements: [LIST - validation, error handling, logging, etc.]. Design the script: (1) Data extraction (how to get data from source), (2) Data transformation (cleaning, formatting, mapping), (3) Data validation (check for errors, duplicates), (4) Data entry (how to input into destination), (5) Error handling (what if something fails?), and (6) Logging (track what was done). Choose appropriate tools: Python (pandas, selenium, requests), JavaScript/Node.js, RPA tools (UiPath, Automation Anywhere), or browser automation (Puppeteer, Playwright). Provide code structure, key functions, configuration options, and usage instructions. Include testing approach and safety measures (backup, rollback).

variations.short: Create automation script for [TASK] moving data from [SOURCE] to [DESTINATION]. Include extraction, transformation, validation, entry, error handling.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive data entry automation solution for [TASK] in [CONTEXT]. Analyze requirements: source system (database, CSV, API, web form, Excel), destination system (database, CRM, web form, API), data volume (records per run), frequency (one-time, scheduled, real-time), data mapping (field correspondences, transformations), validation rules (required fields, formats, business rules), and error tolerance (strict vs. permissive). Design automation architecture: extraction layer (read from source, handle pagination, API rate limits), transformation layer (data cleaning, format conversion, field mapping, calculations), validation layer (schema validation, business rule checks, duplicate detection), entry layer (API calls, form filling, database inserts, UI automation), error handling (retry logic, error logging, notification), and logging (audit trail, success/failure tracking). Select technology stack: Python (pandas for data, selenium/playwright for web, requests for APIs, sqlalchemy for databases), JavaScript/Node.js (for web automation), RPA tools (for UI-heavy tasks), or hybrid approach. Create script structure: configuration (credentials, endpoints, mappings), extraction functions, transformation functions, validation functions, entry functions, error handling, logging, and main execution flow. Include safety features: dry-run mode (preview without changes), backup creation, transaction rollback, rate limiting, and data sanitization. Provide implementation guide: environment setup, dependencies installation, configuration, testing (unit tests, integration tests, sample data), deployment, scheduling (cron, task scheduler), and monitoring (success rates, error alerts). Document: code comments, usage instructions, troubleshooting guide, and maintenance procedures.

Design bot commands: (1) Command syntax (/command [options]), (2) What each command does, (3) Required permissions/scopes, (4) Response format (text, blocks, modals), (5) Error handling, and (6) Help documentation. Consider Slack features: slash commands, interactive components (buttons, selects), modals, shortcuts, events (message, reaction, member), and workflows. Design user interactions: how users invoke the bot, what information they provide, what the bot returns, and follow-up actions. Include examples of command usage. variations.detailed: Create comprehensive Slack bot design for [PURPOSE] in [CONTEXT] with use cases: [LIST]. Define bot capabilities: commands (slash commands, interactive actions), workflows (automated triggers, multi-step processes), integrations (connect to external APIs, databases, services), and notifications (proactive alerts, scheduled messages). Design command architecture: command name (/command), description, syntax (parameters, options, flags), functionality (what it does, API calls, data processing), response format (simple text, rich blocks, modals, files), error messages (user-friendly, actionable), help text (usage examples, parameter descriptions), and permissions (OAuth scopes needed). title: Spreadsheet Formula Builder
primary_use_case: Create complex spreadsheet formulas to automate calculations and data processing
user_role: Analyst, Accountant, Data Analyst, Power User
output_type: Spreadsheet formulas with explanations and usage instructions
prompt_text: Create spreadsheet formulas for [TASK]: [DESCRIBE - e.g., calculate metrics, look up data, aggregate values]. Data structure: [DESCRIBE LAYOUT]. Requirements: [LIST WHAT NEEDS TO BE CALCULATED]. Design formulas for: (1) Lookups (VLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, XLOOKUP), (2) Aggregations (SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS), (3) Text manipulation (CONCATENATE, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, SUBSTITUTE), (4) Date calculations (DATEDIF, WORKDAY, EOMONTH), (5) Conditional logic (IF, IFS, SWITCH, nested IFs), and (6) Array formulas (for complex calculations). For each formula, provide: the formula syntax, explanation of how it works, cell references, example with sample data, and error handling (IFERROR, ISERROR). Consider performance for large datasets. Provide alternative approaches if applicable. Include instructions for copying formulas across ranges.

variations.short: Create formulas for [TASK] in spreadsheet. Include lookups, aggregations, text manipulation, conditionals with explanations.
variations.detailed: Develop comprehensive spreadsheet formula solution for [TASK] in [CONTEXT] with data structure: [DESCRIBE]. Analyze requirements: calculations needed (metrics, aggregations, transformations), data relationships (lookups, joins, filters), conditions (IF logic, multiple criteria), and output format (single values, arrays, formatted text). Design formula architecture: lookup formulas (VLOOKUP for simple lookups, INDEX/MATCH for flexible lookups, XLOOKUP for modern Excel, HLOOKUP for horizontal data), aggregation formulas (SUMIFS/COUNTIFS/AVERAGEIFS for conditional sums, SUMPRODUCT for complex conditions, array formulas for advanced calculations), text formulas (CONCATENATE/TEXTJOIN for combining, LEFT/RIGHT/MID for extraction, SUBSTITUTE/REPLACE for modification, TRIM/CLEAN for cleaning, UPPER/LOWER/PROPER for case), date formulas (TODAY/NOW for current date/time, DATEDIF for differences, WORKDAY for business days, EOMONTH for month ends, YEAR/MONTH/DAY for extraction), logical formulas (IF/IFS for conditions, AND/OR for multiple conditions, SWITCH for multiple values, nested IFs for complex logic), and array formulas (for multi-cell calculations, dynamic arrays in modern Excel). For each formula, provide: complete syntax, parameter explanations, cell reference examples, step-by-step breakdown, example with sample data, error handling (IFERROR wrapper, ISERROR checks), performance considerations (volatile functions, array formula efficiency), and alternatives (different approaches, simpler versions). Create formula combinations: nested formulas, formula chains, and helper columns strategy. Include best practices: naming ranges for clarity, avoiding hardcoded values, documenting complex formulas, testing with sample data, and optimizing for performance. Provide implementation guide: where to place formulas, how to copy/drag formulas, absolute vs. relative references ($), and troubleshooting common errors (#N/A, #VALUE, #REF).

Design tool ecosystem: task manager (Todoist, Things, TickTick), note-taking (Notion, Obsidian, Roam), calendar (Google Calendar, Outlook), habit tracker (Habitica, Streaks, Loop), automation (Zapier, IFTTT, Shortcuts), and integration (sync between tools, reduce friction). Design review system: daily review (evening reflection, next day planning), weekly review (accomplishments, challenges, adjustments), monthly review (goal progress, system refinement), and quarterly review (big picture, goal setting). Design implementation: phase 1 (core system, essential tools), phase 2 (automation, integrations), phase 3 (optimization, refinement), setup steps (tool configuration, workflow creation, habit establishment), and adoption (start small, build gradually, iterate). Include best practices: start simple, focus on systems not goals, measure what matters, iterate based on what works, and maintain flexibility.

Provide both serif/sans-serif combinations and complementary pairings.

variations.short: Create a font pairing guide with 10 combinations and usage examples.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive font pairing guide document: introduction explaining font pairing principles (contrast, harmony, hierarchy), 10 font pairing examples each including: font names and classifications (serif, sans-serif, display, script), visual examples showing headline (48pt+), subheading (24pt), and body text (12-14pt) usage, explanation of why the pairing works (contrast in weight, style, or structure), recommended use cases (print, web, branding, etc.), and example applications (poster, website, brochure). Include pairing categories: serif + sans-serif combinations (classic and modern), sans-serif + sans-serif (contrasting weights and styles), display + body text, script + sans-serif, and monospace + sans-serif. Use clean layout with ample whitespace, clear typography hierarchy, and visual examples. Design as both print reference guide and digital PDF. Include font sources and licensing information.
variations.strict: Exactly 10 font pairings. Each pairing must show headline (48pt+), subheading (24pt), body (12-14pt) examples. Include explanation for each pairing. Maximum 2 pages per pairing example.

tips: Pair fonts with sufficient contrast (serif with sans-serif, or different weights/styles). Avoid pairing similar fonts. Test readability at various sizes. Consider the mood and tone of your project. Use font pairing tools for inspiration.

title: Layout Grid System
primary_use_case: Design a flexible grid system for consistent layouts
prompt_text: Create a comprehensive grid system including 12-column, 16-column, and modular grid options for various layout needs. Design templates showing how to use grids for web pages, print documents, and mobile layouts. Include guidelines for margins, gutters, baseline grids, and responsive breakpoints. Provide visual examples of grid usage in different contexts.

variations.short: Design a flexible grid system with 12-column, 16-column, and modular options.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive layout grid system guide: 12-column grid system (standard for web and print) with specifications for column width, gutter width, and margins, 16-column grid system (for more complex layouts) with specifications, modular grid system (for editorial and magazine layouts) with base unit and module specifications, baseline grid system (for typography alignment) with line height and spacing rules, responsive grid breakpoints (mobile: 4 columns, tablet: 8 columns, desktop: 12 columns), and application examples showing grid usage in: website homepage layout, magazine spread, brochure design, and mobile app interface. Include guidelines for: margin specifications (outer margins for print, container margins for web), gutter spacing (consistent spacing between columns), column usage (spanning multiple columns for emphasis), and alignment rules (text alignment, image alignment, element positioning). Design visual guides showing grid overlays on actual layouts, specifications document with measurements, and template files for common design software. Use clear annotations and measurements.
variations.strict: Include 12-column, 16-column, modular, and baseline grids. Specify exact measurements: column widths, gutter widths (minimum 20px), margins (minimum 40px for print, 20px for web). Provide breakpoints: mobile (320px+), tablet (768px+), desktop (1024px+).

tips: Use consistent gutter widths throughout. Align elements to the grid for visual harmony. Use the grid as a guide, not a constraint. Test layouts at different breakpoints. Document your grid system for team consistency.

title: Whitespace Design
primary_use_case: Create designs that effectively use whitespace for clarity and impact
prompt_text: Design a series of examples demonstrating effective whitespace usage including minimalist posters, clean web layouts, elegant business cards, and sophisticated print materials. Show how whitespace creates visual hierarchy, improves readability, and enhances the perceived value of content. Include before/after comparisons and guidelines for whitespace ratios.

variations.short: Create design examples showing effective whitespace usage for clarity and impact.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive whitespace design guide with examples: minimalist poster design (80% whitespace, single focal point), clean website homepage (generous margins, breathing room between sections), elegant business card (centered layout with ample whitespace), sophisticated letterhead (classic proportions, balanced spacing), luxury product packaging (minimal text, maximum whitespace), editorial magazine spread (varied whitespace creating rhythm), and before/after comparisons showing cluttered vs. clean designs. Include guidelines for: whitespace ratios (suggest 40-60% whitespace for luxury/minimalist designs, 20-30% for standard designs), margin specifications (outer margins, internal spacing), padding around elements (text blocks, images, buttons), line spacing (leading) for readability, and visual hierarchy through spacing. Explain how whitespace: creates focus and emphasis, improves readability and comprehension, enhances perceived value and luxury, guides eye movement, and creates balance. Design examples in various formats: print (posters, cards, letterhead) and digital (web pages, social media graphics).
variations.strict: Include 7 design examples. Each must demonstrate specific whitespace principles. Provide exact whitespace ratios: margins minimum 20% of page width, padding between elements minimum 40px, line spacing 1.5x font size minimum. Show before/after comparisons.

tips: Don't be afraid of empty space - it's a design element. Use whitespace to create visual hierarchy. More whitespace often equals higher perceived value. Balance whitespace with content. Test readability with actual content.

title: Visual Hierarchy Design
primary_use_case: Design layouts that guide the eye through content effectively
prompt_text: Create design examples demonstrating visual hierarchy principles including size contrast, color emphasis, typography scale, spacing, and positioning. Design layouts for landing pages, magazine spreads, infographics, and posters that effectively guide the viewer's eye through the content in the intended order. Include annotations explaining hierarchy decisions.

variations.short: Design examples showing visual hierarchy through size, color, typography, and spacing.
variations.detailed: Design comprehensive visual hierarchy examples: landing page design showing primary headline (largest, boldest), secondary headline, body text, and call-to-action button (color emphasis), magazine spread with headline hierarchy, pull quotes, body text, and captions, infographic with title, section headers, data points, and supporting text, poster design with main message, supporting information, and details, and dashboard interface with primary metrics, secondary data, and tertiary information. Demonstrate hierarchy techniques: size contrast (headlines 3-5x larger than body text), color emphasis (bright colors for important elements, neutrals for supporting), typography scale (4-5 levels: display, headline, subhead, body, caption), spacing (more space around important elements), positioning (F-pattern and Z-pattern layouts), and visual weight (bold vs. light, filled vs. outlined). Include annotations on each example showing: eye flow path (numbered sequence), hierarchy levels (1-5 scale), and design decisions. Explain how each technique guides attention and creates order.
variations.strict: Include 5 design examples. Each must show clear hierarchy levels (minimum 3 levels). Provide annotations: eye flow path, hierarchy scale (1-5), size ratios (headline:body minimum 3:1), color contrast specifications.

tips: Establish a clear focal point. Use size, color, and spacing to create hierarchy. Guide the eye in a logical order (F-pattern or Z-pattern). Test your hierarchy by asking what catches attention first. Maintain consistency throughout the design.

title: Responsive Layout Design
primary_use_case: Design layouts that adapt effectively across different screen sizes
prompt_text: Design responsive layouts for a website showing desktop (1920px), tablet (768px), and mobile (375px) versions. Create flexible grid systems, scalable typography, adaptive images, and navigation patterns that work across devices. Include breakpoint specifications and design guidelines for maintaining visual hierarchy and usability at all sizes.

variations.short: Create responsive layouts for desktop, tablet, and mobile with flexible grids and scalable typography.
variations.detailed: Design comprehensive responsive layout system: desktop layout (1920px width) with multi-column grid (12 columns), full navigation menu, large hero images, sidebars, and detailed content, tablet layout (768px width) with adapted grid (8 columns), simplified navigation (hamburger menu), adjusted image sizes, and optimized content width, mobile layout (375px width) with single column layout, mobile navigation (hamburger menu with slide-out), stacked content sections, touch-friendly buttons (minimum 44x44px), and optimized typography. Include specifications for: breakpoints (mobile: 320-767px, tablet: 768-1023px, desktop: 1024px+), flexible grid system (percentage-based columns, max-width containers), scalable typography (fluid typography using clamp() or viewport units, minimum 16px base size), adaptive images (srcset for different resolutions, max-width: 100%), navigation patterns (desktop: horizontal menu, mobile: hamburger menu), touch targets (minimum 44x44px for mobile), and content prioritization (most important content first on mobile). Design examples showing: homepage, product page, blog post, and contact page across all three breakpoints. Include annotations showing how elements adapt.
variations.strict: Design for 3 breakpoints: mobile (375px), tablet (768px), desktop (1920px). Grid: mobile (1 column), tablet (8 columns), desktop (12 columns). Typography: base 16px minimum, scalable using clamp(). Touch targets: 44x44px minimum. Images: max-width 100%, responsive.

tips: Design mobile-first, then scale up. Test layouts at actual device sizes. Ensure touch targets are large enough. Prioritize content for smaller screens. Use flexible units (percentages, em, rem) instead of fixed pixels. Test on real devices.

title: Icon Set Design
primary_use_case: Create a cohesive set of icons for applications or websites
prompt_text: Design a set of 30 icons with consistent style, stroke width, corner radius, and visual weight. Create icons for common actions (home, search, settings, user, etc.) and ensure they work at multiple sizes (16px, 24px, 32px, 48px). Use a unified design language with consistent proportions and spacing. Provide icons in both filled and outlined styles.

variations.short: Create a set of 30 consistent icons in multiple sizes with unified style.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive icon set of 30 icons covering: navigation icons (home, menu, back, forward, search), user icons (profile, account, login, logout, settings), action icons (add, delete, edit, save, share, download, upload), communication icons (message, email, phone, notification), content icons (image, video, document, folder, file), social icons (like, comment, share, follow), and utility icons (help, info, warning, error, success). Use consistent design principles: unified stroke width (2px for 24px icons, scalable), consistent corner radius (2px rounded corners), uniform visual weight (balanced line weights and fills), consistent style (outlined, filled, or mixed), and standardized grid (24x24px base grid with padding). Design icons in multiple sizes: 16px (for small UI elements), 24px (standard size), 32px (medium emphasis), and 48px (large emphasis). Provide both outlined and filled versions. Ensure icons are recognizable at small sizes, work in monochrome, and maintain consistency across the set. Export in SVG format for scalability and provide PNG versions for compatibility.
variations.strict: Exactly 30 icons. Consistent stroke width (2px base), corner radius (2px), visual weight. Sizes: 16px, 24px, 32px, 48px. Both outlined and filled versions. SVG format required.

tips: Start with a grid system for consistency. Keep designs simple and recognizable. Test icons at small sizes. Ensure icons work in both light and dark themes. Use consistent stroke widths and corner radius. Create a style guide for the icon set.

title: Custom Illustration Design
primary_use_case: Create custom illustrations for branding, marketing, or editorial use
prompt_text: Design a custom illustration style guide and create 5 example illustrations demonstrating the style. Establish a consistent visual language including color palette, line style, shading technique, and character proportions. Create illustrations suitable for use in marketing materials, websites, and print publications. Ensure the style is distinctive and scalable.

variations.short: Create a custom illustration style with 5 examples and style guide.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive custom illustration system: style guide defining illustration approach (flat design, isometric, hand-drawn, geometric, etc.), color palette (5-7 colors with usage guidelines), line style specifications (stroke width, line caps, joins), shading and texture techniques (flat colors, gradients, patterns, textures), character design guidelines (if applicable: proportions, facial features, body types), and composition rules (perspective, depth, layering). Create 5 example illustrations demonstrating the style: hero illustration for website homepage, product illustration showing features, editorial illustration for article, social media graphic with illustration, and icon-style illustration for app. Each illustration should: follow the established style guide, work at multiple sizes (from social media to large prints), maintain brand consistency, and be versatile for various applications. Include technical specifications: file formats (AI, SVG, PNG at various resolutions), color modes (RGB for digital, CMYK for print), and usage guidelines. Provide both full-color and simplified versions for different use cases.
variations.strict: Create style guide with exact specifications: color palette (5-7 colors with HEX codes), line style (stroke width, caps, joins), shading technique. Design exactly 5 illustrations following the style. All illustrations must work at multiple sizes (minimum 3 sizes: small, medium, large).

tips: Develop a strong style guide first. Keep illustrations consistent in style and color. Consider how illustrations will be used across different media. Test illustrations at various sizes. Create both detailed and simplified versions. Ensure illustrations align with brand identity.

title: Infographic Elements Design
primary_use_case: Create reusable graphic elements for infographic design
prompt_text: Design a library of infographic elements including icons, charts, diagrams, arrows, connectors, backgrounds, and decorative elements. Create a cohesive visual style with consistent colors, shapes, and styling. Design elements that are modular and can be combined to create complete infographics. Provide elements in various sizes and formats.

variations.short: Create a library of infographic elements with icons, charts, and connectors.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive infographic elements library: icon set (50+ icons covering common topics: people, technology, business, nature, etc.), chart elements (bar chart templates, pie chart segments, line graph elements, progress bars), diagram components (flowchart shapes, process arrows, connectors, decision diamonds), decorative elements (borders, frames, dividers, patterns, backgrounds), text elements (number callouts, percentage displays, stat boxes, quote bubbles), and illustration elements (simple illustrations, characters, objects, scenes). Use consistent design principles: unified color palette (5-7 colors with variations), consistent style (flat design, outlined, or mixed), standardized sizing (modular sizes: small, medium, large), and compatible shapes (rounded corners, sharp corners, or mixed). Design elements to be modular and combinable. Provide elements in: vector format (SVG, AI) for scalability, raster format (PNG with transparency) for quick use, and organized by category. Include example infographic showing how elements combine. Create both colored and monochrome versions for flexibility.
variations.strict: Include: 50+ icons, chart templates (bar, pie, line, progress), diagram components (flowchart shapes, arrows, connectors), decorative elements (borders, patterns), text elements (callouts, stat boxes). Consistent color palette (5-7 colors), modular sizing, vector format (SVG).

tips: Keep elements simple and recognizable. Ensure all elements work together cohesively. Design for scalability (vector format). Create a style guide for element usage. Organize elements by category for easy access. Test elements in combination before finalizing.

title: Achievement Badges Design
primary_use_case: Design achievement badges for gamification, certifications, or rewards
prompt_text: Design a set of 15 achievement badges with different levels (bronze, silver, gold) and categories. Create visually appealing badges with icons, text, and decorative elements. Ensure badges are recognizable at small sizes and work well in both digital and print formats. Design a cohesive badge system with consistent styling.

variations.short: Create 15 achievement badges with different levels and categories.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive achievement badge system: 15 badges organized into 5 categories (3 badges each) with 3 levels per category (bronze, silver, gold), badge categories such as: learning milestones (beginner, intermediate, advanced), participation levels (active, engaged, champion), skill achievements (novice, skilled, expert), completion badges (starter, finisher, master), and special achievements (first, streak, perfect). Each badge should include: central icon or symbol representing the achievement, level indicator (bronze/silver/gold color coding or symbols), badge name/text, decorative border or frame, and background design. Use consistent design principles: unified shape (circular, hexagonal, shield, or custom), consistent size (standard badge size with variations), color coding for levels (bronze: warm browns/oranges, silver: grays/silvers, gold: yellows/golds), readable typography, and scalable design. Design badges in multiple sizes: small (64x64px for UI), medium (128x128px for profiles), and large (256x256px for certificates). Provide both colored and outlined versions. Ensure badges are recognizable and motivating.
variations.strict: Exactly 15 badges: 5 categories x 3 levels. Consistent shape and size. Color coding: bronze (warm tones), silver (grays), gold (yellows). Sizes: 64px, 128px, 256px. Include icon, level indicator, and text on each badge.

tips: Make badges visually appealing and motivating. Use clear level differentiation (color, design complexity). Ensure badges are recognizable at small sizes. Test badges in context (user profiles, certificates). Create a badge hierarchy that encourages progression.

title: Pattern Design
primary_use_case: Create repeating patterns for backgrounds, textiles, or surface design
prompt_text: Design 5 repeating patterns with different styles (geometric, organic, floral, abstract, and illustrative). Create seamless tileable patterns that work as backgrounds, textures, or surface designs. Ensure patterns tile perfectly without visible seams. Design patterns suitable for various applications including digital backgrounds, print materials, and product surfaces.

variations.short: Create 5 seamless repeating patterns in different styles.
variations.detailed: Design a collection of 5 repeating patterns: geometric pattern (shapes, lines, angles - modern and structured), organic pattern (flowing shapes, natural forms - soft and fluid), floral pattern (flowers, leaves, botanical elements - decorative and elegant), abstract pattern (non-representational shapes and forms - artistic and versatile), and illustrative pattern (characters, objects, scenes - narrative and playful). Each pattern should: tile seamlessly without visible seams (test horizontal and vertical tiling), work at multiple scales (detailed view and zoomed out), use consistent color palette (3-5 colors per pattern), maintain visual balance and rhythm, and be versatile for various applications. Design patterns for: digital backgrounds (websites, social media), print materials (packaging, stationery, textiles), and product surfaces (fabric, wallpaper, ceramics). Provide patterns in: vector format (AI, SVG) for scalability, raster format (PNG, JPG) at various resolutions, and seamless tile files. Include examples showing patterns applied to: website background, product packaging, fabric swatch, and wall covering. Test patterns at different scales and orientations.
variations.strict: Exactly 5 patterns: geometric, organic, floral, abstract, illustrative. Each must tile seamlessly (test horizontal and vertical). Use 3-5 colors per pattern. Provide vector (SVG) and raster (PNG) formats. Patterns must work at multiple scales.

tips: Test patterns thoroughly for seamless tiling. Consider how patterns will look at different scales. Use consistent color palettes. Ensure patterns don't become overwhelming when repeated. Create both subtle and bold versions. Test patterns in their intended applications.

title: Animated Social Graphic
primary_use_case: Design animated graphics for social media posts and stories
prompt_text: Design an animated social media graphic with motion effects including text animations, icon movements, color transitions, and background effects. Create designs optimized for Instagram Stories, Facebook posts, and Twitter. Ensure animations are engaging but not distracting, and work well in both square and vertical formats. Include specifications for animation timing and effects.

variations.short: Create an animated social media graphic with text, icons, and background animations.
variations.detailed: Design animated social media graphics for multiple platforms: Instagram Stories format (1080x1920px vertical) with animated text reveal, icon animations, and background effects, Instagram Post format (1080x1080px square) with product showcase animation, Facebook Post format (1200x630px) with call-to-action animation, and Twitter format (1200x675px) with quote or stat animation. Include animation effects: text animations (fade in, slide in, typewriter effect, bounce), icon/illustration animations (rotation, scale, movement, color change), background effects (gradient shift, particle effects, pattern animation), and transition effects (fade, slide, zoom). Design for 3-5 second loops optimized for autoplay. Use engaging but non-distracting animations, brand-consistent colors and fonts, readable text (test on mobile devices), and clear call-to-action. Provide specifications: frame rate (24fps or 30fps), duration (3-5 seconds), loop settings, file formats (MP4, GIF, or platform-specific formats), and file size optimization. Include static versions for platforms that don't support animation.
variations.strict: Design for 4 formats: Instagram Stories (1080x1920px), Instagram Post (1080x1080px), Facebook (1200x630px), Twitter (1200x675px). Animation duration: 3-5 seconds, loop. Include text, icon, and background animations. File formats: MP4 and GIF. Maximum file size: 5MB for GIFs.

tips: Keep animations subtle and purposeful. Test on actual social media platforms. Ensure text is readable throughout the animation. Optimize file sizes for fast loading. Create static fallbacks. Consider autoplay and sound-off viewing. Test on mobile devices.

title: GIF Design
primary_use_case: Create engaging GIF animations for marketing and communication
prompt_text: Design 3 GIF animations with different purposes: product showcase, tutorial/demo, and promotional message. Create looping animations that are engaging and communicate effectively. Optimize GIFs for file size while maintaining quality. Ensure animations work well in email, on websites, and social media platforms.

variations.short: Create 3 GIF animations: product showcase, tutorial, and promotional message.
variations.detailed: Design 3 GIF animations for different purposes: product showcase GIF (demonstrating product features, rotating product view, or highlighting benefits - 800x800px, 5-8 second loop), tutorial/demo GIF (showing step-by-step process, how-to instructions, or feature walkthrough - 1200x675px, 10-15 second loop), and promotional message GIF (announcing sale, new product, or event - 1080x1080px, 3-5 second loop). Each GIF should include: clear visual storytelling, smooth animation transitions, brand-consistent design, readable text (if applicable), and optimized file size. Use animation techniques: frame-by-frame animation, tweening, color transitions, text reveals, and motion graphics. Optimize for: file size (aim for under 2MB for web, under 1MB for email), color reduction (256 colors or less), frame rate (15-24fps), and duration (shorter is better). Provide specifications: dimensions, frame count, duration, file size, and usage recommendations. Include static preview images. Test GIFs in email clients and on various platforms.
variations.strict: Exactly 3 GIFs: product showcase (800x800px, 5-8 sec), tutorial (1200x675px, 10-15 sec), promotional (1080x1080px, 3-5 sec). Maximum file size: 2MB for web, 1MB for email. Frame rate: 15-24fps. Color limit: 256 colors.

tips: Keep GIFs short and focused. Optimize file sizes for fast loading. Use limited color palettes. Test in email clients (not all support GIFs). Create clear, simple animations. Consider file size vs. quality trade-offs. Provide static alternatives.

title: Interactive Infographic Design
primary_use_case: Design interactive infographics for web with hover effects and animations
prompt_text: Design an interactive infographic with hover effects, click interactions, animated data visualizations, and progressive disclosure. Create a responsive design that works on desktop and tablet devices. Include specifications for interactions, animations, and technical implementation. Ensure the design is engaging while maintaining usability and accessibility.

variations.short: Create an interactive infographic with hover effects, animations, and click interactions.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive interactive infographic for web: layout design (desktop: 1200px width, tablet: 768px width) with sections for data visualization, timeline, comparison charts, and detailed information, interactive elements including: hover effects (highlighting data points, showing tooltips, revealing additional information), click interactions (expanding sections, filtering data, switching views), animated data visualizations (charts that animate on scroll, counters that count up, progress bars that fill), and progressive disclosure (showing summary first, details on interaction). Include specifications for: interaction states (default, hover, active, focus), animation timing (ease-in-out, duration 0.3-0.5s), responsive breakpoints (desktop: 1024px+, tablet: 768-1023px), accessibility features (keyboard navigation, screen reader support, focus indicators), and technical requirements (HTML/CSS/JavaScript structure, framework recommendations, performance considerations). Design visual mockups showing: default state, hover states, expanded states, and mobile adaptation. Ensure design maintains visual hierarchy and usability while adding interactivity. Include loading states and error handling considerations.
variations.strict: Design for desktop (1200px) and tablet (768px). Include hover effects, click interactions, animated visualizations, progressive disclosure. Interaction timing: 0.3-0.5s. Accessibility: keyboard navigation, focus indicators. Responsive breakpoints: desktop 1024px+, tablet 768-1023px.

tips: Keep interactions intuitive and discoverable. Provide visual feedback for all interactions. Ensure accessibility (keyboard navigation, screen readers). Optimize for performance (lazy loading, efficient animations). Test on various devices and browsers. Include loading and error states.

title: Micro-animation Design
primary_use_case: Design subtle micro-animations for UI elements and interactions
prompt_text: Design a library of micro-animations for common UI interactions including button hovers, loading states, transitions, feedback animations, and state changes. Create subtle, purposeful animations that enhance usability and provide visual feedback. Include timing specifications, easing functions, and implementation guidelines. Ensure animations are performant and accessible.

variations.short: Create a library of micro-animations for UI interactions with timing and easing specifications.
variations.detailed: Design a comprehensive micro-animation library for UI: button animations (hover state: scale 1.05x, color transition, 0.2s duration, active state: scale 0.95x, 0.1s duration), loading states (spinner animation: 1s rotation, pulse animation: 1.5s fade in/out, skeleton screens: shimmer effect), page transitions (fade: 0.3s ease-in-out, slide: 0.4s ease-out, zoom: 0.3s ease-in), feedback animations (success checkmark: 0.5s scale and fade, error shake: 0.4s horizontal movement, notification slide-in: 0.3s from top), state changes (toggle switch: 0.2s slide, accordion expand: 0.3s height animation, tab switch: 0.25s fade), and form interactions (input focus: border color transition 0.2s, validation feedback: 0.3s color change, error message: 0.3s slide down). Include specifications for: timing (duration in seconds: 0.1s for instant feedback, 0.2-0.3s for standard, 0.4-0.5s for complex), easing functions (ease-in-out for most, ease-out for entrances, ease-in for exits), performance considerations (use transform and opacity, avoid layout-triggering properties), accessibility (respect prefers-reduced-motion, provide instant feedback), and implementation guidelines (CSS animations, JavaScript, or animation libraries). Create visual examples and code snippets.
variations.strict: Include: button animations (hover 0.2s, active 0.1s), loading states (spinner 1s, pulse 1.5s), transitions (fade 0.3s, slide 0.4s), feedback (success 0.5s, error 0.4s), state changes (toggle 0.2s, accordion 0.3s). All animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion. Use transform/opacity only for performance.

tips: Keep animations subtle and purposeful. Use consistent timing across the interface. Respect user preferences (prefers-reduced-motion). Optimize for performance (use transform/opacity). Provide instant feedback for user actions. Test animations on various devices and browsers.

title: Video Thumbnail Design
primary_use_case: Design compelling video thumbnails for YouTube, social media, or video platforms
prompt_text: Design 5 video thumbnail templates with different styles optimized for YouTube (1280x720px). Create eye-catching designs with bold text, compelling imagery, and clear focal points. Ensure thumbnails are readable at small sizes and stand out in video grids. Include templates for different video types: tutorial, vlog, product review, and entertainment content.

variations.short: Create 5 YouTube thumbnail templates with bold text and compelling imagery.
variations.detailed: Design 5 video thumbnail templates for YouTube (1280x720px, 16:9 aspect ratio): tutorial/educational thumbnail (with step number, clear title, and relevant imagery), vlog/lifestyle thumbnail (featuring person or scene, engaging title, and personal branding), product review thumbnail (product image, rating or key benefit, and attention-grabbing text), entertainment/funny thumbnail (expressive faces, bold text, and vibrant colors), and news/informational thumbnail (headline text, relevant imagery, and professional styling). Each thumbnail should include: large, readable text (minimum 60pt, bold font, high contrast), compelling focal point (person, product, or key visual element), strategic use of color (bright, contrasting colors that stand out), minimal text (3-7 words maximum), and brand consistency (channel colors, fonts, style). Design thumbnails to: be readable at small sizes (test at 120x67px), stand out in video grids, create curiosity and click-through, and work across devices (desktop, mobile, TV). Include safe zones (keep important elements within center 80% to avoid platform UI overlays). Provide templates in PSD or design software format with layers for easy customization. Include examples showing thumbnails in YouTube grid context.
variations.strict: Exactly 5 thumbnails: tutorial, vlog, product review, entertainment, news. Size: 1280x720px (16:9). Text minimum 60pt, bold, high contrast. Maximum 7 words per thumbnail. Keep important elements in center 80% safe zone. Test at 120x67px size.

tips: Use large, bold text that's readable at small sizes. Create a clear focal point. Use high contrast colors. Keep text minimal and impactful. Test thumbnails at actual small sizes. Study successful thumbnails in your niche. Include faces or expressive imagery when relevant. Maintain brand consistency across thumbnails.
